en.title: Baby in a Basket
story: A mummy had a baby boy. A bad king wanted to hurt him.
So the mummy made a little basket, like a boat.
She put her baby inside and let it float on the river. Splish, splash!
His big sister Miriam watched. Then a princess found the baby. ‘I will look after him!’
God kept baby Moses safe.

verse.text: God watches over me.

en.action: Rock a pretend baby in your arms. Then float your hands like a little boat on the water.
lessons: God watches over me, day and night.
questions: Who looks after you? (Mommy, Daddy… and God!)
prayer: Thank you, God,
for keeping me safe. Amen.

af.title: Baba in ’n Mandjie
story: ’n Mamma het ’n babaseuntjie gehad. ’n Slegte koning wou hom seermaak.
Toe maak die mamma ’n mandjie, soos ’n bootjie.
Sy sit haar baba daarin en laat dit op die rivier dryf. Plas, plas!
Sy groot sussie Mirjam het gekyk. Toe kry ’n prinses die baba. ‘Ek sal na hom kyk!’
God het baba Moses veilig gehou.

verse.text: God pas my op.

af.action: Wieg ’n kamma-baba in jou arms. Laat dan jou hande soos ’n bootjie op die water dryf.
lessons: God pas my op, dag en nag.
questions: Wie kyk na jou? (Mamma, Pappa… en God!)
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U my veilig hou. Amen.

en.title: Hidden in the Reeds
story: Many years after Joseph, God’s people, the Israelites, had grown into a huge nation in Egypt. A new Pharaoh came to power who didn’t care about Joseph or his God. He was afraid of the Israelites, so he made them slaves. When that didn’t stop them growing, he gave a terrible order: every baby boy must be thrown into the Nile River.

One Israelite mother, Jochebed, had a baby boy. She saw that he was special, and she hid him for three months. When she couldn’t hide him any longer, she wove a basket out of reeds, coated it with tar so it would float, laid her son inside, and placed it among the reeds at the edge of the Nile. His big sister, Miriam, hid nearby to watch.

Then Pharaoh’s own daughter came down to the river to bathe. She saw the basket, opened it, and the baby started to cry. She felt sorry for him. ‘This is one of the Hebrew babies,’ she said. Brave Miriam stepped out: ‘Shall I find a Hebrew woman to feed the baby for you?’ The princess said yes, and Miriam ran to fetch… the baby’s own mother!
So Jochebed got to raise her son, and was even paid for it! When he was older, the princess adopted him and named him Moses, which sounds like ‘drawn out’, because she drew him out of the water.

Notice that God isn’t mentioned once in these ten verses. But He was working in every detail: a mother’s courage, a sister’s quick thinking, a princess’s kind heart. The very river that was meant to destroy Moses became the place where God saved him. God was protecting the one He would later use to rescue His whole people.

verse.text: The Lord will watch over your coming and going, now and forever.

lessons: God watches over His children, even when we can’t see Him working.
God uses ordinary people’s courage and kindness in His plans.
God can turn the very thing meant for harm into a place of rescue.
questions: Who were the three women who helped save Moses?
Why do you think God isn’t mentioned in this story, even though He was clearly at work?
When have you seen God take care of you, maybe through other people?
en.listen: Be still for one minute. Ask God: ‘How have you been watching over me?’ Listen. Maybe a memory or a person will come to mind. Thank God for it.
prayer: Father, thank you that you watch over me every moment.
Thank you for the people you use to care for me, like…
Help me to trust you even when I can’t see you working.

mission.text: Tomorrow, whenever you feel worried, remind yourself: ‘God is watching over me, just like He watched over Moses.’

en.journal: Draw the basket in the reeds. Around it, write the names of people God has used to look after you.

af.title: Weggesteek in die Riete
story: Baie jare ná Josef het God se mense, die Israeliete, in Egipte ’n groot volk geword. ’n Nuwe Farao het koning geword wat nie vir Josef of sy God omgegee het nie. Hy was bang vir die Israeliete, toe maak hy hulle slawe. Toe hulle steeds meer word, het hy ’n verskriklike bevel gegee: elke babaseuntjie moet in die Nylrivier gegooi word.

Een Israelitiese ma, Jogebed, het ’n babaseuntjie gehad. Sy het gesien hy is spesiaal, en sy het hom drie maande lank weggesteek. Toe sy hom nie langer kon wegsteek nie, het sy ’n mandjie van riete gevleg, dit met teer gesmeer sodat dit kon dryf, haar seun daarin gelê en dit tussen die riete langs die Nyl neergesit. Sy groot sus, Mirjam, het naby weggekruip om te kyk.

Toe kom Farao se eie dogter na die rivier om te bad. Sy sien die mandjie, maak dit oop, en die baba begin huil. Sy het jammer vir hom gevoel. ‘Dit is een van die Hebreeuse babas,’ het sy gesê. Dapper Mirjam het nader gestap: ‘Moet ek ’n Hebreeuse vrou gaan soek om die baba vir u te voed?’ Die prinses het ja gesê, en Mirjam het gehardloop om… die baba se eie ma te gaan haal!

So het Jogebed haar eie seun grootgemaak, en sy is selfs daarvoor betaal! Toe hy ouer was, het die prinses hom aangeneem en hom Moses genoem, wat klink soos ‘uitgetrek’, want sy het hom uit die water getrek.

Let op dat God nie een keer in hierdie tien verse genoem word nie. Tog was Hy in elke klein dingetjie aan die werk: ’n ma se moed, ’n sussie se slim plan, ’n prinses se goeie hart. Die einste rivier wat Moses moes doodmaak, het die plek geword waar God hom gered het. God het die een beskerm wat Hy later sou gebruik om sy hele volk te red.

verse.text: Die Here pas jou op as jy kom en as jy gaan, nou en vir altyd.

lessons: God pas sy kinders op, selfs as ons Hom nie sien werk nie.
God gebruik gewone mense se moed en goedheid in sy planne.
God kan juis die ding wat ons moes seermaak, in ’n plek van redding verander.
questions: Wie was die drie vroue wat gehelp het om Moses te red?
Hoekom dink jy word God nie in hierdie storie genoem nie, al was Hy duidelik aan die werk?
Wanneer het jy al gesien hoe God na jou kyk, dalk deur ander mense?
af.listen: Wees een minuut lank stil. Vra God: ‘Hoe het U my opgepas?’ Luister. Dalk kom ’n herinnering of ’n mens in jou gedagtes op. Sê dankie vir God daarvoor.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U my elke oomblik oppas.
Dankie vir die mense wat U gebruik om na my te kyk, soos…
Help my om U te vertrou, selfs as ek nie sien hoe U werk nie.

mission.text: As jy môre bekommerd voel, sê vir jouself: ‘God pas my op, net soos Hy Moses opgepas het.’

af.journal: Teken die mandjie in die riete. Skryf rondom dit die name van mense wat God gebruik het om na jou te kyk.

trait.en: God watches over me
trait.af: God waak oor my

en.title: The Bush That Wouldn't Burn
story: Moses grew up and became a shepherd in the desert. One day, while looking after his sheep near a mountain, he saw something very strange: a bush on fire! The flames crackled and glowed, but the bush wasn’t burning up!
Moses went closer for a look. Then a voice came from the bush: ‘Moses! Moses!’ It was God! ‘Take off your sandals,’ God said, ‘because you are standing on holy ground.’

Holy means God is perfect and pure and completely special. There is no one like him. Moses hid his face. Then God said, ‘I have seen my people being hurt in Egypt. I have heard them crying. I am going to rescue them, and I am sending you.’
Moses asked, ‘What is your name?’ God answered, ‘I AM WHO I AM.’ God has always been, and always will be.

verse.text: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.

lessons: God is holy: perfect, pure and like no one else.
God sees and hears when his people are hurting.
God knows your name, just like he knew Moses’ name.
questions: Why do you think Moses took off his sandals?
How can we show God he is special to us? (Singing, praying quietly, listening.)
prayer: Holy God,
there is no one like you.
You are perfect and good.
Thank you that you know my name. Amen.

mission.text: Sing a song to God tomorrow, just for him.

af.title: Die Bos wat nie Uitbrand nie
story: Moses het grootgeword en ’n skaapwagter in die woestyn geword. Eendag, terwyl hy naby ’n berg na sy skape kyk, sien hy iets baie vreemds: ’n bos wat brand! Die vlamme het geknetter en gegloei, maar die bos het nie uitgebrand nie!
Moses het nader gegaan om te kyk. Toe kom ’n stem uit die bos: ‘Moses! Moses!’ Dit was God! ‘Trek jou sandale uit,’ het God gesê, ‘want jy staan op heilige grond.’

Heilig beteken God is volmaak en rein en heeltemal spesiaal. Daar is niemand soos Hy nie. Moses het sy gesig weggedraai. Toe sê God: ‘Ek het gesien hoe my mense in Egipte seergemaak word. Ek het hulle hoor huil. Ek gaan hulle red, en Ek stuur jou.’
Moses het gevra: ‘Wat is u naam?’ God het geantwoord: ‘EK IS WIE EK IS.’ God was nog altyd, en sal altyd wees.

verse.text: Heilig, heilig, heilig is die Here.

lessons: God is heilig: volmaak, rein en soos niemand anders nie.
God sien en hoor wanneer sy mense seerkry.
God ken jou naam, net soos Hy Moses se naam geken het.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Moses sy sandale uitgetrek?
Hoe kan ons vir God wys dat Hy spesiaal is vir ons? (Sing, stil bid, luister.)
prayer: Heilige God,
daar is niemand soos U nie.
U is volmaak en goed.
Dankie dat U my naam ken. Amen.

mission.text: Sing môre ’n liedjie vir God, net vir Hom.

en.title: The Bush That Wouldn't Burn
story: Moses grew up and became a shepherd in the desert. One day, while looking after his sheep near a mountain, he saw something very strange: a bush on fire! The flames crackled and glowed, but the bush wasn’t burning up!
Moses went closer for a look. Then a voice came from the bush: ‘Moses! Moses!’ It was God! ‘Take off your sandals,’ God said, ‘because you are standing on holy ground.’

Holy means God is perfect and pure and completely special. There is no one like him. Moses hid his face. Then God said, ‘I have seen my people being hurt in Egypt. I have heard them crying. I am going to rescue them, and I am sending you.’
Moses asked, ‘What is your name?’ God answered, ‘I AM WHO I AM.’ God has always been, and always will be.

verse.text: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.

lessons: God is holy: perfect, pure and like no one else.
God sees and hears when his people are hurting.
God knows your name, just like he knew Moses’ name.
questions: Why do you think Moses took off his sandals?
How can we show God he is special to us? (Singing, praying quietly, listening.)
prayer: Holy God,
there is no one like you.
You are perfect and good.
Thank you that you know my name. Amen.

mission.text: Sing a song to God tomorrow, just for him.

en.fact: In many Bibles, God’s special name is printed as LORD in capital letters. It comes from ‘I AM’.
en.deeper: What does it mean that God is holy? How is he different from everyone else?
en.journal: Write ‘Holy, holy, holy’ in your best decorated letters.

af.title: Die Bos wat nie Uitbrand nie
story: Moses het grootgeword en ’n skaapwagter in die woestyn geword. Eendag, terwyl hy naby ’n berg na sy skape kyk, sien hy iets baie vreemds: ’n bos wat brand! Die vlamme het geknetter en gegloei, maar die bos het nie uitgebrand nie!
Moses het nader gegaan om te kyk. Toe kom ’n stem uit die bos: ‘Moses! Moses!’ Dit was God! ‘Trek jou sandale uit,’ het God gesê, ‘want jy staan op heilige grond.’

Heilig beteken God is volmaak en rein en heeltemal spesiaal. Daar is niemand soos Hy nie. Moses het sy gesig weggedraai. Toe sê God: ‘Ek het gesien hoe my mense in Egipte seergemaak word. Ek het hulle hoor huil. Ek gaan hulle red, en Ek stuur jou.’
Moses het gevra: ‘Wat is u naam?’ God het geantwoord: ‘EK IS WIE EK IS.’ God was nog altyd, en sal altyd wees.

verse.text: Heilig, heilig, heilig is die Here.

lessons: God is heilig: volmaak, rein en soos niemand anders nie.
God sien en hoor wanneer sy mense seerkry.
God ken jou naam, net soos Hy Moses se naam geken het.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Moses sy sandale uitgetrek?
Hoe kan ons vir God wys dat Hy spesiaal is vir ons? (Sing, stil bid, luister.)
prayer: Heilige God,
daar is niemand soos U nie.
U is volmaak en goed.
Dankie dat U my naam ken. Amen.

mission.text: Sing môre ’n liedjie vir God, net vir Hom.

af.fact: In baie Bybels word God se spesiale naam as HERE in hoofletters geskryf. Dit kom van ‘EK IS’.
af.deeper: Wat beteken dit dat God heilig is? Hoe is Hy anders as almal?
af.journal: Skryf ‘Heilig, heilig, heilig’ in jou mooiste versierde letters.

en.title: The Bush on Fire
story: Moses looked after sheep. Baa, baa!
One day he saw a bush on fire. Crackle, crackle! But the bush did not burn up!
God called from the bush: ‘Moses! Moses!’
‘Take off your shoes,’ said God. ‘This is a special place.’
God is so special. There is no one like God!

verse.text: Holy, holy, holy is God.

en.action: Pretend to take off your shoes very slowly and quietly. Then whisper: ‘God is special.’
lessons: God is special. There is no one like Him.
questions: What sound does a sheep make?
prayer: Dear God,
you are so special. I love you. Amen.

af.title: Die Bos wat Brand
story: Moses het na skape gekyk. Mê, mê!
Eendag sien hy ’n bos wat brand. Knetter, knetter! Maar die bos brand nie op nie!
God het uit die bos geroep: ‘Moses! Moses!’
‘Trek jou skoene uit,’ het God gesê. ‘Dit is ’n spesiale plek.’
God is so spesiaal. Daar is niemand soos God nie!

verse.text: Heilig, heilig, heilig is God.

af.action: Maak of jy jou skoene baie stadig en stil uittrek. Fluister dan: ‘God is spesiaal.’
lessons: God is spesiaal. Daar is niemand soos Hy nie.
questions: Watter geluid maak ’n skaap?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is so spesiaal. Ek is lief vir U. Amen.

en.title: Holy Ground
story: Moses grew up as a prince in Pharaoh’s palace, but he never forgot that he was an Israelite. One day, when he was forty, he saw an Egyptian beating an Israelite slave. Moses killed the Egyptian, and had to run for his life into the desert. For the next forty years he worked as a shepherd, far from Egypt. He probably thought God had forgotten all about him.

Then one day, near Mount Sinai, Moses saw something strange: a bush blazing with fire, yet it wasn’t burning up. As he went closer, God called to him from the bush: ‘Moses! Moses!’ God knew his name. ‘Do not come any closer,’ God said. ‘Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.’

Holy means set apart, completely pure, and utterly different from anything else. God is not just a bigger, stronger person. He is perfectly good, with no darkness in Him at all. Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God.

But God hadn’t come to scare Moses away. He had come with a message of love: ‘I have seen the misery of my people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out. I am concerned about their suffering, and I have come down to rescue them.’ The holy God cared deeply about His hurting people, and He was sending Moses to lead them out.

Moses asked, ‘What is your name?’ God answered, ‘I AM WHO I AM.’ God didn’t begin, and He will never end. He doesn’t need anything or anyone. And yet this great, holy God chose to come close, call a shepherd by name and rescue slaves. Because of Jesus, we can come close to this holy God too, not in fear but as His children.

verse.text: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty.

lessons: God is holy: perfectly pure and good, with no one like Him.
The holy God sees, hears and cares about people who are suffering.
Because of Jesus, we can come close to the holy God as His children.
questions: Why did God tell Moses to take off his sandals?
What does God’s name, ‘I AM WHO I AM’, tell us about Him?
How does it feel to know that the holy God also knows your name and cares about you?
en.listen: Take a moment to be very still, as if you were standing on holy ground. Tell God: ‘You are holy.’ Then ask: ‘What do you want to say to me?’ Listen quietly.
prayer: Holy God, there is no one like you.
Thank you that you see and care about…
Thank you that because of Jesus I can come close to you.

mission.text: Tomorrow, find a quiet moment to worship God: sing a song or simply tell Him why He is wonderful.

en.journal: Write down five words that describe God after reading this story. Which one means the most to you, and why?

af.title: Heilige Grond
story: Moses het as ’n prins in Farao se paleis grootgeword, maar hy het nooit vergeet dat hy ’n Israeliet is nie. Eendag, toe hy veertig was, het hy gesien hoe ’n Egiptenaar ’n Israelitiese slaaf slaan. Moses het die Egiptenaar doodgemaak, en hy moes vir sy lewe na die woestyn vlug. Die volgende veertig jaar het hy as ’n skaapwagter gewerk, ver van Egipte af. Hy het seker gedink God het van hom vergeet.

Toe, op ’n dag naby die berg Sinai, sien Moses iets vreemds: ’n bos wat helder brand, maar dit brand nie op nie. Toe hy nader gaan, het God uit die bos na hom geroep: ‘Moses! Moses!’ God het sy naam geken. ‘Moenie nader kom nie,’ het God gesê. ‘Trek jou sandale uit, want die plek waar jy staan, is heilige grond.’

Heilig beteken apart, heeltemal rein, en totaal anders as enigiets anders. God is nie net ’n groter, sterker mens nie. Hy is volmaak goed, sonder enige donkerte in Hom. Moses het sy gesig weggesteek, want hy was bang om na God te kyk.

Maar God het nie gekom om Moses weg te skrik nie. Hy het met ’n boodskap van liefde gekom: ‘Ek het gesien hoe swaar my volk in Egipte kry. Ek het hulle hoor roep. Ek gee om oor hulle pyn, en Ek het afgekom om hulle te red.’ Die heilige God het baie omgegee vir sy mense wat seerkry, en Hy het Moses gestuur om hulle uit te lei.

Moses het gevra: ‘Wat is u naam?’ God het geantwoord: ‘EK IS WIE EK IS.’ God het nie begin nie, en Hy sal nooit eindig nie. Hy het niks en niemand nodig nie. En tog het hierdie groot, heilige God gekies om naby te kom, ’n skaapwagter op sy naam te roep en slawe te red. Danksy Jesus kan ons ook naby aan hierdie heilige God kom, nie bang nie, maar as sy kinders.

verse.text: Heilig, heilig, heilig is die Here, die Almagtige.

lessons: God is heilig: volmaak rein en goed, en daar is niemand soos Hy nie.
Die heilige God sien, hoor en gee om vir mense wat swaarkry.
Danksy Jesus kan ons as sy kinders naby aan die heilige God kom.
questions: Hoekom het God vir Moses gesê om sy sandale uit te trek?
Wat sê God se naam, ‘EK IS WIE EK IS’, vir ons oor Hom?
Hoe voel dit om te weet die heilige God ken ook jou naam en gee om vir jou?
af.listen: Wees ’n oomblik baie stil, asof jy op heilige grond staan. Sê vir God: ‘U is heilig.’ Vra dan: ‘Wat wil U vir my sê?’ Luister stil.
prayer: Heilige God, daar is niemand soos U nie.
Dankie dat U sien en omgee oor…
Dankie dat ek danksy Jesus naby aan U kan kom.

mission.text: Kry môre ’n stil oomblik om God te aanbid: sing ’n lied of sê net vir Hom hoekom Hy wonderlik is.

af.journal: Skryf vyf woorde neer wat God beskryf nadat jy hierdie storie gelees het. Watter een beteken die meeste vir jou, en hoekom?

trait.en: God is holy: perfect and like no one else
trait.af: God is heilig: volmaak, en daar is niemand soos Hy nie

en.title: A Path Through the Sea
story: God sent Moses to the king of Egypt: ‘Let my people go!’ After many signs from God, the king finally said yes. Off went God’s people, thousands and thousands of them!

But then the king changed his mind. He sent his army with horses and chariots to chase them. God’s people came to the edge of the Red Sea. Water in front. An army behind. Nowhere to go! They were very scared.

Moses said, ‘Don’t be afraid! The Lord will fight for you.’ Moses held out his staff, and God sent a strong wind. WHOOOOSH! The sea split in two, with walls of water on each side and dry ground in the middle! God’s people walked right through to the other side.
When they were all safe, the water came crashing back down. God had rescued them! They sang and danced and praised their mighty God.

verse.text: The Lord will fight for you. You only need to be still.

lessons: God is mighty. Even the sea obeys him.
When we feel stuck, God can make a way.
God is a rescuer.
questions: What do you think it was like to walk between walls of water?
What makes you feel stuck or scared?
prayer: Mighty God,
you can do anything!
When I feel stuck,
help me trust you to make a way. Amen.

mission.text: Learn the sea action: hands together, then push them apart like the sea opening. Do it when you feel scared.

af.title: ’n Pad deur die See
story: God het Moses na die koning van Egipte gestuur: ‘Laat my volk gaan!’ Ná baie tekens van God het die koning uiteindelik ja gesê. Daar gaan God se mense, duisende en duisende van hulle!

Maar toe verander die koning van plan. Hy stuur sy leër met perde en strydwaens agter hulle aan. God se mense het by die Rooi See gekom. Water voor. ’n Leër agter. Nêrens om heen te gaan nie! Hulle was baie bang.

Moses het gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie! Die Here sal vir julle veg.’ Moses het sy staf uitgesteek, en God het ’n sterk wind gestuur. WOESJ! Die see het in twee gesplits, met mure van water aan elke kant en droë grond in die middel! God se mense het reg deur tot aan die ander kant gestap.
Toe almal veilig was, het die water teruggestort. God het hulle gered! Hulle het gesing en gedans en hulle magtige God geprys.

verse.text: Die Here sal vir julle veg. Julle hoef net stil te wees.

lessons: God is magtig. Selfs die see luister na Hom.
As ons vasgekeer voel, kan God ’n pad maak.
God is ’n Redder.
questions: Hoe dink jy was dit om tussen mure van water te loop?
Wat laat jou vasgekeer of bang voel?
prayer: Magtige God,
U kan enigiets doen!
As ek vasgekeer voel,
help my om U te vertrou om ’n pad te maak. Amen.

mission.text: Leer die see-aksie: hande saam, druk hulle dan uitmekaar soos die see wat oopgaan. Doen dit as jy bang voel.

What makes you feel stuck or scared?

you can do anything!
When I feel stuck,

en.fact: God led his people with a tall cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night. They never needed a map!
en.deeper: The people were stuck between the sea and an army. When do you sometimes feel stuck?
en.journal: Draw the walls of water and write Exodus 14:14 on the dry path in the middle.

God is ’n Redder.

af.fact: God het sy mense bedags met ’n hoë wolk gelei en snags met ’n vuurkolom. Hulle het nooit ’n kaart nodig gehad nie!
af.deeper: Die mense was vasgekeer tussen die see en ’n leër. Wanneer voel jy soms vasgekeer?
af.journal: Teken die mure van water en skryf Eksodus 14:14 op die droë pad in die middel.

en.title: A Path Through the Sea
story: God’s people were running away from a bad king.
Oh no! The big sea was in front of them!
Moses held up his stick. Whoosh! God made the sea open up!
The water stood up like big walls. God’s people walked through on dry ground.
God saved them! They sang and danced: ‘Hooray for God!’

verse.text: God will fight for you.

en.action: Put your hands together, then push them wide apart like the sea opening. Whoosh! Then walk through the middle.
lessons: God is strong. God saves me.
questions: Can you dance and sing ‘Hooray for God’?
prayer: Thank you, God,
you are so strong! Amen.

af.title: ’n Pad deur die See
story: God se mense het weggehardloop van ’n slegte koning.
O nee! Die groot see was voor hulle!
Moses het sy stok opgehou. Woesj! God het die see laat oopgaan!
Die water het soos groot mure gestaan. God se mense het op droë grond deurgeloop.
God het hulle gered! Hulle het gesing en gedans: ‘Hoera vir God!’

verse.text: God sal vir jou veg.

af.action: Sit jou hande teen mekaar, en druk hulle dan wyd oop soos die see wat oopgaan. Woesj! Loop dan deur die middel.
lessons: God is sterk. God red my.
questions: Kan jy dans en sing ‘Hoera vir God’?
prayer: Dankie, God,
U is so sterk! Amen.

en.title: The Lord Will Fight for You
story: Moses went back to Egypt and told Pharaoh, ‘The Lord says: Let my people go!’ Pharaoh refused, again and again. So God sent ten plagues on Egypt. The last one was the most terrible: the firstborn son in every house would die. But God gave His people a way to be safe. Each family was to sacrifice a lamb and paint its blood on their doorframe. When death passed through Egypt that night, it passed over every house marked by the blood. That is why it is called the Passover, and it is a picture of Jesus, the Lamb of God, whose blood keeps us safe.
Finally Pharaoh let them go. Hundreds of thousands of Israelites marched out of Egypt, free. God led them with a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.

But then Pharaoh changed his mind and chased them with six hundred chariots. The Israelites were trapped: the Red Sea in front of them, the Egyptian army behind them. They panicked and cried out, ‘Why did you bring us out here to die?’

Moses answered with some of the bravest words in the Bible: ‘Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today. The Lord will fight for you; you need only to be still.’

God told Moses to stretch out his staff over the sea. All night a strong east wind blew, and the sea split in two, with a wall of water on the right and on the left. The Israelites walked through on dry ground! When the Egyptians followed, the water came crashing back. God’s people stood on the other shore, saved, and they sang a song of praise to the God who had rescued them.
Sometimes we feel trapped too, with a problem in front and fear behind. God doesn’t always split seas, but He is still the God who fights for His children.

verse.text: The Lord will fight for you; you need only to be still.

lessons: God is mighty: He rescues His people when there seems to be no way out.
The Passover lamb points to Jesus, whose blood keeps us safe.
When we are afraid, we can be still and trust God to fight for us.
questions: What kept the Israelite families safe on the night of the Passover?
How is Jesus like the Passover lamb?
What is a ‘Red Sea’ problem you are facing? What would it look like to ‘be still’ and trust God with it?
en.listen: Sit very still for one minute. Bring God the thing that worries you most. Ask: ‘Lord, how will you fight for me in this?’ Listen, and share what you sense with your parent.
prayer: Mighty God, you made a way through the sea.
Please fight for me in…
Thank you for Jesus, the Lamb who keeps me safe.

mission.text: Tomorrow, when you feel stuck or scared, take a deep breath and say Exodus 14:14 out loud.

en.journal: Draw the walls of water with a path through the middle. On the path, write a problem you are trusting God with.

af.title: Die Here Sal vir Jou Veg
story: Moses het teruggegaan Egipte toe en vir Farao gesê: ‘Die Here sê: Laat my volk gaan!’ Farao het keer op keer geweier. Toe stuur God tien plae oor Egipte. Die laaste een was die verskriklikste: die oudste seun in elke huis sou sterf. Maar God het vir sy mense ’n manier gegee om veilig te wees. Elke familie moes ’n lam slag en sy bloed aan hulle deurkosyn smeer. Toe die dood daardie nag deur Egipte gaan, het dit by elke huis met die bloed verbygegaan. Daarom word dit die Pasga genoem, en dit is ’n prentjie van Jesus, die Lam van God, wie se bloed ons veilig hou.
Eindelik het Farao hulle laat gaan. Honderde duisende Israeliete het vry uit Egipte gestap. God het hulle bedags met ’n wolkkolom en snags met ’n vuurkolom gelei.

Maar toe verander Farao van plan en jaag hulle agterna met seshonderd strydwaens. Die Israeliete was vasgekeer: die Rooi See voor hulle, die Egiptiese leër agter hulle. Hulle het paniekerig geword en uitgeroep: ‘Hoekom het jy ons hierheen gebring om dood te gaan?’

Moses het met van die dapperste woorde in die Bybel geantwoord: ‘Moenie bang wees nie. Staan vas, en julle sal sien hoe die Here julle vandag red. Die Here sal vir julle veg; julle hoef net stil te wees.’

God het vir Moses gesê om sy staf oor die see uit te steek. Die hele nag het ’n sterk oostewind gewaai, en die see het in twee verdeel, met ’n muur van water aan die regterkant en aan die linkerkant. Die Israeliete het op droë grond deurgeloop! Toe die Egiptenare agterna kom, het die water teruggestort. God se mense het aan die ander kant gestaan, gered, en hulle het ’n lofliedjie gesing vir die God wat hulle gered het.
Soms voel ons ook vasgekeer, met ’n probleem voor ons en vrees agter ons. God verdeel nie altyd seë nie, maar Hy is steeds die God wat vir sy kinders veg.

verse.text: Die Here sal vir julle veg; julle hoef net stil te wees.

lessons: God is magtig: Hy red sy mense as dit lyk of daar geen uitweg is nie.
Die Pasga-lam wys na Jesus, wie se bloed ons veilig hou.
As ons bang is, kan ons stil wees en God vertrou om vir ons te veg.
questions: Wat het die Israelitiese families op die Pasga-nag veilig gehou?
Hoe is Jesus soos die Pasga-lam?
Wat is ’n ‘Rooi See’-probleem wat jy het? Hoe sal dit lyk om ‘stil te wees’ en God daarmee te vertrou?
af.listen: Sit een minuut lank baie stil. Bring vir God die ding wat jou die meeste bekommer. Vra: ‘Here, hoe gaan U hierin vir my veg?’ Luister, en vertel jou ouer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Magtige God, U het ’n pad deur die see gemaak.
Veg asseblief vir my in…
Dankie vir Jesus, die Lam wat my veilig hou.

mission.text: As jy môre vasgekeer of bang voel, haal diep asem en sê Eksodus 14:14 hardop.

af.journal: Teken die mure van water met ’n pad deur die middel. Skryf op die pad ’n probleem waarmee jy God vertrou.

trait.en: God is mighty and he rescues
trait.af: God is magtig en Hy red

en.title: Bread from the Sky
story: After crossing the sea, God’s people walked into the desert. It was hot and sandy, and there were no shops, no farms and no food. Soon tummies were rumbling. ‘We’re hungry!’ the people grumbled.

God said, ‘I will rain down bread from heaven for you.’ The next morning, the ground was covered with little white flakes, like frost. ‘What is it?’ the people asked. In their language that sounds like ‘manna’, so that is what they called it! It tasted like biscuits made with honey. Yum!
Every morning God sent fresh manna, enough for everyone. In the evenings he sent birds called quail for meat. For forty years in the desert, God never once forgot to feed them.
God knows what we need, and he loves to take care of us.

verse.text: My God will meet all your needs.

lessons: God gives us what we need.
We can ask God for what we need, every day.
Instead of grumbling, we can say thank you.
questions: What are some things God gives you every day?
What could you say instead of grumbling?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for my food,
my bed and my family.
You give me everything I need. Amen.

mission.text: Before every meal tomorrow, say a thank-you prayer.

af.title: Brood uit die Hemel
story: Ná die see het God se mense die woestyn in gestap. Dit was warm en sanderig, en daar was geen winkels, geen plase en geen kos nie. Gou het mae begin grom. ‘Ons is honger!’ het die mense gekla.

God het gesê: ‘Ek sal brood uit die hemel vir julle laat reën.’ Die volgende oggend was die grond vol klein wit vlokkies, soos ryp. ‘Wat is dit?’ het die mense gevra. In hulle taal klink dit soos ‘manna’, en dit is wat hulle dit genoem het! Dit het gesmaak soos koekies met heuning. Lekker!
Elke oggend het God vars manna gestuur, genoeg vir almal. Saans het Hy voëls gestuur, kwartels, vir vleis. Veertig jaar lank in die woestyn het God nie een keer vergeet om hulle kos te gee nie.
God weet wat ons nodig het, en Hy sorg graag vir ons.

verse.text: My God sal in al julle behoeftes voorsien.

lessons: God gee ons wat ons nodig het.
Ons kan God elke dag vra vir wat ons nodig het.
In plaas daarvan om te kla, kan ons dankie sê.
questions: Watter dinge gee God elke dag vir jou?
Wat kan jy sê in plaas daarvan om te kla?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir my kos,
my bed en my familie.
U gee my alles wat ek nodig het. Amen.

mission.text: Sê môre voor elke ete ’n dankie-gebed.

en.title: Bread from the Sky
story: After crossing the sea, God’s people walked into the desert. It was hot and sandy, and there were no shops, no farms and no food. Soon tummies were rumbling. ‘We’re hungry!’ the people grumbled.

God said, ‘I will rain down bread from heaven for you.’ The next morning, the ground was covered with little white flakes, like frost. ‘What is it?’ the people asked. In their language that sounds like ‘manna’, so that is what they called it! It tasted like biscuits made with honey. Yum!
Every morning God sent fresh manna, enough for everyone. In the evenings he sent birds called quail for meat. For forty years in the desert, God never once forgot to feed them.
God knows what we need, and he loves to take care of us.

verse.text: My God will meet all your needs.

lessons: God gives us what we need.
We can ask God for what we need, every day.
Instead of grumbling, we can say thank you.
questions: What are some things God gives you every day?
What could you say instead of grumbling?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for my food,
my bed and my family.
You give me everything I need. Amen.

mission.text: Before every meal tomorrow, say a thank-you prayer.

en.fact: Each person gathered about two litres of manna a day: just enough food for that day.
en.deeper: God gave just enough for each day. Why do you think he didn’t give a whole year’s worth at once?
en.journal: Make a list of ten things God gives you every day.

af.title: Brood uit die Hemel
story: Ná die see het God se mense die woestyn in gestap. Dit was warm en sanderig, en daar was geen winkels, geen plase en geen kos nie. Gou het mae begin grom. ‘Ons is honger!’ het die mense gekla.

God het gesê: ‘Ek sal brood uit die hemel vir julle laat reën.’ Die volgende oggend was die grond vol klein wit vlokkies, soos ryp. ‘Wat is dit?’ het die mense gevra. In hulle taal klink dit soos ‘manna’, en dit is wat hulle dit genoem het! Dit het gesmaak soos koekies met heuning. Lekker!
Elke oggend het God vars manna gestuur, genoeg vir almal. Saans het Hy voëls gestuur, kwartels, vir vleis. Veertig jaar lank in die woestyn het God nie een keer vergeet om hulle kos te gee nie.
God weet wat ons nodig het, en Hy sorg graag vir ons.

verse.text: My God sal in al julle behoeftes voorsien.

lessons: God gee ons wat ons nodig het.
Ons kan God elke dag vra vir wat ons nodig het.
In plaas daarvan om te kla, kan ons dankie sê.
questions: Watter dinge gee God elke dag vir jou?
Wat kan jy sê in plaas daarvan om te kla?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir my kos,
my bed en my familie.
U gee my alles wat ek nodig het. Amen.

mission.text: Sê môre voor elke ete ’n dankie-gebed.

af.fact: Elke mens het omtrent twee liter manna per dag opgetel: net genoeg kos vir daardie dag.
af.deeper: God het net genoeg vir elke dag gegee. Hoekom dink jy het Hy nie ’n hele jaar se kos op een slag gegee nie?
af.journal: Maak ’n lys van tien dinge wat God elke dag vir jou gee.

en.title: Bread from the Sky
story: God’s people walked and walked in the hot desert.
Their tummies rumbled. ‘We are hungry!’
In the morning, there was white bread on the ground, like snow!
Yummy! It tasted like honey biscuits.
Every day God gave them food. God gives us what we need.

verse.text: God gives me what I need.

en.action: Rub your tummy and say ‘Yum, yum!’ Then pretend to pick up bread from the ground and put it in a basket.
lessons: God gives me what I need.
questions: What is your favourite food? Let’s thank God for it!
prayer: Thank you, God,
for my yummy food. Amen.

af.title: Brood uit die Hemel
story: God se mense het geloop en geloop in die warm woestyn.
Hulle maagies het gegrom. ‘Ons is honger!’
Die oggend was daar wit brood op die grond, soos sneeu!
Lekker! Dit het soos heuningkoekies gesmaak.
Elke dag het God vir hulle kos gegee. God gee vir ons wat ons nodig het.

verse.text: God gee my wat ek nodig het.

af.action: Vryf jou maag en sê ‘Lekker, lekker!’ Maak dan of jy brood van die grond optel en in ’n mandjie sit.
lessons: God gee my wat ek nodig het.
questions: Wat is jou gunstelingkos? Kom ons sê dankie vir God daarvoor!
prayer: Dankie, God,
vir my lekker kos. Amen.

en.title: Enough for Today
story: Only six weeks after God split the Red Sea, the Israelites were in the desert, and they were hungry. Instead of asking God for help, they grumbled: ‘If only we had died in Egypt! There we had pots of meat and all the bread we wanted!’ They had already forgotten how terrible slavery had been, and how mighty God had been.

God could have been angry, but instead He was generous. ‘I will rain down bread from heaven for you,’ He told Moses. That evening, flocks of quail birds covered the camp, so they had meat. The next morning, when the dew dried, the ground was covered with thin white flakes like frost. ‘What is it?’ the people asked. In Hebrew that is ‘man hu?’, so they called it manna. It tasted like wafers made with honey.

God gave simple instructions: collect just enough for each person for one day. Some people didn’t trust God, so they kept extra overnight. In the morning it was full of maggots and smelled terrible! But on the sixth day God told them to collect double, so they could rest on the Sabbath, and that manna stayed fresh. For forty years God never missed a single morning.

Why only enough for one day? Because God was teaching His people to depend on Him daily, like children who trust their father to put food on the table. That is why Jesus taught us to pray, ‘Give us today our daily bread.’
Later Jesus said something amazing: ‘I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry.’ The manna kept people alive for a day. Jesus gives us life with God that lasts forever.

verse.text: My God will meet all your needs.

lessons: God is our Provider: He gives His children what they need.
God wants us to depend on Him every day, like children trust a good father.
Jesus is the bread of life who gives us life with God forever.
questions: Why did the manna go bad when people kept extra?
Why do you think God gave just enough for one day at a time?
Instead of grumbling, what could the Israelites have done when they were hungry? What can you do when you’re worried about something?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘What do I need from you today?’ Listen. Then thank Him that He already knows and cares.
prayer: Father, thank you for giving me what I need every day, like…
Help me to trust you instead of grumbling.
Thank you that Jesus is the bread of life.

mission.text: Before every meal tomorrow, thank God for your food. And if you catch yourself grumbling, change it into a thank-you.

en.journal: Make two columns: ‘Things I need’ and ‘Things I want’. What do you notice? Thank God for everything on the first list.

af.title: Genoeg vir Vandag
story: Net ses weke nadat God die Rooi See verdeel het, was die Israeliete in die woestyn, en hulle was honger. In plaas daarvan om God om hulp te vra, het hulle gekla: ‘As ons maar net in Egipte gesterf het! Daar het ons potte vol vleis en al die brood gehad wat ons wou hê!’ Hulle het al vergeet hoe verskriklik slawerny was, en hoe magtig God was.

God kon kwaad geword het, maar Hy was eerder vrygewig. ‘Ek sal brood uit die hemel vir julle laat reën,’ het Hy vir Moses gesê. Daardie aand het swerms kwartels die kamp bedek, sodat hulle vleis gehad het. Die volgende oggend, toe die dou opdroog, was die grond bedek met dun wit vlokkies soos ryp. ‘Wat is dit?’ het die mense gevra. In Hebreeus is dit ‘man hoe?’, toe noem hulle dit manna. Dit het gesmaak soos koekies met heuning.

God het eenvoudige opdragte gegee: maak net genoeg vir elke mens vir een dag bymekaar. Party mense het God nie vertrou nie, toe hou hulle ekstra oor tot die volgende dag. Die oggend was dit vol wurms en het dit vreeslik gestink! Maar op die sesde dag het God gesê hulle moet dubbel bymekaarmaak, sodat hulle op die Sabbat kon rus, en daardie manna het vars gebly. Veertig jaar lank het God nie een oggend oorgeslaan nie.

Hoekom net genoeg vir een dag? Omdat God sy mense geleer het om elke dag op Hom staat te maak, soos kinders wat hulle pa vertrou om kos op die tafel te sit. Dit is hoekom Jesus ons geleer het om te bid: ‘Gee ons vandag ons daaglikse brood.’

Later het Jesus iets wonderliks gesê: ‘Ek is die brood van die lewe. Wie na My toe kom, sal nooit honger kry nie.’ Die manna het mense vir een dag aan die lewe gehou. Jesus gee vir ons ’n lewe saam met God wat vir altyd hou.

verse.text: My God sal in al julle behoeftes voorsien.

lessons: God is ons Voorsiener: Hy gee vir sy kinders wat hulle nodig het.
God wil hê ons moet elke dag op Hom staatmaak, soos kinders ’n goeie pa vertrou.
Jesus is die brood van die lewe wat vir ons ’n lewe saam met God gee, vir altyd.
questions: Hoekom het die manna sleg geword as mense ekstra gehou het?
Hoekom dink jy het God net genoeg vir een dag op ’n slag gegee?
Wat kon die Israeliete gedoen het in plaas daarvan om te kla toe hulle honger was? Wat kan jy doen as jy oor iets bekommerd is?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Wat het ek vandag van U nodig?’ Luister. Sê dan vir Hom dankie dat Hy dit klaar weet en omgee.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U elke dag vir my gee wat ek nodig het, soos…
Help my om U te vertrou in plaas daarvan om te kla.
Dankie dat Jesus die brood van die lewe is.

mission.text: Sê môre voor elke ete dankie vir God vir jou kos. En as jy agterkom jy kla, verander dit in ’n dankie.

af.journal: Maak twee kolomme: ‘Dinge wat ek nodig het’ en ‘Dinge wat ek graag wil hê’. Wat sien jy raak? Sê dankie vir God vir alles op die eerste lys.

trait.en: God gives me what I need
trait.af: God gee my wat ek nodig het

en.title: Rules from a Loving Father
story: God led his people to a big mountain called Mount Sinai. The mountain rumbled with thunder, lightning flashed, and a thick cloud covered the top. God called Moses to come up the mountain.

There God gave Moses ten special rules, written on two stone tablets. Love God most of all. Don’t make anything more important than God. Honour your mum and dad. Don’t steal. Don’t lie. Don’t want what belongs to others.

Why did God give rules? Not to spoil the fun! God’s rules are like the railing on a high bridge: they keep us safe. God is good, and his ways are always best for us. He gave the rules because he loves his people and wants them to live happily together.
Later, Jesus said all the rules fit into two: love God with all your heart, and love other people.

verse.text: Taste and see that the Lord is good.

lessons: God is good, and everything he tells us to do is good for us.
God’s rules show us how to love him and love others.
Obeying God is one way of loving him back.
questions: What rules does Mom have that keep you safe? Why does she make them?
Which of God’s rules is easy for you? Which one is hard?
prayer: Dear God,
you are good, and your ways are best.
Help me love you most of all
and love the people around me. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, show God you love Him: say a happy ‘yes’ the first time you’re asked.

af.title: Reëls van ’n Liefdevolle Vader
story: God het sy mense na ’n groot berg gelei wat die berg Sinai genoem word. Die berg het gedreun van die donder, weerlig het geflits, en ’n dik wolk het die bopunt bedek. God het Moses geroep om op die berg te kom.

Daar het God vir Moses tien spesiale reëls gegee, op twee kliptafels geskryf. Het God die liefste van almal. Moenie enigiets belangriker as God maak nie. Eer jou ma en pa. Moenie steel nie. Moenie lieg nie. Moenie begeer wat aan ander behoort nie.

Hoekom het God reëls gegee? Nie om die pret te bederf nie! God se reëls is soos die reling op ’n hoë brug: hulle hou ons veilig. God is goed, en sy pad is altyd die beste vir ons. Hy het die reëls gegee omdat Hy sy kinders liefhet en wil hê hulle moet gelukkig saam lewe.
Later het Jesus gesê al die reëls pas in twee: het God lief met jou hele hart, en het ander mense lief.

verse.text: Proe en sien dat die Here goed is.

lessons: God is goed, en alles wat Hy vir ons sê om te doen, is goed vir ons.
God se reëls wys ons hoe om Hom en ander lief te hê.
Om God te gehoorsaam is een manier om Hom terug lief te hê.
questions: Watter reëls het Mamma wat jou veilig hou? Hoekom maak sy hulle?
Watter een van God se reëls is maklik vir jou? Watter een is moeilik?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is goed, en u pad is die beste.
Help my om U die liefste van almal te hê
en die mense rondom my lief te hê. Amen.

mission.text: Wys môre vir God jy is lief vir Hom: sê die eerste keer bly ‘ja’ as jy gevra word.

en.fact: The Bible says the Ten Commandments were written on stone ‘by the finger of God’ (Exodus 31:18).
en.deeper: Which of the ten rules do you think is the hardest for children your age? Why?
en.journal: Write the two biggest rules Jesus gave: love God and love others. Draw a heart around them.

af.fact: Die Bybel sê die Tien Gebooie is op klip geskryf ‘met die vinger van God’ (Eksodus 31:18).
af.deeper: Watter een van die tien reëls dink jy is die moeilikste vir kinders van jou ouderdom? Hoekom?
af.journal: Skryf die twee grootste reëls wat Jesus gegee het: het God lief en het ander lief. Teken ’n hart om hulle.

en.title: God’s Good Rules
story: God’s people came to a big mountain. Boom, boom went the thunder!
God gave Moses ten good rules, written on stone.
Love God. Love your mommy and daddy. Be kind. Tell the truth.
God gave good rules because He loves His children.
We obey God because we love Him too!

verse.text: God is good.

en.action: Make thunder by drumming on your legs. Then count to ten on your fingers for God’s ten good rules.
lessons: God’s rules are good, because He loves me.
questions: What is one way you can be kind tomorrow?
prayer: Dear God,
I love you. Help me to be kind. Amen.

af.title: God se Goeie Reëls
story: God se mense het by ’n groot berg gekom. Boem, boem het die donder gegaan!
God het vir Moses tien goeie reëls gegee, op klip geskryf.
Het God lief. Het jou mamma en pappa lief. Wees gaaf. Praat die waarheid.
God het goeie reëls gegee omdat Hy sy kinders liefhet.
Ons luister na God omdat ons Hom ook liefhet!

verse.text: God is goed.

af.action: Maak donder deur op jou bene te tromme. Tel dan tot tien op jou vingers vir God se tien goeie reëls.
lessons: God se reëls is goed, want Hy is lief vir my.
questions: Hoe kan jy môre gaaf wees?
prayer: Liewe God,
ek is lief vir U. Help my om gaaf te wees. Amen.

en.title: Rescued First, Then Rules
story: Three months after leaving Egypt, the Israelites camped at the foot of Mount Sinai. Thunder rumbled, lightning flashed, a thick cloud covered the mountain, and a trumpet blast grew louder and louder. The whole mountain shook. God was about to speak to His people.

Before giving a single rule, God said this: ‘I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.’ Don’t miss the order! God didn’t say, ‘Keep these rules, and then I will rescue you.’ He rescued them first, while they were still grumbling slaves. The rules came afterwards, to show a rescued, loved people how to live as God’s family.

Then God gave the Ten Commandments. The first four are about loving God: have no other gods; don’t worship idols; honour God’s name; keep the Sabbath day holy. The last six are about loving people: honour your father and mother; do not murder; be faithful in marriage; do not steal; do not lie about others; do not want what belongs to someone else.

God’s commandments are not a list of ways to earn His love. They are like the guardrails on a mountain road: they keep us safe and show us the good way. A loving father gives his children rules because he loves them, not so that they can make him love them.

Later, someone asked Jesus which commandment is the greatest. Jesus answered: ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind… and love your neighbour as yourself.’ All the commandments hang on love. And Jesus said, ‘If you love me, keep my commands.’ We obey not to be accepted, but because we already are, and we love Him.

verse.text: Taste and see that the Lord is good.

lessons: God rescued His people first, then gave them His good commandments.
God’s commandments show us how to love Him and love others.
We obey God because we love Him, not to earn His love. He already loves us.
questions: What did God say right before He gave the Ten Commandments? Why is that order important?
Which commandments are about loving God, and which are about loving people?
Is there one of God’s commandments that is hard for you? How could loving God help you with it?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Which of your good ways do you want to help me with this week?’ Listen. God’s answer won’t sound like a scary telling-off. It will sound like a loving Father helping His child.
prayer: Father, thank you that you loved me and rescued me first.
Help me to obey you because I love you, especially with…
Thank you that your ways are good.

mission.text: Tomorrow, show God you love Him: say a happy ‘yes’ the first time a parent asks you to do something.

en.journal: Draw two tablets of stone. On the first, write ‘Love God’ and three ways you can do it. On the second, write ‘Love others’ and three ways you can do it.

af.title: Eers Gered, Dan Reëls
story: Drie maande nadat hulle uit Egipte vertrek het, het die Israeliete aan die voet van die berg Sinai kamp opgeslaan. Donder het gerommel, weerlig het geflits, ’n dik wolk het die berg bedek, en ’n trompet het al hoe harder geblaas. Die hele berg het geskud. God was op die punt om met sy mense te praat.

Voordat God een enkele reël gegee het, het Hy dit gesê: ‘Ek is die Here jou God wat jou uit Egipte gebring het, uit die land waar jy ’n slaaf was.’ Moenie die volgorde mis nie! God het nie gesê: ‘Hou hierdie reëls, dan sal Ek julle red nie.’ Hy het hulle eers gered, terwyl hulle nog klaende slawe was. Die reëls het daarna gekom, om ’n geredde, geliefde volk te wys hoe om as God se familie te lewe.

Toe gee God die Tien Gebooie. Die eerste vier gaan oor God liefhê: moenie ander gode hê nie; moenie afgode aanbid nie; eer God se naam; hou die Sabbat heilig. Die laaste ses gaan oor mense liefhê: eer jou pa en jou ma; moenie moord pleeg nie; wees getrou in die huwelik; moenie steel nie; moenie leuens oor ander vertel nie; moenie hê wat aan iemand anders behoort nie.

God se gebooie is nie ’n lys van maniere om sy liefde te verdien nie. Hulle is soos die relings langs ’n bergpad: hulle hou ons veilig en wys ons die goeie pad. ’n Liefdevolle pa gee vir sy kinders reëls omdat hy hulle liefhet, nie sodat hulle hom kan laat liefhê nie.

Later het iemand vir Jesus gevra watter gebod die grootste is. Jesus het geantwoord: ‘Jy moet die Here jou God liefhê met jou hele hart en met jou hele siel en met jou hele verstand… en jou naaste soos jouself.’ Al die gebooie hang aan liefde. En Jesus het gesê: ‘As julle My liefhet, sal julle my gebooie hou.’ Ons gehoorsaam nie om aanvaar te word nie, maar omdat ons klaar aanvaar is, en omdat ons Hom liefhet.

verse.text: Proe en sien dat die Here goed is.

lessons: God het sy mense eers gered, en hulle toe sy goeie gebooie gegee.
God se gebooie wys ons hoe om Hom en ander lief te hê.
Ons gehoorsaam God omdat ons Hom liefhet, nie om sy liefde te verdien nie. Hy het ons klaar lief.
questions: Wat het God gesê net voordat Hy die Tien Gebooie gegee het? Hoekom is daardie volgorde belangrik?
Watter gebooie gaan oor God liefhê, en watter gaan oor mense liefhê?
Is daar een van God se gebooie wat vir jou moeilik is? Hoe kan om God lief te hê jou daarmee help?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Met watter van u goeie paaie wil U my hierdie week help?’ Luister. God se antwoord sal nie soos ’n bangmaak-raas klink nie. Dit sal klink soos ’n liefdevolle Vader wat sy kind help.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U my eerste liefgehad en gered het.
Help my om U te gehoorsaam omdat ek U liefhet, veral met…
Dankie dat u paaie goed is.

mission.text: Wys môre vir God jy is lief vir Hom: sê die eerste keer bly ‘ja’ as ’n ouer jou vra om iets te doen.

af.journal: Teken twee kliptafels. Skryf op die eerste ‘Het God lief’ en drie maniere hoe jy dit kan doen. Skryf op die tweede ‘Het ander lief’ en drie maniere hoe jy dit kan doen.

trait.en: God is good, and his ways are best
trait.af: God is goed, en sy pad is die beste

en.title: The Wall That Fell Down
story: After forty years, God’s people finally reached the land God had promised them. Their new leader was Joshua. But in the way stood the city of Jericho, with huge, thick walls and gates shut tight.
God gave Joshua a very unusual plan: ‘March around the city once a day for six days. Don’t say a word. On the seventh day, march around seven times. Then blow the trumpets and shout!’

That sounded strange! Who knocks down walls by walking? But Joshua and the people trusted God. Day one: march, march, march. Day two… Day six… Then on day seven, around and around they went, seven times. The priests blew their trumpets, TOOOOOT! And everyone shouted as loud as they could.
CRASH! The great walls tumbled down flat! God had done exactly what he said.

verse.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart.

lessons: God can be trusted, even when his plan seems strange.
Obeying God brings big victories.
God does what he says he will do.
questions: Why do you think God asked them to march quietly?
Who do you trust most? Why?
prayer: Dear God,
I trust you with all my heart.
Even when I don’t understand,
help me obey you. Amen.

mission.text: March around your bed seven times tomorrow night, then shout, ‘God can be trusted!’

af.title: Die Muur wat Omgeval Het
story: Ná veertig jaar het God se mense eindelik by die land gekom wat God aan hulle belowe het. Hulle nuwe leier was Josua. Maar in die pad was die stad Jerigo, met groot, dik mure en hekke wat styf toe was.

God het vir Josua ’n baie snaakse plan gegee: ‘Marsjeer ses dae lank een keer per dag om die stad. Moenie ’n woord sê nie. Op die sewende dag, marsjeer sewe keer om. Blaas dan die trompette en skree!’

Dit het vreemd geklink! Wie slaan mure plat deur te loop? Maar Josua en die mense het God vertrou. Dag een: marsjeer, marsjeer, marsjeer. Dag twee… Dag ses… Toe op dag sewe, om en om het hulle gegaan, sewe keer. Die priesters het hulle trompette geblaas, TOETOEEET! En almal het so hard as hulle kon geskree.
KRAAAK! Die groot mure het platgeval! God het presies gedoen wat Hy gesê het.

verse.text: Vertrou op die Here met jou hele hart.

lessons: God kan vertrou word, selfs as sy plan vreemd lyk.
Om God te gehoorsaam bring groot oorwinnings.
God doen wat Hy sê Hy sal doen.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het God hulle gevra om stil te marsjeer?
Wie vertrou jy die meeste? Hoekom?
prayer: Liewe God,
ek vertrou U met my hele hart.
Selfs as ek nie verstaan nie,
help my om U te gehoorsaam. Amen.

mission.text: Marsjeer môreaand sewe keer om jou bed en skree dan: ‘God kan vertrou word!’

en.title: The Wall That Fell Down
story: After forty years, God’s people finally reached the land God had promised them. Their new leader was Joshua. But in the way stood the city of Jericho, with huge, thick walls and gates shut tight.
God gave Joshua a very unusual plan: ‘March around the city once a day for six days. Don’t say a word. On the seventh day, march around seven times. Then blow the trumpets and shout!’

That sounded strange! Who knocks down walls by walking? But Joshua and the people trusted God. Day one: march, march, march. Day two… Day six… Then on day seven, around and around they went, seven times. The priests blew their trumpets, TOOOOOT! And everyone shouted as loud as they could.
CRASH! The great walls tumbled down flat! God had done exactly what he said.

verse.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart.

lessons: God can be trusted, even when his plan seems strange.
Obeying God brings big victories.
God does what he says he will do.
questions: Why do you think God asked them to march quietly?
Who do you trust most? Why?
prayer: Dear God,
I trust you with all my heart.
Even when I don’t understand,
help me obey you. Amen.

mission.text: March around your bed seven times tomorrow night, then shout, ‘God can be trusted!’

en.fact: Jericho is one of the oldest cities in the world. People have lived there for thousands and thousands of years.
en.deeper: Why do you think God gave them such an unusual plan?
en.journal: Draw the walls tumbling down. Write one thing you will trust God with this week.

en.title: The Walls Fall Down
story: There was a city with big, big walls.
God said, ‘March around the city.’ Stomp, stomp, stomp!
They marched for seven days.
Then the trumpets went TOOOT! And everybody shouted!
CRASH! The walls fell down! God did what He said.

verse.text: Trust God with all your heart.

en.action: March around the room. Stomp, stomp! Blow a pretend trumpet, TOOOT! Then fall down: CRASH!
lessons: I can trust God. He does what He says.
questions: Can you make a trumpet sound?
prayer: Dear God,
I trust you. Amen.

af.title: Die Mure Val Om
story: Daar was ’n stad met groot, groot mure.
God het gesê: ‘Marsjeer om die stad.’ Stamp, stamp, stamp!
Hulle het sewe dae lank gemarsjeer.
Toe blaas die trompette TOETOEET! En almal skree!
KRAAK! Die mure het omgeval! God het gedoen wat Hy gesê het.

verse.text: Vertrou God met jou hele hart.

af.action: Marsjeer om die kamer. Stamp, stamp! Blaas ’n kamma-trompet, TOETOEET! Val dan om: KRAAK!

questions: Kan jy ’n trompetgeluid maak?

en.title: The Strangest Battle Plan
story: After forty years in the desert, God’s people finally stood at the edge of the land God had promised them. Moses had died, and God had chosen Joshua to lead them. God told Joshua, ‘Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.’
But right in the way stood Jericho, a city with massive walls and gates locked tight. The people inside were terrified of Israel’s God, but they weren’t going to open those gates.

God gave Joshua a battle plan that made no sense from the outside. No ladders. No battering rams. Instead: march around the city once a day for six days, with seven priests blowing ram’s horn trumpets in front of the ark of the covenant. The soldiers must stay completely silent. On the seventh day, march around seven times, then the priests blow a long blast, the people shout, and the walls will fall.
Imagine marching in silence while the people on the walls laughed at you. Day one. Day two. Nothing happened. Day six. Still nothing. But Joshua and the people kept doing exactly what God said.
On the seventh day they marched around seven times. The trumpets sounded, the people shouted, and the walls of Jericho collapsed. Israel went straight in.

Hebrews 11:30 explains it: ‘By faith the walls of Jericho fell.’ Faith isn’t pretending, and it isn’t just feeling sure. Faith is trusting God enough to do what He says, even when it seems strange, and keeping on trusting while nothing seems to be happening yet.

verse.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart and do not lean on your own understanding.

lessons: God can be trusted, even when His ways seem strange to us.
Faith means doing what God says and continuing to trust Him while we wait.
The battle belongs to God. Our part is to trust and obey.
questions: Why do you think God told the soldiers to stay silent while they marched?
What does Hebrews 11:30 say made the walls fall?
Is there something God asks you to do that doesn’t make sense to your friends? How can you keep trusting Him?
en.listen: Sit quietly. Ask God: ‘Is there a wall in my life you want to bring down?’ Listen, and talk about it with your parent.
prayer: Lord, I trust you with all my heart.
Help me to keep trusting you about…
Thank you that you always keep your word.

mission.text: Tomorrow, do one thing God asks in the Bible, even if it feels hard, like being kind to someone who isn’t kind to you.

en.journal: Draw the walls of Jericho. On each brick, write a worry or a problem. Then write across the picture: ‘By faith the walls fell.’

af.title: Die Snaaksste Gevegsplan
story: Ná veertig jaar in die woestyn het God se mense eindelik aan die rand van die land gestaan wat God aan hulle belowe het. Moses het gesterf, en God het Josua gekies om hulle te lei. God het vir Josua gesê: ‘Wees sterk en moedig. Moenie bang wees nie, want die Here jou God is by jou oral waar jy gaan.’
Maar reg in die pad was Jerigo, ’n stad met reusagtige mure en hekke wat styf gesluit was. Die mense binne was doodbang vir Israel se God, maar hulle sou nie daardie hekke oopmaak nie.

God het vir Josua ’n gevegsplan gegee wat van buite af glad nie sin gemaak het nie. Geen lere nie. Geen stormramme nie. In plaas daarvan: marsjeer ses dae lank een keer per dag om die stad, met sewe priesters wat ramshoringtrompette blaas voor die verbondsark. Die soldate moet heeltemal stil bly. Op die sewende dag, marsjeer sewe keer om, dan blaas die priesters lank, die mense skree, en die mure sal omval.

Stel jou voor jy marsjeer in stilte terwyl die mense op die mure vir jou lag. Dag een. Dag twee. Niks het gebeur nie. Dag ses. Steeds niks. Maar Josua en die mense het aangehou om presies te doen wat God gesê het.
Op die sewende dag het hulle sewe keer om gemarsjeer. Die trompette het geblaas, die mense het geskree, en die mure van Jerigo het ineengestort. Israel het reguit ingegaan.

Hebreërs 11:30 verduidelik dit: ‘Deur die geloof het die mure van Jerigo omgeval.’ Geloof is nie kamma nie, en dit is ook nie net om seker te voel nie. Geloof is om God genoeg te vertrou om te doen wat Hy sê, selfs as dit vreemd lyk, en om aan te hou vertrou terwyl dit lyk of niks nog gebeur nie.

verse.text: Vertrou op die Here met jou hele hart, en moenie op jou eie verstand staatmaak nie.

lessons: God kan vertrou word, selfs as sy paaie vir ons vreemd lyk.
Geloof beteken om te doen wat God sê en aan te hou om Hom te vertrou terwyl ons wag.
Die geveg behoort aan God. Ons deel is om te vertrou en te gehoorsaam.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het God vir die soldate gesê om stil te bly terwyl hulle marsjeer?
Wat sê Hebreërs 11:30 het die mure laat omval?
Is daar iets wat God jou vra om te doen wat vir jou maats nie sin maak nie? Hoe kan jy aanhou om Hom te vertrou?
af.listen: Sit stil. Vra God: ‘Is daar ’n muur in my lewe wat U wil laat omval?’ Luister, en gesels daaroor met jou ouer.
prayer: Here, ek vertrou U met my hele hart.
Help my om aan te hou om U te vertrou oor…
Dankie dat U altyd u woord hou.

mission.text: Doen môre een ding wat God in die Bybel vra, selfs al voel dit moeilik, soos om gaaf te wees met iemand wat nie gaaf met jou is nie.

af.journal: Teken die mure van Jerigo. Skryf op elke baksteen ’n bekommernis of ’n probleem. Skryf dan oor die prent: ‘Deur die geloof het die mure omgeval.’

en.title: Campfire Night
story: Well done, little explorer! Let’s sit by the campfire and remember: God kept baby Moses safe. God is special. God opened the sea. God gave bread from the sky. God’s rules are good. The walls fell down!

en.title: Campfire Night: The Great Rescue Road
story: What a journey! This week God protected a baby in a basket, met Moses in a burning bush, rescued His people through the Passover and the Red Sea, fed them every morning, gave them His good commandments and brought down the walls of Jericho. Every single story is about the God who rescues. And every one points ahead to Jesus, the greatest Rescuer of all.

questions: Which rescue story amazed you most? Why?
How did the Passover and the manna point to Jesus?
What has God rescued you from, or helped you through?
prayer: God, you are my Rescuer, my Provider and my Protector.
This week I saw that you…

Elke enkele storie gaan oor die God wat red. En elkeen wys vorentoe na Jesus, die grootste Redder van almal.
af.game: Reddings-tydlyn: skryf elke storie op ’n aparte stukkie papier (mandjie, bos, see, manna, berg, mure), meng hulle op, en kyk wie kan hulle eerste in die regte volgorde sit, jy of jou ouer. Sê dan een ding wat elke storie oor God wys.
questions: Watter reddingstorie het jou die meeste verbaas? Hoekom?
Hoe het die Pasga en die manna na Jesus gewys?
Waarvan het God jou al gered, of waardeur het Hy jou gehelp?
prayer: God, U is my Redder, my Voorsiener en my Beskermer.
Hierdie week het ek gesien dat U…
Dankie vir Jesus, die grootste Redder van almal.

mission.text: Leer Eksodus 14:14 uit jou kop en sê dit vir iemand in jou familie.

af.journal: Skryf ’n kort dankie-brief aan God vir ’n keer toe Hy jou gered of gehelp het.

en.title: A Voice in the Night
story: Samuel was a boy who lived in God’s house, the temple, helping an old priest named Eli. One night, while Samuel was lying in bed, he heard a voice: ‘Samuel!’
He jumped up and ran to Eli. ‘Here I am! You called me.’ ‘I didn’t call you,’ said Eli. ‘Go back to bed.’ It happened again. And again! Three times!

Then Eli understood. ‘It is God calling you. Next time, say, “Speak, Lord, I’m listening.”’ So Samuel lay down, and the voice came again: ‘Samuel! Samuel!’ This time Samuel said, ‘Speak, Lord. Your servant is listening.’ And God told Samuel important things.
God talked to a boy! Today God speaks to us mostly through the Bible, and sometimes with a quiet thought in our hearts that reminds us of what is good and true.

verse.text: Speak, Lord. I am listening.

lessons: God talks to children, not just grown-ups.
God speaks to us through the Bible.
As a child of God and a friend of Jesus, we talk to him AND listen to him.
questions: How can we listen to God?
Let’s be very quiet for ten seconds and think about God. What came into your mind?
prayer: Dear God,
speak to me. I am listening.
Help me hear you when I read the Bible
and do what you say. Amen.

mission.text: Ask Mom to read you one Bible verse tomorrow and tell you what it means.

af.title: ’n Stem in die Nag
story: Samuel was ’n seun wat in God se huis, die tempel, gewoon het en ’n ou priester met die naam Eli gehelp het. Een nag, terwyl Samuel in die bed lê, hoor hy ’n stem: ‘Samuel!’
Hy het opgespring en na Eli gehardloop. ‘Hier is ek! U het my geroep.’ ‘Ek het jou nie geroep nie,’ sê Eli. ‘Gaan terug bed toe.’ Dit het weer gebeur. En weer! Drie keer!

Toe het Eli verstaan. ‘Dit is God wat jou roep. Volgende keer sê jy: “Praat, Here, ek luister.”’ Samuel het gaan lê, en die stem het weer gekom: ‘Samuel! Samuel!’ Hierdie keer het Samuel gesê: ‘Praat, Here. U dienaar luister.’ En God het vir Samuel belangrike dinge vertel.
God het met ’n seun gepraat! Vandag praat God met ons meestal deur die Bybel, en soms met ’n stil gedagte in ons hart wat ons herinner aan wat goed en waar is.

verse.text: Praat, Here. Ek luister.

lessons: God praat met kinders, nie net met grootmense nie.
God praat met ons deur die Bybel.
As kind van God en vriend van Jesus praat ons met Hom EN luister ons na Hom.
questions: Hoe kan ons na God luister?
Kom ons is tien sekondes baie stil en dink aan God. Wat het in jou gedagtes opgekom?
prayer: Liewe God,
praat met my. Ek luister.
Help my om U te hoor as ek die Bybel lees
en te doen wat U sê. Amen.

mission.text: Vra môre vir Mamma om vir jou een Bybelvers te lees en te vertel wat dit beteken.

en.title: Samuel, Samuel!
story: Samuel was a little boy. He lived in God’s house.
One night, in bed, he heard a voice: ‘Samuel!’
He ran to old Eli. ‘Here I am!’ But Eli said, ‘I didn’t call you.’
It was God calling! So Samuel said, ‘Speak, God. I am listening.’
God talks to children too. God talks to you!

verse.text: Speak, God. I am listening.

en.action: Cup your hand behind your ear and whisper: ‘I am listening.’ Then be very, very quiet for five seconds.
lessons: God talks to me, and I can listen.
questions: Can you be as quiet as a little mouse?
prayer: Dear God,
I am listening. Amen.

af.title: Samuel, Samuel!
story: Samuel was ’n klein seuntjie. Hy het in God se huis gewoon.
Een nag, in die bed, hoor hy ’n stem: ‘Samuel!’
Hy hardloop na ou Eli. ‘Hier is ek!’ Maar Eli sê: ‘Ek het jou nie geroep nie.’
Dit was God wat geroep het! Toe sê Samuel: ‘Praat, God. Ek luister.’
God praat ook met kinders. God praat met jou!

verse.text: Praat, God. Ek luister.

af.action: Hou jou hand agter jou oor en fluister: ‘Ek luister.’ Wees dan vyf sekondes lank baie, baie stil.
lessons: God praat met my, en ek kan luister.
questions: Kan jy so stil soos ’n muisie wees?
prayer: Liewe God,
ek luister. Amen.

en.title: Speak, Lord, I’m Listening
story: Samuel’s mother, Hannah, had prayed for years for a child. When God gave her Samuel, she kept her promise and brought him to the house of the Lord to serve God with Eli, the old priest. So Samuel grew up in the tabernacle, helping Eli, lighting lamps and opening doors.
The Bible says that in those days ‘the word of the Lord was rare’. Not many people were hearing from God, because most of them weren’t listening.

One night, while Samuel was lying down near the ark of God, he heard a voice calling, ‘Samuel!’ He jumped up and ran to Eli: ‘Here I am; you called me.’ ‘I didn’t call,’ said Eli. ‘Go back to bed.’ This happened three times. Samuel didn’t recognise God’s voice yet, because he had never heard it before.

Finally Eli understood that God was calling the boy. He gave Samuel wise advice: ‘If He calls you, say, “Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.”’ So the next time God called, Samuel answered exactly that way, and God spoke to him.

This story shows us three important things. First, God speaks to children, not just to grown-ups. Second, we often need to learn to recognise His voice, and wise older believers can help us, the way Eli helped Samuel. Third, God mostly speaks through His written Word, the Bible, and His Spirit also speaks to our hearts. What He says personally will always agree with the Bible.
The chapter ends by saying that ‘the Lord was with Samuel as he grew up’. Samuel became a prophet who listened to God his whole life. It all began with a boy who said, ‘Speak, Lord. I’m listening.’

verse.text: Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.

lessons: God speaks to children, and He wants to speak to you.
We learn to recognise God’s voice over time, and wise believers can help us.
God speaks through the Bible and by His Spirit, and He never contradicts His Word.
questions: Why didn’t Samuel recognise God’s voice at first?
How did Eli help Samuel? Who helps you to hear God?
What helps you to listen to God? What makes it hard?
en.listen: Pray Samuel’s prayer: ‘Speak, Lord, I’m listening.’ Then sit quietly for two minutes. Write down any thought, Bible verse or picture that comes to mind. Show it to your parent, and check together that it agrees with the Bible.
prayer: Speak, Lord, I’m listening.
Help me to recognise your voice when…
Thank you that you want to talk with me.

mission.text: Tomorrow, read one verse from the Bible and ask God: ‘What do you want to say to me through this?’

en.journal: Start a ‘Listening page’ in your journal. Write today’s date and anything you sensed God saying during your quiet time.

af.title: Praat, Here, Ek Luister
story: Samuel se ma, Hanna, het jare lank vir ’n kind gebid. Toe God vir haar Samuel gee, het sy haar belofte gehou en hom na die huis van die Here gebring om God saam met Eli, die ou priester, te dien. So het Samuel in die tabernakel grootgeword, waar hy vir Eli gehelp, lampe aangesteek en deure oopgemaak het.
Die Bybel sê dat in daardie dae ‘die woord van die Here skaars was’. Nie baie mense het van God gehoor nie, want die meeste van hulle het nie geluister nie.

Een nag, terwyl Samuel naby die ark van God gelê het, het hy ’n stem hoor roep: ‘Samuel!’ Hy het opgespring en na Eli gehardloop: ‘Hier is ek; u het my geroep.’ ‘Ek het nie geroep nie,’ het Eli gesê. ‘Gaan terug bed toe.’ Dit het drie keer gebeur. Samuel het God se stem nog nie herken nie, want hy het dit nog nooit gehoor nie.

Eindelik het Eli verstaan dat God die seun roep. Hy het vir Samuel wyse raad gegee: ‘As Hy jou roep, sê: “Praat, Here, u dienaar luister.”’ Die volgende keer toe God roep, het Samuel presies so geantwoord, en God het met hom gepraat.

Hierdie storie wys ons drie belangrike dinge. Eerstens: God praat met kinders, nie net met grootmense nie. Tweedens: ons moet dikwels leer om sy stem te herken, en wyse ouer gelowiges kan ons help, soos Eli vir Samuel gehelp het. Derdens: God praat meestal deur sy geskrewe Woord, die Bybel, en sy Gees praat ook met ons harte. Wat Hy persoonlik sê, sal altyd ooreenstem met die Bybel.

Die hoofstuk eindig deur te sê dat ‘die Here met Samuel was terwyl hy grootgeword het’. Samuel het ’n profeet geword wat sy hele lewe lank na God geluister het. Dit het alles begin met ’n seun wat gesê het: ‘Praat, Here. Ek luister.’

verse.text: Praat, Here, u dienaar luister.

lessons: God praat met kinders, en Hy wil met jou praat.
Ons leer mettertyd om God se stem te herken, en wyse gelowiges kan ons help.
God praat deur die Bybel en deur sy Gees, en Hy sê nooit iets teen sy Woord nie.
questions: Hoekom het Samuel eers nie God se stem herken nie?
Hoe het Eli vir Samuel gehelp? Wie help jou om God te hoor?
Wat help jou om na God te luister? Wat maak dit moeilik?
af.listen: Bid Samuel se gebed: ‘Praat, Here, ek luister.’ Sit dan twee minute lank stil. Skryf enige gedagte, Bybelvers of prentjie neer wat in jou gedagtes opkom. Wys dit vir jou ouer, en kyk saam of dit met die Bybel ooreenstem.
prayer: Praat, Here, ek luister.
Help my om u stem te herken wanneer…
Dankie dat U met my wil praat.

mission.text: Lees môre een vers uit die Bybel en vra God: ‘Wat wil U deur hierdie vers vir my sê?’

af.journal: Begin ’n ‘Luisterblad’ in jou joernaal. Skryf vandag se datum neer en enigiets wat jy aangevoel het God sê in jou stil tyd.

trait.en: God talks to me, and I can listen
trait.af: God praat met my, en ek kan luister

en.title: The Shepherd Boy Chosen
story: God sent the prophet Samuel (yes, the same Samuel, now all grown up!) to the house of a man named Jesse. ‘One of Jesse’s sons will be the next king,’ God said.

Jesse’s oldest son walked in. He was tall and strong. ‘Surely this is the one!’ thought Samuel. But God said, ‘No. People look at the outside, but I look at the heart.’ Seven sons walked past, and God said no to every one.
‘Do you have any more sons?’ Samuel asked. ‘Only the youngest, David. He’s out looking after the sheep.’ They fetched David, still smelling like sheep! And God said, ‘This is the one.’
David was the youngest and the smallest, but he had a heart that loved God. God chose him to be king.

verse.text: People look at the outside, but the Lord looks at the heart.

lessons: God cares most about what is inside: our heart.
You don’t have to be big to be important to God.
God sees what no one else sees.
questions: What does it mean to have a heart that loves God?
How can we see other people the way God does?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you see my heart.
Make my heart kind and brave
and full of love for you. Amen.

mission.text: Be kind tomorrow to someone who often gets left out.

af.title: Die Skaapwagter wat Gekies Is
story: God het die profeet Samuel (ja, dieselfde Samuel, nou heeltemal groot!) na die huis van ’n man met die naam Isai gestuur. ‘Een van Isai se seuns sal die volgende koning wees,’ het God gesê.

Isai se oudste seun het ingestap. Hy was lank en sterk. ‘Dit is sekerlik hy!’ het Samuel gedink. Maar God het gesê: ‘Nee. Mense kyk na die buitekant, maar Ek kyk na die hart.’ Sewe seuns het verbygestap, en God het nee gesê vir elkeen.
‘Het jy nog seuns?’ vra Samuel. ‘Net die jongste, Dawid. Hy is buite by die skape.’ Hulle het Dawid gaan haal, hy het nog na skape geruik! En God het gesê: ‘Dit is hy.’
Dawid was die jongste en die kleinste, maar hy het ’n hart gehad wat lief was vir God. God het hom gekies om koning te wees.

verse.text: Mense kyk na die buitekant, maar die Here kyk na die hart.

lessons: God gee die meeste om oor wat binne is: ons hart.
Jy hoef nie groot te wees om vir God belangrik te wees nie.
God sien wat niemand anders sien nie.
questions: Wat beteken dit om ’n hart te hê wat lief is vir God?
Hoe kan ons ander mense sien soos God hulle sien?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my hart sien.
Maak my hart gaaf en dapper
en vol liefde vir U. Amen.

mission.text: Wees môre gaaf met iemand wat dikwels uitgelos word.
