en.title: God Sees My Heart
story: God said, ‘One of Jesse’s boys will be king.’
The big, tall brothers came. But God said, ‘Not him… not him… not him.’
The littlest one, David, was out with the sheep.
God said, ‘David is the one! I see his heart. He loves me.’
God sees your heart too. God loves you!

verse.text: God looks at the heart.

en.action: Stand up tall like the big brothers, then crouch down small like little David. Put your hand on your heart: ‘God sees my heart!’
lessons: God sees my heart, and He loves me.
questions: Where is your heart? Can you put your hand on it?
prayer: Dear God,
please give me a heart that loves you. Amen.

af.title: God Sien My Hart
story: God het gesê: ‘Een van Isai se seuns sal koning wees.’
Die groot, lang broers het gekom. Maar God het gesê: ‘Nie hy nie… nie hy nie… nie hy nie.’
Die kleinste een, Dawid, was buite by die skape.
God het gesê: ‘Dawid is die een! Ek sien sy hart. Hy is lief vir My.’
God sien jou hart ook. God is lief vir jou!

verse.text: God kyk na die hart.

af.action: Staan lank soos die groot broers, en hurk dan klein soos klein Dawid. Sit jou hand op jou hart: ‘God sien my hart!’
lessons: God sien my hart, en Hy is lief vir my.
questions: Waar is jou hart? Kan jy jou hand daarop sit?
prayer: Liewe God,
gee my asseblief ’n hart wat U liefhet. Amen.

en.title: The Heart God Sees
story: Israel’s first king, Saul, was tall and impressive, but he stopped obeying God. So God sent the prophet Samuel, now an old man, to Bethlehem, to the family of a man called Jesse. ‘I have chosen one of his sons to be king,’ God said.

Jesse’s sons came in one by one. First came Eliab, the eldest, tall and strong. Samuel thought, ‘Surely this is the one!’ But God said, ‘Do not look at his appearance or his height. The Lord does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.’

Seven sons walked past, and God said no to every one. Samuel was puzzled. ‘Are these all the sons you have?’ Jesse answered, ‘There is still the youngest. He is looking after the sheep.’ Nobody had even thought to invite David!

They sent for him, and the Lord said, ‘Rise and anoint him; this is the one.’ Samuel poured oil on David’s head in front of his brothers, and the Bible says, ‘From that day on the Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon David.’

What did God see in David’s heart? Out in the fields, alone with the sheep, David had been getting to know God. He sang to Him, trusted Him and loved Him. Later the Bible calls David ‘a man after God’s own heart’. David wasn’t perfect; he made some big mistakes later on. But his heart kept turning back to God.

God still looks at hearts today. He isn’t impressed by how tall, clever, popular or good-looking you are. He sees the real you, on the inside, and He loves you. And when you belong to Jesus, His Spirit lives in you, just as He came upon David.

verse.text: People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.

lessons: God looks at the heart, not at outward appearance.
Time alone with God, like David with his sheep, grows a heart that loves Him.
God’s Spirit empowers the people He chooses, and lives in everyone who follows Jesus.
questions: Why did Samuel think Eliab would be the king?
What do you think David did out in the fields that grew his heart for God?
How do you sometimes judge people by how they look? How could you look at their hearts instead?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘What do you see when you look at my heart?’ Listen. His answer will be truthful but always loving. Write down what you sense.
prayer: Lord, thank you that you see my heart.
Make my heart like David’s: a heart that loves you and…
Fill me with your Holy Spirit.

mission.text: Tomorrow, look out for someone who is often overlooked, like David was, and include them.

en.journal: Draw a big heart. Inside it, write what you want God to find there. Outside it, write things people usually notice about you.

af.title: Die Hart wat God Sien
story: Israel se eerste koning, Saul, was lank en indrukwekkend, maar hy het opgehou om God te gehoorsaam. Toe stuur God die profeet Samuel, nou ’n ou man, na Betlehem, na die familie van ’n man met die naam Isai. ‘Ek het een van sy seuns gekies om koning te wees,’ het God gesê.

Isai se seuns het een vir een ingekom. Eerste was Eliab, die oudste, lank en sterk. Samuel het gedink: ‘Dit is sekerlik hy!’ Maar God het gesê: ‘Moenie na sy voorkoms of sy lengte kyk nie. Die Here kyk nie na wat mense na kyk nie. Mense kyk na die buitekant, maar die Here kyk na die hart.’

Sewe seuns het verbygestap, en God het vir elkeen nee gesê. Samuel was verward. ‘Is dit al die seuns wat jy het?’ Isai het geantwoord: ‘Daar is nog die jongste. Hy pas die skape op.’ Niemand het eers daaraan gedink om Dawid te nooi nie!

Hulle het hom laat roep, en die Here het gesê: ‘Staan op en salf hom; dit is hy.’ Samuel het olie op Dawid se kop gegooi voor sy broers, en die Bybel sê: ‘Van daardie dag af het die Gees van die Here kragtig oor Dawid gekom.’

Wat het God in Dawid se hart gesien? Buite in die veld, alleen by die skape, het Dawid vir God leer ken. Hy het vir Hom gesing, Hom vertrou en Hom liefgehad. Later noem die Bybel Dawid ‘’n man na God se hart’. Dawid was nie volmaak nie; hy het later groot foute gemaak. Maar sy hart het altyd weer na God teruggedraai.

God kyk vandag nog na harte. Hy is nie beïndruk deur hoe lank, slim, gewild of mooi jy is nie. Hy sien die regte jy, aan die binnekant, en Hy is lief vir jou. En as jy aan Jesus behoort, woon sy Gees in jou, net soos Hy oor Dawid gekom het.

verse.text: Mense kyk na die buitekant, maar die Here kyk na die hart.

lessons: God kyk na die hart, nie na die buitekant nie.
Tyd alleen met God, soos Dawid by sy skape, laat ’n hart groei wat Hom liefhet.
God se Gees gee krag aan die mense wat Hy kies, en woon in almal wat Jesus volg.
questions: Hoekom het Samuel gedink Eliab sal die koning wees?
Wat dink jy het Dawid in die veld gedoen wat sy hart vir God laat groei het?
Hoe oordeel jy soms mense op grond van hoe hulle lyk? Hoe kan jy eerder na hulle harte kyk?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Wat sien U as U na my hart kyk?’ Luister. Sy antwoord sal eerlik wees, maar altyd liefdevol. Skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Here, dankie dat U my hart sien.
Maak my hart soos Dawid s’n: ’n hart wat U liefhet en…
Vul my met u Heilige Gees.

mission.text: Kyk môre uit vir iemand wat dikwels oor die hoof gesien word, soos Dawid, en sluit hulle in.

af.journal: Teken ’n groot hart. Skryf daarin wat jy wil hê God daar moet kry. Skryf buite die hart dinge wat mense gewoonlik van jou raaksien.

trait.en: God looks at my heart
trait.af: God kyk na my hart

en.title: The Giant Goes Down
story: God’s people were at war, and the enemy had a giant called Goliath. He was nearly three metres tall, taller than a basketball hoop! Every day he stomped out and roared, ‘Who will fight me?’ And all the soldiers ran away, shaking.
Young David came to bring food to his brothers. He heard Goliath shouting and said, ‘Who does he think he is, talking about God’s people like that? I’ll fight him!’
The king offered David his armour, but it was far too big and clanky. So David took only his shepherd’s sling and picked five smooth stones from a stream.

Goliath laughed at him. But David called out, ‘You come with a sword, but I come in the name of the Lord!’ David swung his sling, whirr, whirr, whirr, and let go. The stone hit Goliath right on the forehead. THUD! The giant fell flat on his face. God had won the battle!

verse.text: Be strong and brave. The Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.

lessons: God makes us brave, not because we are big, but because he is with us.
Our ‘giants’ (big fears or problems) are small to God.
We can face hard things in God’s name.
questions: What is a ‘giant’ you might face? (A fear, or something hard to do.)
What would David say to you about it?
prayer: Dear God,
you are bigger than any giant.
When I’m scared, make me brave,
because you are with me. Amen.

mission.text: Pick one brave thing to do tomorrow (try a new food, say hi to someone new) and do it with God.

af.title: Die Reus Val Plat
story: God se mense was in ’n oorlog, en die vyand het ’n reus met die naam Goliat gehad. Hy was amper drie meter lank, langer as ’n basketbalring! Elke dag het hy uitgestamp en gebrul: ‘Wie sal teen my veg?’ En al die soldate het bewend weggehardloop.
Die jong Dawid het kos vir sy broers kom bring. Hy het Goliat hoor skree en gesê: ‘Wie dink hy is hy om so oor God se mense te praat? Ek sal teen hom veg!’
Die koning het vir Dawid sy wapenrusting aangebied, maar dit was heeltemal te groot en te raserig. Toe neem Dawid net sy skaapwagter-slinger en kies vyf gladde klippe uit ’n stroompie.

Goliat het vir hom gelag. Maar Dawid het uitgeroep: ‘Jy kom met ’n swaard, maar ek kom in die Naam van die Here!’ Dawid het sy slinger geswaai, woer, woer, woer, en laat los. Die klip het Goliat reg op die voorkop getref. DOEF! Die reus het plat op sy gesig geval. God het die geveg gewen!

verse.text: Wees sterk en dapper. Die Here jou God is by jou oral waar jy gaan.

lessons: God maak ons dapper, nie omdat ons groot is nie, maar omdat Hy by ons is.
Ons ‘reuse’ (groot vrese of probleme) is klein vir God.
Ons kan moeilike dinge in God se Naam aanpak.
questions: Wat is ’n ‘reus’ wat jy dalk moet aanpak? (’n Vrees, of iets wat moeilik is om te doen.)
Wat sou Dawid vir jou daaroor sê?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is groter as enige reus.
As ek bang is, maak my dapper,
want U is by my. Amen.

mission.text: Kies een dapper ding om môre te doen (proe ’n nuwe kos, groet iemand nuut) en doen dit saam met God.

en.title: David and the Giant
story: There was a giant called Goliath. He was big, big, BIG!
‘Who will fight me?’ he shouted. Everyone was scared.
But little David said, ‘God is with me!’
David took his sling and a little stone. Swing, swing… whoosh!
The giant fell down. God made David brave!

verse.text: Be brave! God is with you.

en.action: Stand on your tiptoes and stretch up high like a giant. Then swing a pretend sling: swing, swing, whoosh!
lessons: God makes me brave. He is with me.
questions: What makes you feel scared? God is with you!
prayer: Dear God,
please make me brave. Amen.

af.title: Dawid en die Reus
story: Daar was ’n reus met die naam Goliat. Hy was groot, groot, GROOT!
‘Wie sal teen my veg?’ het hy geskree. Almal was bang.
Maar klein Dawid het gesê: ‘God is by my!’
Dawid het sy slinger en ’n klein klippie gevat. Swaai, swaai… woesj!
Die reus het omgeval. God het Dawid dapper gemaak!

verse.text: Wees dapper! God is by jou.

af.action: Staan op jou tone en rek hoog soos ’n reus. Swaai dan ’n kamma-slinger: swaai, swaai, woesj!
lessons: God maak my dapper. Hy is by my.
questions: Wat maak jou bang? God is by jou!
prayer: Liewe God,
maak my asseblief dapper. Amen.

en.title: In the Name of the Lord
story: The Philistine army had a champion called Goliath. He was nearly three metres tall, and his armour alone weighed about as much as a grown man. For forty days, morning and evening, he stood in the valley and shouted insults at Israel and at Israel’s God: ‘Choose a man and have him come down to me!’ King Saul and all his soldiers were terrified.

Young David arrived with food for his older brothers and heard the giant’s challenge. He was shocked, not by Goliath’s size, but by his words. ‘Who is this man that he should defy the armies of the living God?’

David went to King Saul. ‘Let no one lose heart. I will fight him.’ Saul laughed: ‘You’re only a boy!’ But David explained that, while looking after his father’s sheep, he had fought off a lion and a bear. ‘The Lord who rescued me from the paw of the lion and the bear will rescue me from this Philistine.’ David’s courage came from remembering what God had already done.

Saul gave David his own armour, but it was far too big. So David took only his shepherd’s staff, his sling and five smooth stones from a stream. Goliath sneered at him. But David answered with words full of faith: ‘You come against me with sword and spear, but I come against you in the name of the Lord Almighty. The battle is the Lord’s.’
David ran toward the giant, swung his sling, and the stone struck Goliath on the forehead. The giant fell face down. Israel won the victory that day.

Faith is not pretending a problem is small. David knew Goliath was huge. Faith is knowing that God is bigger. David spoke what God had said, not what the giant said. When we face ‘giants’ of fear, bullying or problems, we can do the same: remember what God has done, speak what He says, and go forward in His name.

verse.text: Be strong and courageous. The Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.

lessons: Our courage comes from knowing that God is bigger than any ‘giant’.
Remembering what God has already done builds our faith for today.
We can speak what God says about our problems, not what our fears say.
questions: Where did David’s courage come from?
What did David say to Goliath? Why were those words full of faith?
What is a ‘giant’ in your life? What does God say about it?
en.listen: Bring your ‘giant’ to God. Ask: ‘Lord, what do you say about this?’ Listen quietly, then find a Bible verse with your parent that answers your fear.
prayer: Lord, you are bigger than any giant.
I bring you my giant: …
Thank you that I can face it in your name.

mission.text: Write tonight’s verse (Joshua 1:9) on a card and say it out loud tomorrow when you face something scary.

en.journal: Make two lists: ‘What the giant says’ and ‘What God says’. Which list will you choose to believe?

af.title: In die Naam van die Here
story: Die Filistynse leër het ’n kampvegter met die naam Goliat gehad. Hy was amper drie meter lank, en net sy wapenrusting was omtrent so swaar soos ’n grootmens. Veertig dae lank, soggens en saans, het hy in die vallei gestaan en Israel en Israel se God uitgeskel: ‘Kies ’n man en laat hom na my toe afkom!’ Koning Saul en al sy soldate was doodbang.

Die jong Dawid het met kos vir sy ouer broers aangekom en die reus se uitdaging gehoor. Hy was geskok, nie oor Goliat se grootte nie, maar oor sy woorde. ‘Wie is hierdie man dat hy die leër van die lewende God uitdaag?’

Dawid het na koning Saul gegaan. ‘Laat niemand moed verloor nie. Ek sal teen hom veg.’ Saul het gelag: ‘Jy is net ’n seun!’ Maar Dawid het verduidelik dat hy, terwyl hy sy pa se skape opgepas het, teen ’n leeu en ’n beer geveg het. ‘Die Here wat my uit die klou van die leeu en die beer gered het, sal my uit die hand van hierdie Filistyn red.’ Dawid se moed het gekom van onthou wat God al gedoen het.

Saul het vir Dawid sy eie wapenrusting gegee, maar dit was heeltemal te groot. Toe het Dawid net sy skaapwagterstok, sy slinger en vyf gladde klippe uit ’n stroompie gevat. Goliat het vir hom gespot. Maar Dawid het geantwoord met woorde vol geloof: ‘Jy kom na my met ’n swaard en ’n spies, maar ek kom na jou in die Naam van die Here, die Almagtige. Die geveg behoort aan die Here.’
Dawid het na die reus toe gehardloop, sy slinger geswaai, en die klip het Goliat teen die voorkop getref. Die reus het op sy gesig neergeval. Israel het daardie dag die oorwinning behaal.

Geloof is nie om te maak of ’n probleem klein is nie. Dawid het geweet Goliat is reusagtig. Geloof is om te weet dat God groter is. Dawid het gesê wat God gesê het, nie wat die reus gesê het nie. As ons ‘reuse’ van vrees, boelies of probleme teëkom, kan ons dieselfde doen: onthou wat God gedoen het, sê wat Hy sê, en gaan vorentoe in sy Naam.

verse.text: Wees sterk en moedig. Die Here jou God is by jou oral waar jy gaan.

lessons: Ons moed kom daarvan om te weet dat God groter is as enige ‘reus’.
As ons onthou wat God al gedoen het, groei ons geloof vir vandag.
Ons kan sê wat God oor ons probleme sê, nie wat ons vrese sê nie.
questions: Waar het Dawid se moed vandaan gekom?
Wat het Dawid vir Goliat gesê? Hoekom was daardie woorde vol geloof?
Wat is ’n ‘reus’ in jou lewe? Wat sê God daaroor?
af.listen: Bring jou ‘reus’ na God. Vra: ‘Here, wat sê U hieroor?’ Luister stil, en soek dan saam met jou ouer ’n Bybelvers wat jou vrees antwoord.
prayer: Here, U is groter as enige reus.
Ek bring vir U my reus: …
Dankie dat ek dit in u Naam kan aanpak.

mission.text: Skryf vanaand se vers (Josua 1:9) op ’n kaartjie en sê dit môre hardop as jy iets bangmakends teëkom.

af.journal: Maak twee lyste: ‘Wat die reus sê’ en ‘Wat God sê’. Watter lys gaan jy kies om te glo?

trait.en: God makes me brave
trait.af: God maak my dapper

en.title: The Good Shepherd Song
story: Remember David the shepherd boy? Out in the fields with his sheep, David would play his harp and write songs to God. One of his songs is one of the most famous songs in the whole world. It is called Psalm 23.

David knew all about sheep. Sheep can’t find their own food. They wander off. They get scared of wolves. They need a shepherd to lead them to green grass and cool water, and to chase away wild animals with his rod and staff.

So David thought, ‘God is like my shepherd! And I am like his sheep!’ God leads us. God feeds us. God protects us. When we go through dark, scary places, God walks right beside us, and he leads us home.
At the end of his song David says, ‘I will live in the house of the Lord forever.’

verse.text: The Lord is my shepherd. I have everything I need.

lessons: God is like a good shepherd who takes care of his sheep.
Even in dark places, God is beside us.
We can follow God like sheep follow their shepherd.
questions: How does a shepherd look after sheep? How does God look after you?
Let’s say it on five fingers: The – Lord – is – my – shepherd.
prayer: Dear Lord,
you are my shepherd.
Lead me, feed me and keep me safe.
I will follow you. Amen.

mission.text: Practise saying ‘The Lord is my shepherd’ on your five fingers.

af.title: Die Goeie Herder se Lied
story: Onthou jy Dawid die skaapwagterseun? Buite in die veld by sy skape het Dawid op sy harp gespeel en liedjies vir God geskryf. Een van sy liedjies is een van die bekendste liedjies in die hele wêreld. Dit heet Psalm 23.

Dawid het alles van skape geweet. Skape kan nie self kos kry nie. Hulle dwaal weg. Hulle word bang vir wolwe. Hulle het ’n herder nodig om hulle na groen gras en koel water te lei, en om wilde diere met sy stok en staf weg te jaag.
Toe dink Dawid: ‘God is soos my herder! En ek is soos sy skaap!’ God lei ons. God voed ons. God beskerm ons. As ons deur donker, bang plekke gaan, loop God reg langs ons, en Hy lei ons huis toe.
Aan die einde van sy lied sê Dawid: ‘Ek sal vir altyd in die huis van die Here woon.’

verse.text: Die Here is my herder. Ek het alles wat ek nodig het.

lessons: God is soos ’n goeie herder wat vir sy skape sorg.
Selfs op donker plekke is God langs ons.
Ons kan God volg soos skape hulle herder volg.
questions: Hoe sorg ’n herder vir skape? Hoe sorg God vir jou?
Kom ons sê dit op vyf vingers: Die – Here – is – my – herder.
prayer: Liewe Here,
U is my herder.
Lei my, voed my en hou my veilig.
Ek sal U volg. Amen.

mission.text: Oefen om ‘Die Here is my herder’ op jou vyf vingers te sê.

en.title: My Shepherd
story: David looked after his sheep. He loved them.
He gave them green grass to eat. Munch, munch!
He gave them cool water to drink. Slurp!
When it was dark, he kept them safe.
David sang: ‘God is my shepherd. He looks after me!’

verse.text: The Lord is my shepherd.

en.action: Crawl like a little sheep and say ‘Baa!’ Then snuggle up close to your shepherd (that’s Mom!).
lessons: God looks after me, like a shepherd looks after his sheep.
questions: What does a sheep say?
prayer: Thank you, God,
for looking after me. Amen.

af.title: My Herder
story: Dawid het na sy skape gekyk. Hy was lief vir hulle.
Hy het vir hulle groen gras gegee om te eet. Kou, kou!
Hy het vir hulle koel water gegee om te drink. Slurp!
As dit donker was, het hy hulle veilig gehou.
Dawid het gesing: ‘God is my herder. Hy kyk na my!’

verse.text: Die Here is my herder.

af.action: Kruip soos ’n klein skapie en sê ‘Mê!’ Kruip dan styf teen jou herder aan (dis Mamma!).
lessons: God kyk na my, soos ’n herder na sy skape kyk.
questions: Wat sê ’n skaap?
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U na my kyk. Amen.

en.title: The Shepherd Who Walks With Me
story: Long before he became king, David spent his days and nights in the fields near Bethlehem looking after sheep. He knew exactly what sheep need: green pasture to eat, quiet water to drink (sheep are scared of rushing streams), protection from wolves, and someone to lead them, because sheep easily wander off and get lost.
One day David realised something wonderful: ‘That is exactly what God is to me!’ So he wrote a song that people all over the world still pray today: Psalm 23.
‘The Lord is my shepherd; I lack nothing.’ David doesn’t say ‘a shepherd’, but ‘my shepherd’. This is personal. God doesn’t just look after the world in general; He looks after you by name.

‘He makes me lie down in green pastures, He leads me beside quiet waters, He refreshes my soul.’ God gives rest when we are tired, peace when we are anxious, and new strength when we feel empty inside.

‘Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.’ Notice that David doesn’t say God will keep us out of every dark valley. Sometimes hard things happen. But we never walk through them alone. The Shepherd walks right next to us.

Hundreds of years later, Jesus said, ‘I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.’ Jesus is the Shepherd David sang about, and He loved His sheep so much that He died for them. Because of Him, the psalm ends with a promise for every child of God: ‘I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.’

verse.text: The Lord is my shepherd; I lack nothing.

lessons: God cares for me personally, like a shepherd for his own sheep.
Even in dark and hard times, God walks with me.
Jesus is the Good Shepherd who gave His life for His sheep.
questions: What do sheep need from a shepherd?
What is the ‘darkest valley’ in Psalm 23? Does God promise we will never go through one?
Which line of Psalm 23 do you need most this week? Why?
en.listen: Read Psalm 23 slowly, out loud. Stop at the line that stands out to you most. Ask the Good Shepherd: ‘Why did you want me to notice this line?’ Listen quietly.
prayer: Jesus, you are my Good Shepherd.
Lead me this week in…
Thank you that you walk with me, even in dark valleys.

mission.text: Learn Psalm 23:1–3 by heart this week. Say it before you sleep tomorrow.

en.journal: Draw yourself as a sheep in Psalm 23: in a green field, by quiet water, or in a dark valley with the Shepherd beside you. Which picture fits your life right now?

af.title: Die Herder wat saam met My Loop
story: Lank voordat hy koning geword het, het Dawid dag en nag in die veld naby Betlehem na skape gekyk. Hy het presies geweet wat skape nodig het: groen weiding om te eet, stil water om te drink (skape is bang vir water wat vinnig vloei), beskerming teen wolwe, en iemand om hulle te lei, want skape dwaal maklik weg en raak verdwaal.
Eendag het Dawid iets wonderliks besef: ‘Dit is presies wat God vir my is!’ Toe skryf hy ’n lied wat mense oor die hele wêreld vandag nog bid: Psalm 23.
‘Die Here is my herder; ek kort niks nie.’ Dawid sê nie ‘’n herder’ nie, maar ‘my herder’. Dit is persoonlik. God kyk nie net in die algemeen na die wêreld nie; Hy kyk na jou, op jou naam.
‘Hy laat my in groen weivelde lê, Hy lei my na waters waar daar rus is, Hy gee my nuwe krag.’ God gee rus as ons moeg is, vrede as ons bekommerd is, en nuwe krag as ons leeg voel binne-in.

‘Selfs al gaan ek deur die donkerste dal, sal ek nie bang wees nie, want U is by my.’ Let op dat Dawid nie sê God sal ons uit elke donker dal hou nie. Soms gebeur moeilike dinge. Maar ons loop nooit alleen daardeur nie. Die Herder loop reg langs ons.

Honderde jare later het Jesus gesê: ‘Ek is die goeie Herder. Die goeie Herder gee sy lewe vir die skape.’ Jesus is die Herder van wie Dawid gesing het, en Hy was so lief vir sy skape dat Hy vir hulle gesterf het. Danksy Hom eindig die psalm met ’n belofte vir elke kind van God: ‘Ek sal vir altyd in die huis van die Here woon.’

verse.text: Die Here is my herder; ek kort niks nie.

lessons: God sorg persoonlik vir my, soos ’n herder vir sy eie skape.
Selfs in donker en moeilike tye loop God saam met my.
Jesus is die goeie Herder wat sy lewe vir sy skape gegee het.
questions: Wat het skape van ’n herder nodig?
Wat is die ‘donkerste dal’ in Psalm 23? Belowe God dat ons nooit deur een sal gaan nie?
Watter reël van Psalm 23 het jy hierdie week die meeste nodig? Hoekom?
af.listen: Lees Psalm 23 stadig en hardop. Stop by die reël wat die meeste vir jou uitstaan. Vra die goeie Herder: ‘Hoekom wou U hê ek moet hierdie reël raaksien?’ Luister stil.
prayer: Jesus, U is my goeie Herder.
Lei my hierdie week in…
Dankie dat U saam met my loop, selfs in donker dale.

mission.text: Leer hierdie week Psalm 23:1–3 uit jou kop. Sê dit môreaand voor jy gaan slaap.

af.journal: Teken jouself as ’n skaap in Psalm 23: in ’n groen veld, by stil water, of in ’n donker dal met die Herder langs jou. Watter prentjie pas nou by jou lewe?

trait.en: God is my shepherd who takes care of me
trait.af: God is my herder wat vir my sorg

en.title: Fire from Heaven
story: In Elijah’s day, the people had started to pray to a pretend god called Baal. So God’s prophet Elijah held a contest on top of Mount Carmel. ‘Let’s each build an altar,’ he said. ‘The god who answers with fire is the real God!’
The 450 prophets of Baal went first. They shouted and danced from morning till lunchtime: ‘Baal, answer us!’ Nothing. Not one puff of smoke. Elijah teased them: ‘Shout louder! Maybe he’s asleep!’
Then it was Elijah’s turn. He even poured water all over his altar, twelve big jars, until everything was soaking wet! Then Elijah prayed a simple prayer: ‘Lord, show everyone that you are God.’
WHOOSH! Fire fell from heaven and burned up everything, even the water! All the people fell down and cried, ‘The Lord, he is God!’

verse.text: The Lord, he is God!

lessons: There is only one true God, and he is alive.
God hears and answers prayer.
Elijah didn’t need to shout. God heard his simple prayer.
questions: Why couldn’t Baal answer? (He wasn’t real.)
Does God hear us when we pray quietly?
prayer: Dear God,
you are the one true God.
You are alive, and you hear me
when I pray. Amen.

mission.text: Pray a short prayer for someone tomorrow, and watch for what God does.

af.title: Vuur uit die Hemel
story: In Elia se tyd het die mense begin bid tot ’n kamma-god met die naam Baal. Toe hou God se profeet Elia ’n kompetisie bo-op die berg Karmel. ‘Kom ons bou elkeen ’n altaar,’ het hy gesê. ‘Die god wat met vuur antwoord, is die regte God!’

Die 450 profete van Baal het eerste gegaan. Hulle het van die oggend tot middagete geskree en gedans: ‘Baal, antwoord ons!’ Niks. Nie eens ’n rokie nie. Elia het hulle geterg: ‘Skree harder! Dalk slaap hy!’
Toe was dit Elia se beurt. Hy het selfs water oor sy altaar gegooi, twaalf groot kanne, totdat alles papnat was! Toe bid Elia ’n eenvoudige gebed: ‘Here, wys vir almal dat U God is.’
WOESJ! Vuur het uit die hemel geval en alles verbrand, selfs die water! Al die mense het neergeval en uitgeroep: ‘Die Here, Hy is God!’

verse.text: Die Here, Hy is God!

lessons: Daar is net een ware God, en Hy leef.
God hoor en antwoord gebed.
Elia hoef nie te skree nie. God het sy eenvoudige gebed gehoor.
questions: Hoekom kon Baal nie antwoord nie? (Hy was nie regtig nie.)
Hoor God ons as ons stil bid?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is die een ware God.
U leef, en U hoor my
as ek bid. Amen.

mission.text: Bid môre ’n kort gebed vir iemand, en kyk wat God doen.

en.title: Fire from Heaven
story: Some people prayed to a pretend god. He could not hear them!
They shouted and jumped. Nothing happened.
Then Elijah prayed to the real God.
WHOOSH! God sent fire from the sky!
Everybody said, ‘The Lord is God!’ God hears when we pray.

verse.text: The Lord is God!

en.action: Jump and shout like the people, then sit very still and fold your hands to pray like Elijah. Then throw your arms up: WHOOSH!
lessons: God is real, and He hears me when I pray.
questions: Does God hear us when we whisper a prayer?
prayer: Dear God,
you are real, and you hear me. Amen.

af.title: Vuur uit die Hemel
story: Party mense het tot ’n kamma-god gebid. Hy kon hulle nie hoor nie!
Hulle het geskree en gespring. Niks het gebeur nie.
Toe bid Elia tot die regte God.
WOESJ! God het vuur uit die lug gestuur!
Almal het gesê: ‘Die Here is God!’ God hoor as ons bid.

verse.text: Die Here is God!

af.action: Spring en skree soos die mense, sit dan baie stil en vou jou hande om te bid soos Elia. Gooi dan jou arms op: WOESJ!
lessons: God is regtig, en Hy hoor my as ek bid.
questions: Hoor God ons as ons ’n gebed fluister?
prayer: Liewe God,

en.title: The God Who Answers by Fire
story: King Ahab and Queen Jezebel had led Israel into worshipping Baal, a made-up god of rain and storms. As a warning, God’s prophet Elijah had announced that no rain would fall, and for three and a half years the land was dry and hungry. Still the people couldn’t decide whom to follow.

So Elijah called everyone to Mount Carmel. ‘How long will you waver between two opinions? If the Lord is God, follow Him; but if Baal is God, follow him.’ He set up a contest: each side would prepare a sacrifice on an altar, but light no fire. ‘The god who answers by fire, He is God.’

The 450 prophets of Baal went first. From morning until noon they shouted, ‘Baal, answer us!’ They danced around their altar and even cut themselves. Elijah teased them: ‘Shout louder! Maybe he’s asleep, or busy!’ But there was no answer. No one paid attention. Baal wasn’t real.

Then Elijah repaired the broken altar of the Lord. To make the miracle impossible to doubt, he had twelve large jars of water poured over the sacrifice until the wood was soaked and the trench around it was full. Then Elijah prayed a simple prayer: ‘Lord, let it be known today that you are God… Answer me, so these people will know that you are turning their hearts back again.’

Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the soil, and even licked up the water in the trench! The people fell on their faces and cried, ‘The Lord, He is God!’ Soon afterwards, Elijah prayed again, and the rain came.

James 5:16 says that ‘the prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective’, and points to Elijah as an example of an ordinary person who prayed with faith. God doesn’t need us to shout or perform. He is real, He hears, and He answers prayer in His way and His time.

verse.text: The Lord, He is God! The Lord, He is God!

lessons: There is only one true and living God. Idols and made-up gods cannot hear or answer.
God answers prayer: He hears simple prayers made with faith.
God wants hearts that follow Him fully, not ones that waver between two choices.
questions: Why did Elijah pour water over his altar?
What was the difference between how the prophets of Baal prayed and how Elijah prayed?
Is there something you are ‘wavering’ about? What would it look like to follow God fully?
en.listen: Pray a simple, honest prayer about something that matters to you. Then sit quietly and ask: ‘Lord, how do you want to answer this?’ Listen, and remember that God sometimes answers ‘yes’, ‘wait’ or ‘I have something better’.
prayer: Lord, you are the one true God, and you hear me.
Tonight I bring you…
I believe you will answer in your way and your time.

mission.text: Start a prayer list. Write down one thing you are praying for, and check back in a few weeks to see how God answered.

en.journal: Write a short, honest prayer, like Elijah’s, in your journal. Leave space underneath to write how God answers.

af.title: Die God wat met Vuur Antwoord
story: Koning Agab en koningin Isebel het Israel gelei om Baal te aanbid, ’n opgemaakte god van reën en storms. As ’n waarskuwing het God se profeet Elia aangekondig dat daar geen reën sou val nie, en drie en ’n half jaar lank was die land droog en honger. Tog kon die mense nie besluit wie om te volg nie.

Toe roep Elia almal na die berg Karmel. ‘Hoe lank gaan julle nog tussen twee keuses hink? As die Here God is, volg Hom; maar as Baal God is, volg hom.’ Hy het ’n kompetisie gereël: elke kant sou ’n offer op ’n altaar voorberei, maar geen vuur aansteek nie. ‘Die god wat met vuur antwoord, Hy is God.’

Die 450 profete van Baal het eerste gegaan. Van die oggend tot middag het hulle geskree: ‘Baal, antwoord ons!’ Hulle het om hulle altaar gedans en selfs hulleself gesny. Elia het hulle geterg: ‘Skree harder! Dalk slaap hy, of hy is besig!’ Maar daar was geen antwoord nie. Niemand het ag geslaan nie. Baal was nie regtig nie.

Toe het Elia die stukkende altaar van die Here herstel. Om die wonderwerk onmoontlik te maak om aan te twyfel, het hy twaalf groot kanne water oor die offer laat gooi totdat die hout papnat was en die sloot rondom vol was. Toe bid Elia ’n eenvoudige gebed: ‘Here, laat dit vandag bekend word dat U God is… Antwoord my, sodat hierdie mense kan weet dat U hulle harte weer na U toe terugdraai.’

Vuur het uit die hemel geval en die offer, die hout, die klippe, die grond en selfs die water in die sloot verbrand! Die mense het op hulle gesigte geval en uitgeroep: ‘Die Here, Hy is God!’ Kort daarna het Elia weer gebid, en die reën het gekom.

Jakobus 5:16 sê dat ‘die gebed van ’n regverdige mens baie krag het’, en wys na Elia as ’n voorbeeld van ’n gewone mens wat met geloof gebid het. God het nie nodig dat ons skree of ’n vertoning lewer nie. Hy is regtig, Hy hoor, en Hy antwoord gebed op sy manier en op sy tyd.

verse.text: Die Here, Hy is God! Die Here, Hy is God!

lessons: Daar is net een ware en lewende God. Afgode en opgemaakte gode kan nie hoor of antwoord nie.
God antwoord gebed: Hy hoor eenvoudige gebede wat met geloof gebid word.
God wil harte hê wat Hom heeltemal volg, nie harte wat tussen twee keuses hink nie.
questions: Hoekom het Elia water oor sy altaar gegooi?
Wat was die verskil tussen hoe die profete van Baal gebid het en hoe Elia gebid het?
Is daar iets waaroor jy ‘hink’? Hoe sal dit lyk om God heeltemal te volg?
af.listen: Bid ’n eenvoudige, eerlike gebed oor iets wat vir jou saak maak. Sit dan stil en vra: ‘Here, hoe wil U dit antwoord?’ Luister, en onthou dat God soms ‘ja’, ‘wag’ of ‘Ek het iets beters’ antwoord.
prayer: Here, U is die een ware God, en U hoor my.
Vanaand bring ek vir U…
Ek glo U sal op u manier en op u tyd antwoord.

mission.text: Begin ’n gebedslys. Skryf een ding neer waarvoor jy bid, en kyk oor ’n paar weke hoe God geantwoord het.

af.journal: Skryf ’n kort, eerlike gebed soos Elia s’n in jou joernaal. Laat plek daaronder om te skryf hoe God antwoord.

trait.en: There is only one true God, and he hears me

en.title: Daniel and the Lions
story: Daniel loved God and prayed to him three times every day, at his window. Some jealous men tricked the king into making a new law: ‘For thirty days, nobody may pray to anyone except the king. Anyone who does will be thrown to the lions!’

Did Daniel stop praying? No! He went to his window, knelt down and prayed to God, just like always. The jealous men ran to tell the king. The king was very sad, because he liked Daniel, but the law could not be changed. Daniel was thrown into a den of hungry lions, and a big stone was rolled over the opening.
The king couldn’t sleep all night. Early next morning he ran to the den. ‘Daniel! Has your God saved you?’
‘Yes, O king!’ called Daniel. ‘My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths!’ There was not one scratch on him. Then the king told everyone to honour Daniel’s God.

verse.text: My God sent his angel, and his angel shut the mouths of the lions.

lessons: God is with us everywhere, even in a lions’ den.
Talking to God every day was very important to Daniel.
We can keep loving God even when other people don’t.
questions: Why did Daniel keep praying?
When are good times in your day to talk to God?
prayer: Dear God,
you are always with me,
at home, at school, everywhere.
Help me talk to you every day like Daniel. Amen.

mission.text: Pick three times tomorrow to pray, like Daniel: morning, lunchtime and bedtime.

af.title: Daniël en die Leeus
story: Daniël was lief vir God en het elke dag drie keer by sy venster tot Hom gebid. ’n Paar jaloerse mans het die koning laat ’n nuwe wet maak: ‘Vir dertig dae mag niemand tot iemand anders as die koning bid nie. Enigiemand wat dit doen, word vir die leeus gegooi!’

Het Daniël opgehou bid? Nee! Hy het na sy venster gegaan, gekniel en tot God gebid, net soos altyd. Die jaloerse mans het gehardloop om vir die koning te gaan vertel. Die koning was baie hartseer, want hy was lief vir Daniël, maar die wet kon nie verander word nie. Daniël is in ’n kuil vol honger leeus gegooi, en ’n groot klip is oor die opening gerol.
Die koning kon die hele nag nie slaap nie. Vroeg die volgende oggend het hy na die kuil gehardloop. ‘Daniël! Het jou God jou gered?’
‘Ja, o koning!’ roep Daniël. ‘My God het sy engel gestuur en die leeus se bekke toegemaak!’ Daar was nie een krapmerk op hom nie. Toe het die koning vir almal gesê om Daniël se God te eer.

verse.text: My God het sy engel gestuur, en sy engel het die bekke van die leeus toegemaak.

lessons: God is oral by ons, selfs in ’n leeukuil.
Om elke dag met God te praat was vir Daniël baie belangrik.
Ons kan aanhou om God lief te hê, selfs as ander mense dit nie doen nie.
questions: Hoekom het Daniël aangehou bid?
Wanneer in jou dag is goeie tye om met God te praat?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is altyd by my,
by die huis, by die skool, oral.
Help my om elke dag met U te praat soos Daniël. Amen.

mission.text: Kies môre drie tye om te bid, soos Daniël: oggend, middag en slaaptyd.

en.title: Daniel and the Lions
story: Daniel loved God. He prayed every day by his window.
Some men made a bad rule: ‘No praying to God!’
But Daniel still prayed. So they put him with the lions. ROAR!
God sent an angel to shut the lions’ mouths. Snap!
Daniel was safe. God was with him all night!

verse.text: My God shut the lions’ mouths.

en.action: Roar like a big lion. Then snap your hands shut like the lions’ mouths, and fold your hands to pray like Daniel.
lessons: God is always with me, everywhere.
questions: Where can we talk to God? (Everywhere!)
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for being with me. Amen.

af.title: Daniël en die Leeus
story: Daniël was lief vir God. Hy het elke dag by sy venster gebid.
’n Paar mans het ’n slegte reël gemaak: ‘Geen bid tot God nie!’
Maar Daniël het steeds gebid. Toe sit hulle hom by die leeus. BRUL!
God het ’n engel gestuur om die leeus se bekke toe te maak. Klap!
Daniël was veilig. God was die hele nag by hom!

verse.text: My God het die leeus se bekke toegemaak.

af.action: Brul soos ’n groot leeu. Klap dan jou hande toe soos die leeus se bekke, en vou jou hande om te bid soos Daniël.
lessons: God is altyd by my, oral.
questions: Waar kan ons met God praat? (Oral!)
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U by my is. Amen.

en.title: Faithful in the Lions’ Den
story: Daniel had been taken from Jerusalem to Babylon as a teenager. Decades later, now an old man, he was one of the top leaders in the Persian empire under King Darius. Daniel was so honest and hard-working that the king planned to put him in charge of the whole kingdom.

The other officials were jealous. They searched for something wrong in Daniel’s work but couldn’t find a single mistake. So they said, ‘We will never find any basis for charges against Daniel unless it has something to do with the law of his God.’ They knew Daniel prayed to God three times a day.
They tricked King Darius into signing a law: for thirty days, anyone who prayed to any god or man except the king would be thrown into the lions’ den. Once signed, the law could not be changed.

When Daniel heard about the law, he went home, opened the windows of his upstairs room toward Jerusalem, knelt down and prayed, giving thanks to God, ‘just as he had done before’. Daniel’s prayer life wasn’t something he did only in emergencies. It was a daily friendship with God that he wasn’t willing to give up.

The officials caught him and reported him. The king was upset, because he liked Daniel, but he couldn’t change the law. Daniel was thrown into the den, and a stone was rolled over the entrance. The king said, ‘May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you!’

At dawn the king rushed to the den. ‘Daniel, has your God been able to rescue you?’ Daniel answered, ‘My God sent His angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions.’ Not a scratch was found on him, ‘because he had trusted in his God.’ Then King Darius commanded his whole empire to honour the living God.

verse.text: My God sent His angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions.

lessons: God is always with His children, even in the most dangerous places.
A daily friendship with God gives us courage when tests come.
God honours those who stay faithful to Him, and uses their faith to point others to Him.
questions: Why couldn’t the officials find anything wrong with Daniel?
What do you think Daniel prayed about three times a day for all those years?
What would help you build a daily habit of talking with God?
en.listen: Daniel thanked God even when he was in danger. Spend one minute thanking God for things. Then ask: ‘Lord, how can I spend time with you every day?’ Listen for His idea.
prayer: Lord, thank you that you are always with me.
Help me to be faithful to you like Daniel, even when…
I want to talk with you every day.

mission.text: Choose three times tomorrow (like Daniel) to talk to God: when you wake up, at lunch and at bedtime.

en.journal: Draw a window like Daniel’s. Around it, write the three times each day you will talk with God, and what you might thank Him for.

af.title: Getrou in die Leeukuil
story: Daniël is as ’n tiener uit Jerusalem na Babel weggevoer. Baie jare later, nou ’n ou man, was hy een van die hoofleiers in die Persiese ryk onder koning Darius. Daniël was so eerlik en hardwerkend dat die koning beplan het om hom oor die hele koninkryk aan te stel.

Die ander amptenare was jaloers. Hulle het na iets verkeerds in Daniël se werk gesoek, maar kon nie een enkele fout kry nie. Toe sê hulle: ‘Ons sal nooit iets kry om Daniël van te beskuldig nie, tensy dit met die wet van sy God te doen het.’ Hulle het geweet Daniël bid drie keer per dag tot God.

Hulle het koning Darius gekul om ’n wet te teken: vir dertig dae sou enigiemand wat tot enige god of mens behalwe die koning bid, in die leeukuil gegooi word. Sodra dit geteken was, kon die wet nie verander word nie.

Toe Daniël van die wet hoor, het hy huis toe gegaan, die vensters van sy bokamer na Jerusalem oopgemaak, gekniel en gebid, en God gedank, ‘net soos hy altyd gedoen het’. Daniël se gebedslewe was nie iets wat hy net in noodgevalle gedoen het nie. Dit was ’n daaglikse vriendskap met God wat hy nie wou opgee nie.

Die amptenare het hom betrap en hom aangekla. Die koning was ontsteld, want hy was lief vir Daniël, maar hy kon nie die wet verander nie. Daniël is in die kuil gegooi, en ’n klip is oor die ingang gerol. Die koning het gesê: ‘Mag jou God, wat jy altyd dien, jou red!’

Met sonop het die koning na die kuil gehardloop. ‘Daniël, kon jou God jou red?’ Daniël het geantwoord: ‘My God het sy engel gestuur, en hy het die bekke van die leeus toegemaak.’ Daar was nie een krapmerk op hom nie, ‘omdat hy op sy God vertrou het’. Toe het koning Darius sy hele ryk beveel om die lewende God te eer.

verse.text: My God het sy engel gestuur, en hy het die bekke van die leeus toegemaak.

lessons: God is altyd by sy kinders, selfs op die gevaarlikste plekke.
’n Daaglikse vriendskap met God gee ons moed wanneer toetse kom.
God eer die wat aan Hom getrou bly, en gebruik hulle geloof om ander na Hom te wys.
questions: Hoekom kon die amptenare niks verkeerd met Daniël kry nie?
Waaroor dink jy het Daniël al daardie jare drie keer per dag gebid?
Wat sal jou help om ’n daaglikse gewoonte te bou om met God te praat?
af.listen: Daniël het God gedank selfs toe hy in gevaar was. Spandeer een minuut om God vir dinge te dank. Vra dan: ‘Here, hoe kan ek elke dag tyd saam met U spandeer?’ Luister vir sy plan.
prayer: Here, dankie dat U altyd by my is.
Help my om getrou aan U te wees soos Daniël, selfs as…
Ek wil elke dag met U praat.

mission.text: Kies môre drie tye (soos Daniël) om met God te praat: as jy wakker word, middagete en slaaptyd.

af.journal: Teken ’n venster soos Daniël s’n. Skryf rondom dit die drie tye elke dag wanneer jy met God sal praat, en waarvoor jy Hom kan dank.

en.title: Campfire Night: Brave Hearts Mountain
story: You’ve climbed Brave Hearts Mountain! This week a boy learned to hear God’s voice, a shepherd was chosen for his heart, a giant fell, a psalm reminded us that the Good Shepherd walks with us, fire fell from heaven, and lions couldn’t touch a man who prayed. In every story, courage came from the same place: knowing God, talking with Him and trusting Him.
en.game: Courage cards: each of you writes a ‘giant’ (a fear or problem) on a piece of paper. Swap papers, then find a Bible verse from this week that answers the other person’s giant.
questions: Which brave person from this week would you most like to be like? Why?
What did all of them have in common?
What have you learned this week about hearing God’s voice?
prayer: Lord, you speak to me, you see my heart and you make me brave.
This week I want to be brave about…
Thank you that you are always with me.

mission.text: Learn Joshua 1:9 by heart and say it to someone in your family.

en.journal: Look back at your ‘Listening page’. Write down anything you sensed God saying this week, and one way you saw Him make you brave.

story: Jy het Dapperhart-berg geklim! Hierdie week het ’n seun geleer om God se stem te hoor, ’n skaapwagter is gekies vanweë sy hart, ’n reus het geval, ’n psalm het ons herinner dat die goeie Herder saam met ons loop, vuur het uit die hemel geval, en leeus kon nie ’n man aanraak wat gebid het nie. In elke storie het moed van dieselfde plek gekom: om God te ken, met Hom te praat en Hom te vertrou.

questions: Op watter dapper mens van hierdie week wil jy die meeste lyk? Hoekom?
Wat het hulle almal in gemeen gehad?

prayer: Here, U praat met my, U sien my hart en U maak my dapper.

en.title: Jonah and the Giant Fish
story: God told Jonah, ‘Go to the city of Nineveh and tell the people to stop doing bad things.’ But Jonah didn’t want to go. So he jumped on a boat going the opposite way!

Out at sea, God sent a huge storm. The waves crashed and the boat creaked. Jonah knew it was because he had run away from God. ‘Throw me into the sea,’ he told the sailors, ‘and the storm will stop.’ SPLASH! In went Jonah… and GULP! A giant fish swallowed him whole!
For three days and three nights Jonah sat inside the fish’s belly. Yuck! There he prayed, ‘I’m sorry, God. Please help me!’ God heard him. The fish spat Jonah out, BLEURGH, onto the beach.
God gave Jonah a second chance, and this time Jonah went to Nineveh. The people of Nineveh said sorry to God too, and God forgave them. God loves to give second chances.

verse.text: The Lord’s love never runs out. His kindness is new every morning.

lessons: God gives second chances.
You can never run so far that God can’t find you.
God loves all people, even people we find hard to like.
questions: Why did Jonah run away?
Do you need a second chance with someone? Does God give you one?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for second chances.
When I run away from what’s right,
bring me back to you. Amen.

mission.text: Give someone a second chance tomorrow when they make a mistake.

en.title: Jonah and the Big Fish
story: God said, ‘Jonah, go to the big city.’ But Jonah ran away on a boat!
A big storm came. Splash, crash went the waves!
Jonah fell into the sea, and a big fish swallowed him. Gulp!
Inside the fish Jonah prayed, ‘Sorry, God!’
The fish spat him out on the beach. God gave Jonah another chance!

verse.text: God’s love never runs out.

en.action: Rock from side to side like a boat in a storm. Then open your arms wide and GULP like a big fish!
lessons: When I say sorry, God gives me another chance.
questions: What sound does a big fish make? Gulp!
prayer: Thank you, God,
for loving me when I say sorry. Amen.

af.title: Jona en die Groot Vis
story: God het gesê: ‘Jona, gaan na die groot stad.’ Maar Jona het op ’n boot weggehardloop!
’n Groot storm het gekom. Plons, kraak het die golwe gegaan!
Jona het in die see geval, en ’n groot vis het hom ingesluk. Sluk!
Binne-in die vis het Jona gebid: ‘Jammer, God!’
Die vis het hom op die strand uitgespoeg. God het vir Jona nog ’n kans gegee!

verse.text: God se liefde raak nooit op nie.

af.action: Wieg heen en weer soos ’n boot in ’n storm. Maak dan jou arms wyd oop en SLUK soos ’n groot vis!

questions: Watter geluid maak ’n groot vis? Sluk!
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U my liefhet as ek jammer sê. Amen.

en.title: Running from God, Caught by Grace
story: God gave the prophet Jonah a clear instruction: ‘Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before me.’ Nineveh was the capital of Assyria, Israel’s cruel enemy. Jonah didn’t want those people to have any chance of forgiveness. So he did the opposite: he went down to the port and bought a ticket on a ship sailing as far away as possible.

But you can’t outrun God. He sent a violent storm. The sailors were terrified and threw cargo overboard, while Jonah slept below deck. When they discovered he was running from God, Jonah told them, ‘Throw me into the sea, and it will become calm.’ They did, and the storm stopped immediately.

Then ‘the Lord provided a huge fish to swallow Jonah’. Notice the word ‘provided’. The fish wasn’t a punishment; it was God’s rescue! For three days and nights Jonah sat in the dark, and there he finally prayed: ‘In my distress I called to the Lord, and He answered me.’ The fish spat Jonah out onto dry land.

Then the word of the Lord came to Jonah ‘a second time’. God gave him a second chance. This time Jonah went to Nineveh. He preached, and the whole city, from the king down, turned from their evil ways and asked God for mercy. And God forgave them.

You might think Jonah would be thrilled, but he was furious! He said to God, ‘I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in love.’ Jonah was angry because God was kind to people Jonah didn’t like.

The book ends with God asking Jonah a question: shouldn’t I care about all these people? God’s mercy is bigger than our likes and dislikes. He gives second chances to runaway prophets and to cruel cities, and He gives them to us, through Jesus.

verse.text: Because of the Lord’s great love we are not consumed, for His compassions never fail. They are new every morning.

lessons: God is merciful: He gives second chances to people who turn back to Him.
We can never run so far that God cannot reach us.
God’s mercy is for everyone, even people we find hard to love.
questions: Why didn’t Jonah want to go to Nineveh?
How was the big fish actually a rescue?
Is there someone you don’t want God to be kind to? What would God say to you about them?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Is there anywhere I am running from you?’ Listen. If something comes to mind, turn back to Him. Then listen again for His kind words to you.
prayer: God, thank you for second chances.
I’m sorry for running from you when…
Help me to want your mercy for everyone, even…

mission.text: Tomorrow, give someone a second chance: forgive them quickly, or include someone you usually avoid.

en.journal: Write about a time you got a second chance. How did it feel? Then write a short prayer for someone who needs a second chance.

af.title: Weghardloop van God, Gevang deur Genade
story: God het die profeet Jona ’n duidelike opdrag gegee: ‘Gaan na die groot stad Nineve en preek teen hom, want sy slegtheid het voor My gekom.’ Nineve was die hoofstad van Assirië, Israel se wrede vyand. Jona wou nie hê daardie mense moet enige kans op vergifnis kry nie. Toe doen hy die teenoorgestelde: hy gaan na die hawe en koop ’n kaartjie op ’n skip wat so ver as moontlik vaar.

Maar jy kan nie van God af weghardloop nie. Hy het ’n wilde storm gestuur. Die matrose was doodbang en het vrag oorboord gegooi, terwyl Jona onder op die skip geslaap het. Toe hulle uitvind hy hardloop van God af weg, het Jona vir hulle gesê: ‘Gooi my in die see, dan sal dit kalm word.’ Hulle het, en die storm het dadelik opgehou.

Toe het ‘die Here ’n groot vis gestuur om Jona in te sluk’. Die vis was nie ’n straf nie; dit was God se redding! Drie dae en nagte lank het Jona in die donker gesit, en daar het hy eindelik gebid: ‘In my nood het ek na die Here geroep, en Hy het my geantwoord.’ Die vis het Jona op droë grond uitgespoeg.

Toe het die woord van die Here ‘vir die tweede keer’ na Jona gekom. God het hom ’n tweede kans gegee. Hierdie keer het Jona na Nineve gegaan. Hy het gepreek, en die hele stad, van die koning af tot almal, het van hulle slegte paaie omgedraai en God om genade gevra. En God het hulle vergewe.

Jy sou dink Jona sou baie bly wees, maar hy was woedend! Hy het vir God gesê: ‘Ek het geweet U is ’n God wat genadig en barmhartig is, wat nie gou kwaad word nie en vol liefde is.’ Jona was kwaad omdat God goed was vir mense van wie Jona nie gehou het nie.

Die boek eindig met ’n vraag van God aan Jona: moet Ek nie omgee vir al hierdie mense nie? God se genade is groter as wie ons van hou en nie van hou nie. Hy gee tweede kanse aan profete wat weghardloop en aan wrede stede, en Hy gee dit aan ons, deur Jesus.

verse.text: Die Here se liefde raak nooit op nie; sy goedheid is elke oggend nuut.

lessons: God is genadig: Hy gee tweede kanse aan mense wat na Hom terugdraai.
Ons kan nooit so ver weghardloop dat God ons nie kan bereik nie.
God se genade is vir almal, selfs vir mense vir wie ons moeilik kan liefhê.
questions: Hoekom wou Jona nie na Nineve gaan nie?
Hoe was die groot vis eintlik ’n redding?
Is daar iemand vir wie jy nie wil hê God goed moet wees nie? Wat sou God vir jou oor hulle sê?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Is daar iets waarvoor ek van U af weghardloop?’ Luister. As iets opkom, draai terug na Hom. Luister dan weer na sy liefdevolle woorde vir jou.
prayer: God, dankie vir tweede kanse.
Ek is jammer dat ek van U af weggehardloop het toe…
Help my om u genade vir almal te wil hê, selfs vir…

mission.text: Gee môre vir iemand ’n tweede kans: vergewe hulle vinnig, of sluit iemand in wat jy gewoonlik vermy.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n keer toe jy ’n tweede kans gekry het. Hoe het dit gevoel? Skryf dan ’n kort gebed vir iemand wat ’n tweede kans nodig het.

en.title: Three Friends in the Fire
story: King Nebuchadnezzar (try saying that fast!) built a giant golden statue, as tall as a big tree. ‘When the music plays, everyone must bow down to my statue,’ he ordered. ‘Whoever doesn’t will be thrown into a blazing furnace!’

The music played. Everyone bowed… except three young men: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. ‘We will only worship the true God,’ they said. ‘Our God can save us. And even if he doesn’t, we still won’t bow.’

The king was furious. ‘Make the fire seven times hotter!’ The three friends were tied up and thrown in. But then the king jumped up. ‘Wait! I see FOUR men walking around in the fire, and they’re not tied up!’
God was in the fire with them! They came out without even smelling of smoke. The king said, ‘No other god can save like this!’

verse.text: The Lord is the great King over all the earth.

lessons: God is the true King, greater than any king.
Only God deserves our worship. He is the most important.
God is with us in the hottest, hardest moments.
questions: What things can become more important to us than God? (Toys? Screens?)
What made the three friends so brave?
prayer: Dear God,
you are the King of everything.
You are the most important
in my life. Amen.

mission.text: Before playing tomorrow, say, ‘God, you are number one!’

af.title: Drie Vriende in die Vuur
story: Koning Nebukadnesar (probeer dit vinnig sê!) het ’n reuse goue beeld gebou, so hoog soos ’n groot boom. ‘As die musiek speel, moet almal voor my beeld buig,’ het hy beveel. ‘Wie dit nie doen nie, word in ’n brandende oond gegooi!’

Die musiek het gespeel. Almal het gebuig… behalwe drie jong mans: Sadrag, Mesag en Abednego. ‘Ons aanbid net die ware God,’ het hulle gesê. ‘Ons God kan ons red. En selfs as Hy dit nie doen nie, sal ons steeds nie buig nie.’

Die koning was woedend. ‘Maak die vuur sewe keer warmer!’ Die drie vriende is vasgebind en ingegooi. Maar toe spring die koning op. ‘Wag! Ek sien VIER mans wat in die vuur rondloop, en hulle is nie vasgebind nie!’
God was saam met hulle in die vuur! Hulle het uitgekom sonder om eens na rook te ruik. Die koning het gesê: ‘Geen ander god kan so red nie!’

verse.text: Die Here is die groot Koning oor die hele aarde.

lessons: God is die ware Koning, groter as enige koning.
Net God verdien ons aanbidding. Hy is die belangrikste.
God is by ons in die warmste, moeilikste oomblikke.
questions: Watter dinge kan vir ons belangriker as God word? (Speelgoed? Skerms?)
Wat het die drie vriende so dapper gemaak?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is die Koning van alles.
U is die belangrikste
in my lewe. Amen.

mission.text: Sê môre voor jy speel: ‘God, U is nommer een!’

en.title: Three Friends and the Fire
story: A king made a big gold statue. ‘Everybody bow down!’ he said.
But three friends said, ‘We only bow to God!’
The king was very cross. He put them in a hot, hot fire!
But look! God was in the fire with them!
They came out safe. Not even their hair was burnt!

verse.text: God is the King of everything.

en.action: Stand up straight and tall like the three friends: ‘We only bow to God!’ Then wiggle your fingers like flickering flames.
lessons: God is the biggest King. I love Him most.
questions: Can you stand up tall and strong?
prayer: Dear God,
you are my King. Amen.

af.title: Drie Vriende en die Vuur
story: ’n Koning het ’n groot goue beeld gemaak. ‘Almal moet buig!’ het hy gesê.
Maar drie vriende het gesê: ‘Ons buig net voor God!’
Die koning was baie kwaad. Hy het hulle in ’n warm, warm vuur gegooi!
Maar kyk! God was saam met hulle in die vuur!
Hulle het veilig uitgekom. Nie eens hulle hare was verbrand nie!

verse.text: God is die Koning van alles.

af.action: Staan regop en lank soos die drie vriende: ‘Ons buig net voor God!’ Wikkel dan jou vingers soos vlammetjies.
lessons: God is die grootste Koning. Ek is die liefste vir Hom.
questions: Kan jy regop en sterk staan?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is my Koning. Amen.

en.title: Even If He Does Not
story: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon built a golden statue about twenty-seven metres tall and gathered all his officials. A herald announced: when the music plays, everyone must fall down and worship the statue. Anyone who refused would be thrown into a blazing furnace.

The music played, and thousands of people bowed. Three young Jewish men stayed standing: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. They had been taken from Jerusalem and trained to serve the king, and they served him well. But they would not worship anyone except the true God.

Furious, the king gave them one more chance, and then sneered, ‘What god will be able to rescue you from my hand?’ Their answer is one of the bravest in the Bible: ‘The God we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace, and He will deliver us from Your Majesty’s hand. But even if He does not, we want you to know that we will not serve your gods.’
Notice their faith. They believed God could save them. They also trusted Him enough to stay faithful even if He chose not to. Their faith wasn’t in a particular result; it was in God Himself.

The king ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter. The heat was so fierce that it killed the soldiers who threw the three men in. Then the king leapt to his feet: ‘Weren’t there three men we tied up? Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods!’

God was in the fire with them. When they came out, not a hair was singed, and they didn’t even smell of smoke. Nebuchadnezzar praised their God, ‘for no other god can save in this way’. God doesn’t always keep us out of the fire, but He promises to be with us in it.

verse.text: For the Lord Most High is awesome, the great King over all the earth.

lessons: God alone is King, and He alone deserves our worship.
True faith trusts God Himself, not only the result we hope for.
God is with His children in the fire: we never face trouble alone.
questions: What did the three friends say they would do ‘even if’ God didn’t rescue them?
Who was the fourth man in the fire?
What ‘statues’ do people bow to today (things they make more important than God)?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Is there anything I have made more important than you?’ Listen honestly. Then tell God He is your King.
prayer: God, you are the great King over everything.
Help me to put you first, above…
Thank you that you are with me in hard times.

mission.text: Tomorrow, before you play or watch anything, spend a few minutes with God first, to show Him He comes first.

en.journal: Write the words ‘Even if He does not…’ and finish the sentence in your own words, as a prayer of trust.

af.title: Selfs as Hy Nie Doen Nie
story: Koning Nebukadnesar van Babel het ’n goue beeld van omtrent sewe-en-twintig meter hoog gebou en al sy amptenare bymekaargeroep. ’n Omroeper het aangekondig: as die musiek speel, moet almal neerval en die beeld aanbid. Enigiemand wat weier, sou in ’n brandende oond gegooi word.

Die musiek het gespeel, en duisende mense het gebuig. Drie jong Joodse mans het bly staan: Sadrag, Mesag en Abednego. Hulle is uit Jerusalem weggevoer en opgelei om die koning te dien, en hulle het hom goed gedien. Maar hulle sou niemand behalwe die ware God aanbid nie.

Woedend het die koning hulle nog een kans gegee, en toe gespot: ‘Watter god sal julle uit my hand kan red?’ Hulle antwoord is een van die dapperste in die Bybel: ‘Die God wat ons dien, kan ons uit die oond red, en Hy sal ons uit u hand red, o koning. Maar selfs as Hy dit nie doen nie, moet u weet dat ons nie u gode sal dien nie.’

Kyk na hulle geloof. Hulle het geglo God kán hulle red. Hulle het Hom ook genoeg vertrou om getrou te bly, selfs as Hy kies om dit nie te doen nie. Hulle geloof was nie in ’n sekere uitkoms nie; dit was in God self.

Die koning het beveel dat die oond sewe keer warmer gemaak word. Die hitte was so erg dat dit die soldate doodgemaak het wat die drie mans ingegooi het. Toe spring die koning op: ‘Het ons nie drie mans vasgebind nie? Kyk! Ek sien vier mans wat in die vuur rondloop, los en ongedeerd, en die vierde lyk soos ’n seun van die gode!’

God was saam met hulle in die vuur. Toe hulle uitkom, was nie een haar geskroei nie, en hulle het nie eens na rook geruik nie. Nebukadnesar het hulle God geprys, ‘want geen ander god kan so red nie’. God hou ons nie altyd uit die vuur nie, maar Hy belowe om saam met ons daarin te wees.

verse.text: Want die Here, die Allerhoogste, is ontsagwekkend, die groot Koning oor die hele aarde.

lessons: God alleen is Koning, en Hy alleen verdien ons aanbidding.
Ware geloof vertrou God self, nie net die uitkoms waarop ons hoop nie.
God is saam met sy kinders in die vuur: ons staan nooit alleen voor moeilikheid nie.
questions: Wat het die drie vriende gesê sal hulle doen ‘selfs as’ God hulle nie red nie?
Wie was die vierde man in die vuur?
Watter ‘beelde’ buig mense vandag voor (dinge wat hulle belangriker as God maak)?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Is daar iets wat ek belangriker as U gemaak het?’ Luister eerlik. Sê dan vir God Hy is jou Koning.
prayer: God, U is die groot Koning oor alles.
Help my om U eerste te stel, bo…
Dankie dat U by my is in moeilike tye.

mission.text: Spandeer môre, voordat jy speel of iets kyk, eers ’n paar minute saam met God, om vir Hom te wys Hy kom eerste.

af.journal: Skryf die woorde ‘Selfs as Hy nie…’ en maak die sin in jou eie woorde klaar, as ’n gebed van vertroue.

trait.en: God is the King over everything
trait.af: God is die Koning oor alles

en.title: The Brave Queen
story: Esther was a Jewish girl who became queen of Persia. But a wicked man named Haman tricked the king into making a law to destroy all of God’s people, the Jews. Esther’s people were in big danger!

Her cousin Mordecai said, ‘Esther, maybe God made you queen for such a time as this!’ But there was a problem. Nobody was allowed to see the king without being invited, not even the queen. If he didn’t hold out his golden sceptre, she could be killed.

Esther asked all God’s people to pray for three days. Then, bravely, she walked into the throne room. The king looked up… and held out his golden sceptre! Esther told him about Haman’s wicked plan. The king was angry with Haman, and God’s people were saved.
God’s name isn’t even written in the book of Esther, but God was working behind the scenes the whole time.

verse.text: ‘I know the plans I have for you,’ says the Lord. ‘Plans to give you hope.’

lessons: God has a good plan, even when we can’t see him working.
God puts us where we are for a reason.
Praying before doing brave things helps.
questions: Why did Esther ask people to pray first?
Where has God put you? (Your family, your school.) How can you help there?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for your good plans for me.
Help me be brave like Esther
wherever you put me. Amen.

mission.text: Ask Mom to pray with you before something hard tomorrow.

af.title: Die Dapper Koningin
story: Ester was ’n Joodse meisie wat koningin van Persië geword het. Maar ’n slegte man met die naam Haman het die koning gekul om ’n wet te maak om al God se mense, die Jode, uit te wis. Ester se mense was in groot gevaar!

Haar neef Mordegai het gesê: ‘Ester, dalk het God jou koningin gemaak juis vir ’n tyd soos hierdie!’ Maar daar was ’n probleem. Niemand mag die koning sien sonder ’n uitnodiging nie, selfs nie die koningin nie. As hy nie sy goue septer uithou nie, kon sy doodgemaak word.

Ester het al God se mense gevra om drie dae lank te bid. Toe, baie dapper, het sy die troonsaal binnegestap. Die koning het opgekyk… en sy goue septer uitgehou! Ester het hom van Haman se slegte plan vertel. Die koning was kwaad vir Haman, en God se mense is gered.
God se naam word nie eens in die boek Ester geskryf nie, maar God was die hele tyd agter die skerms aan die werk.

verse.text: ‘Ek weet watter planne Ek vir jou het,’ sê die Here. ‘Planne om jou hoop te gee.’

lessons: God het ’n goeie plan, selfs as ons Hom nie sien werk nie.
God sit ons met ’n rede waar ons is.
Om te bid voordat ons dapper dinge doen, help.
questions: Hoekom het Ester mense gevra om eers te bid?
Waar het God jou gesit? (Jou familie, jou skool.) Hoe kan jy daar help?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir u goeie planne vir my.
Help my om dapper te wees soos Ester,
oral waar U my sit. Amen.

mission.text: Vra Mamma om môre saam met jou te bid voor iets moeiliks.

af.deeper: Ester was bang, maar sy het tog gegaan. Kan jy bang en dapper wees op dieselfde tyd?
af.journal: Skryf: ‘Dalk het God my hier gesit vir ’n tyd soos hierdie.’ Maak dan ’n lys van die plekke waar God jou gesit het.

en.title: Brave Queen Esther
story: Esther was a beautiful queen.
A bad man wanted to hurt God’s people. Oh no!
Esther was scared. But she prayed, and her friends prayed too.
Then she bravely went to the king. The king smiled and held out his gold stick!
Esther saved God’s people. God had a plan all along!

verse.text: God has good plans for me.

en.action: Put on a pretend crown and walk like a queen or king. Then hold out a pretend gold stick and smile!
lessons: God has a good plan for me.
questions: Can you walk like a queen or a king?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for your good plans. Amen.

af.title: Dapper Koningin Ester
story: Ester was ’n pragtige koningin.
’n Slegte man wou God se mense seermaak. O nee!
Ester was bang. Maar sy het gebid, en haar vriende het ook gebid.
Toe het sy dapper na die koning gegaan. Die koning het geglimlag en sy goue stok uitgehou!
Ester het God se mense gered. God het heeltyd ’n plan gehad!

verse.text: God het goeie planne vir my.

af.action: Sit ’n kamma-kroon op en loop soos ’n koningin of koning. Hou dan ’n kamma-goue stok uit en glimlag!
lessons: God het ’n goeie plan vir my.
questions: Kan jy loop soos ’n koningin of ’n koning?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir u goeie planne. Amen.

en.title: For Such a Time as This
story: Esther was a Jewish orphan living in Persia, raised by her older cousin Mordecai. When King Xerxes searched his empire for a new queen, Esther was chosen. On Mordecai’s advice, she didn’t tell anyone she was Jewish.

Meanwhile, a proud official named Haman hated Mordecai because he wouldn’t bow to him. When Haman discovered Mordecai was a Jew, he decided to destroy every Jew in the empire. He tricked the king into signing a law that, on a set day, all the Jews could be killed.

Mordecai sent a message to Esther: she must go to the king and plead for her people. But there was a problem. Anyone who went to the king without being invited could be put to death, unless the king held out his golden sceptre. Esther hadn’t been called for a whole month.

Mordecai replied with famous words: ‘Who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?’ Esther made her decision: ‘Go, gather all the Jews, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days. I and my attendants will fast as you do. Then I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish.’

After three days Esther went to the king. He held out the sceptre! Over two banquets she revealed Haman’s evil plan, and the king turned against Haman. A new law allowed the Jews to defend themselves, and God’s people were saved. Jewish families still celebrate it today at the festival of Purim.

Here is something surprising: God’s name is never mentioned in the book of Esther. Yet He was working through every detail: an orphan becoming queen, a sleepless night for the king, perfect timing. God placed Esther exactly where she needed to be. He places you where you are for a reason too.

verse.text: ‘I know the plans I have for you,’ declares the Lord, ‘plans to give you hope and a future.’

lessons: God has a good plan, even when we can’t see Him working.
God places His children where they are for a reason.
Courage often begins with prayer, and with asking others to pray with us.
questions: Why was it dangerous for Esther to go to the king?
What did Esther do before she went? Why do you think that mattered?
Where has God placed you (your family, school, friends)? How could you be brave there ‘for such a time as this’?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Why have you placed me where I am?’ Listen. Maybe God will remind you of someone at school or in your family who needs you.
prayer: God, thank you that you have a good plan for my life.
Give me courage to…
Use me where you have placed me.

mission.text: Before something hard tomorrow, ask a parent or friend to pray with you, like Esther did.

en.journal: Write ‘For such a time as this’ at the top of a page. Underneath, list the places and people God has put in your life, and one way you can help each one.

af.title: Vir ’n Tyd soos Hierdie
story: Ester was ’n Joodse weeskind wat in Persië gewoon het, grootgemaak deur haar ouer neef Mordegai. Toe koning Xerxes deur sy ryk na ’n nuwe koningin gesoek het, is Ester gekies. Op Mordegai se raad het sy vir niemand gesê dat sy ’n Jood is nie.

Intussen het ’n trotse amptenaar met die naam Haman Mordegai gehaat omdat hy nie voor hom wou buig nie. Toe Haman uitvind Mordegai is ’n Jood, het hy besluit om elke Jood in die ryk uit te wis. Hy het die koning gekul om ’n wet te teken dat al die Jode op ’n sekere dag doodgemaak kon word.

Mordegai het vir Ester ’n boodskap gestuur: sy moet na die koning gaan en vir haar volk pleit. Maar daar was ’n probleem. Enigiemand wat sonder ’n uitnodiging na die koning gegaan het, kon doodgemaak word, tensy die koning sy goue septer uithou. Ester is al ’n hele maand lank nie geroep nie.

Mordegai het met bekende woorde geantwoord: ‘Wie weet of jy nie juis vir ’n tyd soos hierdie koningin geword het nie?’ Ester het haar besluit geneem: ‘Gaan maak al die Jode bymekaar, en vas vir my. Moenie drie dae lank eet of drink nie. Ek en my diensmeisies sal ook so vas. Dan sal ek na die koning gaan, al is dit teen die wet. En as ek moet sterf, dan sterf ek.’

Ná drie dae het Ester na die koning gegaan. Hy het die septer uitgehou! By twee feesmaaltye het sy Haman se slegte plan bekend gemaak, en die koning het teen Haman gedraai. ’n Nuwe wet het die Jode toegelaat om hulleself te verdedig, en God se mense is gered. Joodse families vier dit vandag nog by die fees van Purim.

Hier is iets verrassends: God se naam word nooit in die boek Ester genoem nie. Tog was Hy in elke detail aan die werk: ’n weeskind wat koningin word, ’n slapelose nag vir die koning, presiese tydsberekening. God het Ester presies op die regte plek gesit. Hy het jou ook met ’n rede gesit waar jy is.

verse.text: ‘Ek weet watter planne Ek vir jou het,’ sê die Here, ‘planne om jou hoop en ’n toekoms te gee.’

lessons: God het ’n goeie plan, selfs as ons Hom nie sien werk nie.
God sit sy kinders met ’n rede waar hulle is.
Moed begin dikwels met gebed, en met om ander te vra om saam met ons te bid.
questions: Hoekom was dit gevaarlik vir Ester om na die koning te gaan?
Wat het Ester gedoen voordat sy gegaan het? Hoekom dink jy was dit belangrik?
Waar het God jou gesit (jou familie, skool, maats)? Hoe kan jy daar dapper wees ‘vir ’n tyd soos hierdie’?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Hoekom het U my gesit waar ek is?’ Luister. Dalk sal God jou herinner aan iemand by die skool of in jou familie wat jou nodig het.
prayer: God, dankie dat U ’n goeie plan vir my lewe het.
Gee my moed om…
Gebruik my waar U my gesit het.

mission.text: Vra môre, voor iets moeiliks, vir ’n ouer of ’n maat om saam met jou te bid, soos Ester gedoen het.

af.journal: Skryf ‘Vir ’n tyd soos hierdie’ bo-aan ’n bladsy. Skryf daaronder die plekke en mense wat God in jou lewe gesit het, en een manier hoe jy elkeen kan help.

trait.en: God has a good plan, even when I can't see it
trait.af: God het ’n goeie plan, selfs as ek dit nie kan sien nie

en.title: Ruth's Kind Heart
story: Naomi was very sad. She had moved far away, and both her husband and her sons had died. ‘I’m going home to Bethlehem,’ she told her daughter-in-law, Ruth. ‘Go back to your own family.’
But Ruth hugged her tight. ‘Where you go, I will go. Your God will be my God.’ So Ruth went with Naomi all the way to Bethlehem.

They had no food, so Ruth went to the fields to pick up the leftover grain behind the harvesters. The field belonged to a kind man named Boaz. ‘Let her pick as much as she wants,’ Boaz told his workers, ‘and drop some extra on purpose for her!’
Later Boaz married Ruth, and they had a baby boy. Naomi was happy again! And guess what? Ruth became the great-grandmother of King David. Many years later, Jesus was born into her family!

verse.text: The Lord is good to everyone. He is kind to all he has made.

lessons: God cares for lonely and sad people.
God often shows his kindness through kind people.
God can bring happiness after sadness.
questions: How did Boaz show God’s kindness?
Who might be lonely that we could be kind to?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for being so kind to me.
Help me be kind like Ruth and Boaz
to people who are sad. Amen.

mission.text: Make a drawing or a card for someone who might be lonely.

af.title: Rut se Gawe Hart
story: Naomi was baie hartseer. Sy het ver weg getrek, en haar man en haar seuns was dood. ‘Ek gaan terug huis toe na Betlehem,’ het sy vir haar skoondogter, Rut, gesê. ‘Gaan terug na jou eie familie.’
Maar Rut het haar styf vasgedruk. ‘Waar jy gaan, sal ek gaan. Jou God sal my God wees.’ Toe het Rut saam met Naomi die hele pad na Betlehem gegaan.

Hulle het geen kos gehad nie, toe gaan Rut na die lande om die oorskietkoring agter die oesters op te tel. Die land het behoort aan ’n vriendelike man met die naam Boas. ‘Laat haar soveel optel as wat sy wil,’ het Boas vir sy werkers gesê, ‘en laat ekstra val, met opset, vir haar!’

Later het Boas met Rut getrou, en hulle het ’n babaseuntjie gekry. Naomi was weer gelukkig! En raai wat? Rut het die oumagrootjie van koning Dawid geword. Baie jare later is Jesus in haar familie gebore!

verse.text: Die Here is goed vir almal. Hy is vriendelik met alles wat Hy gemaak het.

lessons: God gee om vir eensame en hartseer mense.
God wys dikwels sy goedheid deur gawe mense.
God kan blydskap ná hartseer bring.
questions: Hoe het Boas God se goedheid gewys?
Wie is dalk eensaam met wie ons gaaf kan wees?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U so goed is vir my.
Help my om gaaf te wees soos Rut en Boas
met mense wat hartseer is. Amen.

mission.text: Maak ’n tekening of kaartjie vir iemand wat dalk eensaam is.
