af.fact: Rut het van Moab gekom, ’n land wat dikwels Israel se vyand was. Tog het God haar in sy familie verwelkom!
af.deeper: Rut het by Naomi gebly toe dit makliker sou wees om weg te gaan. Wat beteken dit om ’n getroue vriend te wees?
af.journal: Skryf die naam neer van iemand wat dalk eensaam is, en een gawe ding wat jy vir hulle kan doen.

en.title: Ruth Stays Close
story: Naomi was very sad and lonely.
Ruth gave her a big hug. ‘I will stay with you!’
They walked a long way to Bethlehem.
Kind Boaz let Ruth pick up wheat in his field. ‘Take as much as you like!’
God was kind to Ruth and Naomi. They were happy again!

verse.text: God is kind to everyone.

en.action: Give someone a big hug, like Ruth. Then pretend to pick up wheat and put it in your arms.
lessons: God is kind, and He helps me to be kind.
questions: Who can you give a hug to?
prayer: Dear God,
help me to be kind like you. Amen.

af.title: Rut Bly Naby
story: Naomi was baie hartseer en alleen.
Rut het haar styf vasgedruk. ‘Ek sal by jou bly!’
Hulle het ’n lang pad na Betlehem geloop.
Vriendelike Boas het vir Rut koring op sy land laat optel. ‘Vat soveel as wat jy wil!’
God was goed vir Rut en Naomi. Hulle was weer gelukkig!

verse.text: God is goed vir almal.

af.action: Druk iemand styf vas, soos Rut. Maak dan of jy koring optel en dit in jou arms hou.
lessons: God is goed, en Hy help my om gaaf te wees.
questions: Vir wie kan jy ’n drukkie gee?
prayer: Liewe God,
help my om gaaf te wees soos U. Amen.

en.title: Where You Go, I Will Go
story: During a famine, an Israelite woman named Naomi moved with her husband and two sons to the country of Moab. Her sons married Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth. Then tragedy struck: Naomi’s husband and both her sons died. Naomi was left with nothing but sadness. She even said, ‘Don’t call me Naomi [which means ‘pleasant’]. Call me Mara [which means ‘bitter’].’

Naomi decided to go home to Bethlehem, and told her daughters-in-law to go back to their own families. Orpah tearfully said goodbye. But Ruth clung to Naomi and made one of the most beautiful promises in the Bible: ‘Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people and your God my God.’ Ruth, a foreigner, chose to belong to the God of Israel.

In Bethlehem, the two widows had no food. Ruth went to gather leftover grain behind the harvesters, which was something God’s law allowed poor people to do. She happened to choose a field owned by Boaz, a relative of Naomi’s husband. Boaz noticed her and was kind. ‘May the Lord repay you for what you have done,’ he said. ‘May you be richly rewarded by the Lord, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.’ He quietly told his workers to drop extra grain for her.
Boaz was a ‘kinsman-redeemer’, a relative with the right to rescue a family in trouble. He married Ruth and took care of Naomi too. They had a son named Obed, and Naomi held her grandson with joy.

The story ends with a surprise: Obed became the grandfather of King David. Many generations later, Jesus was born from this family line. God welcomed a foreigner from an enemy country into His family and wove her into the story of Jesus. And Jesus is our Redeemer, the One who rescues us and brings us into God’s family.

verse.text: The Lord is good to all; He has compassion on all He has made.

lessons: God cares for people who are lonely, grieving and in need.
God often shows His kindness through the kindness of people.
God welcomes everyone into His family, and Jesus is our Redeemer.
questions: What did Ruth promise Naomi?
How did Boaz show God’s kindness?
Who around you is lonely or going through a sad time? How could you be like Ruth or Boaz to them?
en.listen: Be still and ask God: ‘Who do you want me to be kind to this week?’ Listen. Write down the name that comes to mind.
prayer: God, thank you that you are kind and you care for lonely people.
Please comfort…
Help me to show your kindness like Ruth and Boaz did.

mission.text: Do something kind tomorrow for someone who is sad or lonely: a note, a drawing, or just sitting with them.

en.journal: Write Ruth’s promise (‘Where you go I will go…’) and then write your own promise to God in your own words.

af.title: Waar Jy Gaan, Sal Ek Gaan
story: Tydens ’n hongersnood het ’n Israelitiese vrou met die naam Naomi saam met haar man en twee seuns na die land Moab getrek. Haar seuns het met Moabitiese vroue getrou, Orpa en Rut. Toe tref ’n ramp hulle: Naomi se man en albei haar seuns het gesterf. Naomi het met niks behalwe hartseer agtergebly nie. Sy het selfs gesê: ‘Moenie my Naomi noem nie [dit beteken ‘lieflik’]. Noem my Mara [dit beteken ‘bitter’].’

Naomi het besluit om terug huis toe te gaan na Betlehem, en het vir haar skoondogters gesê om na hulle eie families terug te gaan. Orpa het huilend totsiens gesê. Maar Rut het aan Naomi vasgeklou en een van die mooiste beloftes in die Bybel gemaak: ‘Waar jy gaan, sal ek gaan, en waar jy bly, sal ek bly. Jou volk sal my volk wees en jou God my God.’ Rut, ’n vreemdeling, het gekies om aan die God van Israel te behoort.

In Betlehem het die twee weduwees geen kos gehad nie. Rut het oorskietkoring agter die oesters gaan optel, iets wat God se wet aan arm mense toegelaat het. Sy het toevallig ’n land gekies wat aan Boas behoort het, ’n familielid van Naomi se man. Boas het haar raakgesien en was vriendelik. ‘Mag die Here jou beloon vir wat jy gedoen het,’ het hy gesê. ‘Mag die Here jou ryklik beloon, onder wie se vlerke jy kom skuil het.’ Hy het stilletjies vir sy werkers gesê om ekstra koring vir haar te laat val.

Boas was ’n ‘losser’, ’n familielid met die reg om ’n familie in moeilikheid te red. Hy het met Rut getrou en ook na Naomi omgesien. Hulle het ’n seun gehad met die naam Obed, en Naomi het haar kleinseun met blydskap vasgehou.

Die storie eindig met ’n verrassing: Obed het die oupa van koning Dawid geword. Baie geslagte later is Jesus in hierdie familie gebore. God het ’n vreemdeling uit ’n vyandige land in sy familie verwelkom en haar in die storie van Jesus ingeweef. En Jesus is ons Losser, die Een wat ons red en in God se familie inbring.

verse.text: Die Here is goed vir almal; Hy is vol liefde vir alles wat Hy gemaak het.

lessons: God gee om vir mense wat eensaam, hartseer en in nood is.
God wys dikwels sy goedheid deur die goedheid van mense.
God verwelkom almal in sy familie, en Jesus is ons Losser.
questions: Wat het Rut aan Naomi belowe?
Hoe het Boas God se goedheid gewys?
Wie rondom jou is eensaam of gaan deur ’n hartseer tyd? Hoe kan jy soos Rut of Boas vir hulle wees?
af.listen: Wees stil en vra God: ‘Met wie wil U hê moet ek hierdie week gaaf wees?’ Luister. Skryf die naam neer wat in jou gedagtes opkom.
prayer: God, dankie dat U goed is en omgee vir eensame mense.
Troos asseblief…
Help my om u goedheid te wys soos Rut en Boas.

mission.text: Doen môre iets gaaf vir iemand wat hartseer of eensaam is: ’n briefie, ’n tekening, of net om by hulle te sit.

af.journal: Skryf Rut se belofte (‘Waar jy gaan, sal ek gaan…’) en skryf dan jou eie belofte aan God in jou eie woorde.

trait.en: God is kind and cares for sad and lonely people
trait.af: God is vriendelik en gee om vir hartseer en eensame mense

en.title: The Little Girl Who Helped
story: Naaman was a great army captain, strong and brave. But he had a terrible skin sickness called leprosy, and no doctor could make it better.

In Naaman’s house lived a young servant girl from Israel. She was far from home, but she still trusted God. She said to Naaman’s wife, ‘I wish my master would go to God’s prophet Elisha. He would heal him!’

So Naaman went. Elisha sent a message: ‘Go and wash in the Jordan River seven times.’ Naaman was cross. ‘That muddy river? I thought he would wave his hand and heal me!’ But his servants said, ‘Why not try?’

So Naaman dipped down once… twice… three, four, five, six… SEVEN times. When he came up, his skin was as soft and clean as a little boy’s! ‘Now I know,’ said Naaman, ‘there is no God in all the world except the God of Israel.’

verse.text: Don’t let anyone look down on you because you are young. Be an example.

lessons: God heals, and he cares about our bodies.
God can use children to tell others about him.
Doing things God’s way works best, even when it seems silly.
questions: How did the little girl help Naaman?
Who could you tell about God?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you can use me, even though I’m small.
Please help people who are sick,
like… (name someone). Amen.

mission.text: Tell a friend or family member one thing you have learned about God.

af.title: Die Dogtertjie wat Gehelp Het
story: Naäman was ’n groot leërkaptein, sterk en dapper. Maar hy het ’n verskriklike velsiekte gehad wat melaatsheid genoem word, en geen dokter kon dit gesond maak nie.

In Naäman se huis het ’n jong diensmeisie van Israel gewoon. Sy was ver van die huis af, maar sy het God steeds vertrou. Sy het vir Naäman se vrou gesê: ‘Ek wens my baas wil na God se profeet Elisa gaan. Hy sou hom gesond maak!’

Toe gaan Naäman. Elisa het ’n boodskap gestuur: ‘Gaan was jou sewe keer in die Jordaanrivier.’ Naäman was kwaad. ‘Daardie modderige rivier? Ek het gedink hy sou sy hand swaai en my gesond maak!’ Maar sy diensknegte het gesê: ‘Hoekom probeer u nie?’

Toe duik Naäman af, een keer… twee keer… drie, vier, vyf, ses… SEWE keer. Toe hy opkom, was sy vel so sag en skoon soos ’n seuntjie s’n! ‘Nou weet ek,’ sê Naäman, ‘daar is geen God in die hele wêreld behalwe die God van Israel nie.’

verse.text: Moenie dat iemand op jou neersien omdat jy jonk is nie. Wees ’n voorbeeld.

lessons: God genees, en Hy gee om vir ons liggame.
God kan kinders gebruik om ander van Hom te vertel.
Om dinge op God se manier te doen werk die beste, selfs as dit snaaks lyk.
questions: Hoe het die dogtertjie vir Naäman gehelp?
Vir wie kan jy van God vertel?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my kan gebruik, al is ek klein.
Help asseblief mense wat siek is,
soos… (noem iemand). Amen.

mission.text: Vertel môre vir ’n maatjie of familielid een ding wat jy oor God geleer het.

en.title: The Little Girl Who Helped
story: Naaman was a big, strong soldier. But he had sore, spotty skin.
A little girl in his house said, ‘God’s prophet can make you better!’
The prophet said, ‘Wash in the river seven times.’
Splash! One, two, three, four, five, six, SEVEN!
His skin was all better! God used a little girl to help.

verse.text: God can use me, even though I am little.

en.action: Pretend to wash in the river and count to seven: splash, splash, splash! Then show your clean hands.
lessons: God can use me, even though I am little.
questions: Can you count to seven with me?
prayer: Dear God,
please use me to help others. Amen.

af.title: Die Dogtertjie wat Gehelp Het
story: Naäman was ’n groot, sterk soldaat. Maar hy het seer, kolle-vel gehad.
’n Dogtertjie in sy huis het gesê: ‘God se profeet kan jou gesond maak!’
Die profeet het gesê: ‘Was jou sewe keer in die rivier.’
Plons! Een, twee, drie, vier, vyf, ses, SEWE!
Sy vel was heeltemal gesond! God het ’n dogtertjie gebruik om te help.

verse.text: God kan my gebruik, al is ek klein.

af.action: Maak of jy in die rivier was en tel tot sewe: plons, plons, plons! Wys dan jou skoon hande.
lessons: God kan my gebruik, al is ek klein.
questions: Kan jy saam met my tot sewe tel?
prayer: Liewe God,
gebruik my asseblief om ander te help. Amen.

en.title: A Small Voice, a Big Healing
story: Naaman was the commander of the army of Aram, a powerful enemy of Israel. He was a great hero, highly respected by his king. But he had leprosy, a skin disease that had no cure and would slowly get worse.

On one of their raids into Israel, the Aramean soldiers had captured a young girl, and she became a servant to Naaman’s wife. She had every reason to be bitter. She was far from her family, serving the people who had taken her. But instead she cared. She said, ‘If only my master would see the prophet who is in Samaria! He would cure him of his leprosy.’ Even far from home, she trusted God and believed He could heal.

Naaman travelled to Israel with horses, chariots and expensive gifts, and stopped at the prophet Elisha’s door. Elisha didn’t even come out. He simply sent a messenger: ‘Go, wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored.’

Naaman was furious. He had expected a grand ceremony. ‘Aren’t the rivers of Damascus better than all the waters of Israel?’ He stormed away. But his servants reasoned with him: ‘If the prophet had told you to do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, “Wash and be cleansed”!’

So Naaman humbled himself, went down to the Jordan and dipped seven times. When he came up the seventh time, his skin was restored, clean as a young boy’s. Naaman went back to Elisha and declared, ‘Now I know that there is no God in all the world except in Israel.’

God is a healer, and He still heals today. He cares about our bodies as well as our hearts. And notice how this miracle began: with the faith of a girl whose name we don’t even know. God loves to use children who trust Him.

verse.text: Don’t let anyone look down on you because you are young, but set an example for the believers.

lessons: God is a healer who cares about our bodies as well as our hearts.
God uses children who trust Him to point others to Him.
Receiving from God takes humility: doing things His way, even when it seems too simple.
questions: Why do you think the servant girl wanted to help Naaman, even though he was her captor?
Why was Naaman angry at first? What changed his mind?
Who do you know who needs healing? How could you pray for them, or tell them about God?
en.listen: Think of someone who is sick or hurting. Ask God: ‘How do you want me to pray for them?’ Listen, then pray what you sense, with faith.
prayer: God, you are the Healer.
I pray for… Please heal them and show them your love.
Use me, even though I’m young, to point others to you.

mission.text: Pray for someone who is sick tomorrow, and if you can, tell them (or send a message) that you are praying for them.

en.journal: Draw the servant girl. Next to her, write a few sentences about how you could be like her in your school or neighbourhood.

af.title: ’n Klein Stemmetjie, ’n Groot Genesing
story: Naäman was die bevelvoerder van die leër van Aram, ’n sterk vyand van Israel. Hy was ’n groot held, baie gerespekteer deur sy koning. Maar hy het melaatsheid gehad, ’n velsiekte waarvoor daar geen geneesmiddel was nie en wat stadig erger sou word.

Op een van hulle strooptogte in Israel het die Arameese soldate ’n jong meisie gevang, en sy het ’n diensmeisie vir Naäman se vrou geword. Sy het elke rede gehad om bitter te wees. Sy was ver van haar familie af en het die mense gedien wat haar gevat het. Maar sy het eerder omgegee. Sy het gesê: ‘As my baas maar net na die profeet in Samaria kon gaan! Hy sou hom van sy melaatsheid gesond maak.’ Selfs ver van die huis af het sy God vertrou en geglo Hy kan genees.

Naäman het met perde, strydwaens en duur geskenke na Israel gereis, en voor die profeet Elisa se deur stilgehou. Elisa het nie eens uitgekom nie. Hy het net ’n boodskapper gestuur: ‘Gaan was jou sewe keer in die Jordaan, dan sal jou vel gesond word.’

Naäman was woedend. Hy het ’n groot seremonie verwag. ‘Is die riviere van Damaskus nie beter as al die waters van Israel nie?’ Hy het weggestorm. Maar sy diensknegte het met hom gepraat: ‘As die profeet u gevra het om iets groots te doen, sou u dit nie gedoen het nie? Hoeveel te meer as hy net sê: “Was jou en word skoon”!’

Toe het Naäman homself verootmoedig, na die Jordaan afgegaan en homself sewe keer onder die water gedompel. Toe hy die sewende keer opkom, was sy vel gesond, so skoon soos ’n jong seun s’n. Naäman het na Elisa teruggegaan en verklaar: ‘Nou weet ek dat daar geen God in die hele wêreld is behalwe in Israel nie.’

God is ’n Geneser, en Hy genees vandag nog. Hy gee om vir ons liggame sowel as ons harte. En let op hoe hierdie wonderwerk begin het: met die geloof van ’n meisie wie se naam ons nie eens ken nie. God gebruik graag kinders wat Hom vertrou.

verse.text: Moenie dat iemand op jou neersien omdat jy jonk is nie, maar wees ’n voorbeeld vir die gelowiges.

lessons: God is ’n Geneser wat omgee vir ons liggame sowel as ons harte.
God gebruik kinders wat Hom vertrou om ander na Hom te wys.
Om van God te ontvang vra nederigheid: om dinge op sy manier te doen, selfs as dit te eenvoudig lyk.
questions: Hoekom dink jy wou die diensmeisie Naäman help, al was hy die een wat haar gevang het?
Hoekom was Naäman eers kwaad? Wat het hom van plan laat verander?
Wie ken jy wat genesing nodig het? Hoe kan jy vir hulle bid, of hulle van God vertel?
af.listen: Dink aan iemand wat siek is of seerkry. Vra God: ‘Hoe wil U hê moet ek vir hulle bid?’ Luister, en bid dan met geloof wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, U is die Geneser.
Ek bid vir… Maak hulle asseblief gesond en wys hulle u liefde.
Gebruik my, al is ek jonk, om ander na U te wys.

mission.text: Bid môre vir iemand wat siek is, en as jy kan, sê vir hulle (of stuur ’n boodskap) dat jy vir hulle bid.

af.journal: Teken die diensmeisie. Skryf langs haar ’n paar sinne oor hoe jy soos sy kan wees by jou skool of in jou buurt.

trait.en: God heals, and he uses children too
trait.af: God genees, en Hy gebruik kinders ook

en.title: The Promise of a Rescuer
story: Do you remember the promise God made in the garden, right at the start of our trail? He promised a Rescuer who would fix what sin had broken.

Many years later God gave his prophet Isaiah a message about that Rescuer. Isaiah wrote it down like clues on a treasure map: ‘A young woman will have a baby boy. He will be called Immanuel, which means God with us.’ And: ‘A child will be born to us. He will be called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.’ Another prophet, Micah, even said which little town he would be born in: Bethlehem!
God’s people waited. And waited. Hundreds of years went by. Some people forgot. But God never forgets a promise.
Can you guess who the baby would be? That’s right: Jesus! Soon our trail will lead to the most amazing birthday ever.

verse.text: A child will be born to us… He will be called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

lessons: God planned to send Jesus long before he was born.
God always keeps his promises, even when it takes a long time.
Jesus is ‘God with us’.
questions: Which of Jesus’ names do you like best?
Is it hard to wait for something? What helps?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for your promise to send Jesus.
Thank you that you never forget.
Help me wait with a happy heart. Amen.

mission.text: Learn one of Jesus’ names from Isaiah 9:6 and tell someone what it means.

af.title: Die Belofte van ’n Redder
story: Onthou jy die belofte wat God in die tuin gemaak het, heel aan die begin van ons pad? Hy het ’n Redder belowe wat sou regmaak wat sonde gebreek het.

Baie jare later het God vir sy profeet Jesaja ’n boodskap oor daardie Redder gegee. Jesaja het dit neergeskryf soos leidrade op ’n skatkaart: ‘’n Jong vrou sal ’n seuntjie kry. Hy sal Immanuel genoem word, wat beteken God met ons.’ En: ‘’n Kind is vir ons gebore. Hy sal genoem word Wonderbare Raadsman, Magtige God, Ewige Vader, Vredevors.’ ’n Ander profeet, Miga, het selfs gesê in watter klein dorpie Hy gebore sou word: Betlehem!
God se mense het gewag. En gewag. Honderde jare het verbygegaan. Party mense het vergeet. Maar God vergeet nooit ’n belofte nie.
Kan jy raai wie die baba sou wees? Reg: Jesus! Binnekort lei ons pad na die wonderlikste verjaarsdag ooit.

verse.text: ’n Kind is vir ons gebore… Hy sal genoem word Wonderbare Raadsman, Magtige God, Ewige Vader, Vredevors.

lessons: God het lank voor Jesus se geboorte beplan om Hom te stuur.
God hou altyd sy beloftes, selfs as dit lank vat.
Jesus is ‘God met ons’.
questions: Van watter een van Jesus se name hou jy die meeste?
Is dit moeilik om vir iets te wag? Wat help?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir u belofte om Jesus te stuur.
Dankie dat U nooit vergeet nie.
Help my om met ’n blye hart te wag. Amen.

mission.text: Leer een van Jesus se name uit Jesaja 9 en vertel vir iemand wat dit beteken.

en.title: God’s Big Promise
story: God told Isaiah a secret: ‘One day a special baby will be born.’
‘He will be called Wonderful… Mighty God… Prince of Peace!’
God’s people waited and waited and waited.
Do you know who that baby is? JESUS!
God always keeps His promises.

verse.text: A baby will be born to us.

en.action: Rock a pretend baby in your arms. Then whisper the secret: ‘It’s Jesus!’
lessons: God promised to send Jesus, and He did!
questions: Who is the special baby? (Jesus!)
prayer: Thank you, God,
for sending Jesus. Amen.

af.title: God se Groot Belofte
story: God het vir Jesaja ’n geheim vertel: ‘Eendag sal ’n spesiale baba gebore word.’
‘Hy sal genoem word Wonderbaar… Magtige God… Vredevors!’
God se mense het gewag en gewag en gewag.
Weet jy wie daardie baba is? JESUS!
God hou altyd sy beloftes.

verse.text: ’n Baba sal vir ons gebore word.

af.action: Wieg ’n kamma-baba in jou arms. Fluister dan die geheim: ‘Dis Jesus!’
lessons: God het belowe om Jesus te stuur, en Hy het!
questions: Wie is die spesiale baba? (Jesus!)
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U Jesus gestuur het. Amen.

en.title: Clues About a Coming King
story: Remember the promise God made in the garden, on the very day sin entered the world? He promised that one of Eve’s descendants would crush the serpent’s head. Over the next thousands of years, God kept adding clues about this coming Rescuer, like pieces of a treasure map. Many of them came through the prophet Isaiah, about 700 years before Jesus was born.

Clue one: He would be God with us. ‘The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel’, which means ‘God with us’ (Isaiah 7:14). The Rescuer would not just be a messenger from God. He would be God Himself, come close.

Clue two: He would be a King, and His names tell us what He is like. ‘For to us a child is born, to us a son is given… And He will be called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of the greatness of His government and peace there will be no end’ (Isaiah 9:6–7).
Clue three: He would come from a small town. The prophet Micah wrote that the ruler of Israel would come from Bethlehem, the little town of King David (Micah 5:2).

Clue four, the most surprising: He would suffer for us. ‘He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities… and by His wounds we are healed’ (Isaiah 53:5). The King would also be a sacrifice, taking the punishment we deserved, in our place.

God’s people waited for hundreds of years. Some gave up. But God never forgets a promise. Every one of these clues came true in one person: Jesus. Soon our trail will reach His birth. For now, remember this: God planned your rescue long before you were born, and He keeps every promise He makes.

verse.text: For to us a child is born, to us a son is given. And He will be called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

lessons: God planned to send Jesus, our Rescuer, long before He was born.
Jesus is God with us, the King whose names show what He is like.
Jesus would suffer in our place, so that we could be forgiven and healed.
questions: Which clue about Jesus surprised you most?
What does each of Jesus’ names in Isaiah 9:6 tell us about Him?
Which of those names do you need most right now? Why?
en.listen: Read Jesus’ four names slowly: Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Ask Jesus: ‘Which of these do you want to be for me this week?’ Listen.
prayer: Jesus, you are Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father and Prince of Peace.
This week I need you to be my…
Thank you that God planned my rescue long ago.

mission.text: Learn Isaiah 9:6 by heart this week, and tell someone what one of Jesus’ names means.

en.journal: Draw a treasure map with four clues (Isaiah 7:14, Isaiah 9:6, Micah 5:2, Isaiah 53:5). At the X, write JESUS.

af.title: Leidrade oor ’n Koning wat Kom
story: Onthou jy die belofte wat God in die tuin gemaak het, op die einste dag toe sonde in die wêreld gekom het? Hy het belowe dat een van Eva se nakomelinge die slang se kop sou vermorsel. Oor die volgende duisende jare het God aanhou leidrade gee oor hierdie Redder wat sou kom, soos stukke van ’n skatkaart. Baie van hulle het deur die profeet Jesaja gekom, omtrent 700 jaar voordat Jesus gebore is.

Leidraad een: Hy sou God by ons wees. ‘Die maagd sal swanger word en ’n seun in die wêreld bring, en sy sal Hom Immanuel noem’, wat beteken ‘God met ons’ (Jesaja 7:14). Die Redder sou nie net ’n boodskapper van God wees nie. Hy sou God self wees, wat naby kom.

Leidraad twee: Hy sou ’n Koning wees, en sy name sê vir ons hoe Hy is. ‘Want ’n Kind is vir ons gebore, ’n Seun is aan ons gegee… En Hy sal genoem word Wonderbare Raadsman, Magtige God, Ewige Vader, Vredevors. Sy heerskappy sal groot wees, en aan die vrede sal daar geen einde wees nie’ (Jesaja 9:5–6).
Leidraad drie: Hy sou uit ’n klein dorpie kom. Die profeet Miga het geskryf dat die heerser van Israel uit Betlehem sou kom, die klein dorpie van koning Dawid (Miga 5:1).

Leidraad vier, die verrassendste: Hy sou vir ons ly. ‘Hy is deurboor oor ons oortredinge, Hy is verbrysel oor ons sondes… en deur sy wonde is daar vir ons genesing’ (Jesaja 53:5). Die Koning sou ook ’n offer wees, wat die straf wat ons verdien het, in ons plek sou dra.

God se mense het honderde jare lank gewag. Party het moed opgegee. Maar God vergeet nooit ’n belofte nie. Elkeen van hierdie leidrade het waar geword in een persoon: Jesus. Binnekort sal ons pad by sy geboorte uitkom. Onthou intussen dit: God het jou redding beplan lank voordat jy gebore is, en Hy hou elke belofte wat Hy maak.

verse.text: Want ’n Kind is vir ons gebore, ’n Seun is aan ons gegee. En Hy sal genoem word Wonderbare Raadsman, Magtige God, Ewige Vader, Vredevors.

lessons: God het beplan om Jesus, ons Redder, te stuur lank voordat Hy gebore is.
Jesus is God by ons, die Koning wie se name wys hoe Hy is.
Jesus sou in ons plek ly, sodat ons vergewe en genees kan word.
questions: Watter leidraad oor Jesus het jou die meeste verras?
Wat sê elkeen van Jesus se name in Jesaja 9:5 vir ons oor Hom?
Watter een van daardie name het jy nou die meeste nodig? Hoekom?
af.listen: Lees Jesus se vier name stadig: Wonderbare Raadsman, Magtige God, Ewige Vader, Vredevors. Vra Jesus: ‘Watter een van hierdie wil U hierdie week vir my wees?’ Luister.
prayer: Jesus, U is Wonderbare Raadsman, Magtige God, Ewige Vader en Vredevors.
Hierdie week het ek nodig dat U my… is.
Dankie dat God my redding lank gelede beplan het.

mission.text: Leer hierdie week Jesaja 9:5 uit jou kop, en vertel vir iemand wat een van Jesus se name beteken.

af.journal: Teken ’n skatkaart met vier leidrade (Jesaja 7:14, Jesaja 9:5, Miga 5:1, Jesaja 53:5). Skryf JESUS by die X.

en.title: Campfire Night: The River of Second Chances
story: We sailed down the River of Second Chances! A fish that swallowed Jonah, a fire that couldn’t burn, a brave queen, a kind friend and a promise of a Rescuer. Let’s remember by the fire.
questions: Which treasure about God surprised you?
Why do you think God gives second chances?
prayer: Dear God,
you are merciful and kind.
You are the King, and you have a plan.
Thank you for sending a Rescuer. Amen.

mission.text: Say Lamentations 3:22–23 when you wake up tomorrow, because God’s kindness is new every morning!

en.game: River jump: lay a blanket on the floor as a river. Every time you name a treasure about God, jump across!

af.title: Kampvuuraand: Die Rivier van Tweede Kanse
story: Ons het met die Rivier van Tweede Kanse afgevaar! ’n Vis wat Jona ingesluk het, ’n vuur wat nie kon brand nie, ’n dapper koningin, ’n gawe vriendin en ’n belofte van ’n Redder. Kom ons onthou by die vuur.

Hoekom dink jy gee God tweede kanse?

U is genadig en goed.
U is die Koning, en U het ’n plan.

en.title: Campfire Night
story: Well done, little explorer! Let’s sit by the campfire and remember: God gave Jonah another chance. God was in the fire. God helped brave Esther. God is kind. God used a little girl. God promised to send Jesus!

prayer: Thank you, God,
for loving me so much. Amen.

story: Mooi so, klein ontdekker! Kom ons sit by die kampvuur en onthou: God het vir Jona nog ’n kans gegee. God was in die vuur. God het dapper Ester gehelp. God is goed. God het ’n dogtertjie gebruik. God het belowe om Jesus te stuur!

questions: Vir wie het God nog ’n kans gegee?
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U my so baie liefhet. Amen.

en.title: Campfire Night: The River of Second Chances
story: You’ve sailed the River of Second Chances! This week God rescued a runaway prophet and forgave a whole city, stood in the fire with three faithful friends, placed a brave queen ‘for such a time as this’, welcomed a lonely foreigner into His family, healed a commander through the faith of a servant girl, and promised a coming King. Through every story runs God’s mercy: He keeps reaching out to people who don’t deserve it, and He was preparing the way for Jesus.
en.game: Who said it? Your parent reads a quote from this week (‘Even if He does not…’, ‘Where you go I will go’, ‘For such a time as this’, ‘In my distress I called to the Lord’, ‘Now I know there is no God except in Israel’). You name who said it and why.
questions: Which second chance from this week means the most to you?
Which person this week was the bravest? Which was the kindest?
How did this week’s stories prepare the way for Jesus?
prayer: God, your mercy is new every morning.
Thank you for giving me second chances, like when…
Thank you that you prepared the way for Jesus.

mission.text: Learn Lamentations 3:22–23 by heart, and say it when you wake up tomorrow.

en.journal: Draw a winding river. Along it, draw six small pictures, one for each story this week. At the end of the river, draw a star, because Jesus is coming!

af.title: Kampvuuraand: Die Rivier van Tweede Kanse
story: Jy het met die Rivier van Tweede Kanse gevaar! Hierdie week het God ’n profeet wat weggehardloop het, gered en ’n hele stad vergewe, saam met drie getroue vriende in die vuur gestaan, ’n dapper koningin ‘vir ’n tyd soos hierdie’ op haar plek gesit, ’n eensame vreemdeling in sy familie verwelkom, ’n bevelvoerder genees deur die geloof van ’n diensmeisie, en ’n Koning belowe wat sou kom. Deur elke storie loop God se genade: Hy hou aan om uit te reik na mense wat dit nie verdien nie, en Hy het die pad vir Jesus voorberei.
af.game: Wie het dit gesê? Jou ouer lees ’n aanhaling van hierdie week voor (‘Selfs as Hy nie…’, ‘Waar jy gaan, sal ek gaan’, ‘Vir ’n tyd soos hierdie’, ‘In my nood het ek na die Here geroep’, ‘Nou weet ek daar is geen God behalwe in Israel nie’). Jy sê wie dit gesê het en hoekom.
questions: Watter tweede kans van hierdie week beteken die meeste vir jou?
Wie was hierdie week die dapperste? Wie was die gaafste?
Hoe het hierdie week se stories die pad vir Jesus voorberei?
prayer: God, u genade is elke oggend nuut.
Dankie dat U my tweede kanse gee, soos toe…
Dankie dat U die pad vir Jesus voorberei het.

mission.text: Leer Klaagliedere 3:22–23 uit jou kop, en sê dit môre as jy wakker word.

af.journal: Teken ’n kronkelende rivier. Teken langs dit ses klein prentjies, een vir elke storie van hierdie week. Teken ’n ster aan die einde van die rivier, want Jesus kom!

blurb.en: Jesus shows us exactly what God is like: calming storms and hugging children.
blurb.af: Jesus wys ons presies hoe God is: Hy laat storms bedaar en druk kinders styf vas.

en.text: Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father.

af.text: Wie My gesien het, het die Vader gesien.

en.title: God's Voice at the River
story: When Jesus grew up, he went to the Jordan River, where his cousin John was baptising people: dipping them under the water to show they wanted a fresh, clean start with God.

‘Baptise me too,’ said Jesus. John was surprised. ‘You should be baptising me!’ But Jesus went into the water. When he came up, something amazing happened. The sky opened, and God’s Spirit came down like a dove and landed on Jesus. Then a voice spoke from heaven: ‘This is my Son, whom I love. I am very pleased with him.’
At the river we see God in three ways all at once: the Father speaking, Jesus the Son in the water, and the Holy Spirit like a dove. One God: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
And here is the best part: when we follow Jesus, God becomes our Father too, and he loves us like that.

verse.text: See how much the Father loves us! He calls us his children.

lessons: God is one God: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
God the Father loves Jesus, and he loves you too.
Jesus came to show us what God is like.
questions: How does it feel when Mom says she is proud of you? God feels that way about his children.
What do you think the dove looked like?
prayer: Dear Father in heaven,
thank you for loving me.
Thank you for Jesus, your Son.
I want to be your child. Amen.

mission.text: Ask Mom to tell you about a baptism she remembers.

af.title: God se Stem by die Rivier
story: Toe Jesus groot was, het Hy na die Jordaanrivier gegaan, waar sy neef Johannes mense gedoop het: hulle onder die water gedompel om te wys hulle wil ’n vars, skoon begin met God maak.

‘Doop My ook,’ sê Jesus. Johannes was verbaas. ‘U moet eerder vir my doop!’ Maar Jesus het die water ingegaan. Toe Hy opkom, het iets wonderliks gebeur. Die hemel het oopgegaan, en God se Gees het soos ’n duif neergedaal en op Jesus kom sit. Toe praat ’n stem uit die hemel: ‘Dit is my Seun, vir wie Ek liefhet. Ek is baie bly oor Hom.’
By die rivier sien ons God op drie maniere gelyk: die Vader wat praat, Jesus die Seun in die water, en die Heilige Gees soos ’n duif. Een God: Vader, Seun en Heilige Gees.
En hier is die beste deel: as ons Jesus volg, word God ook ons Vader, en ons word sy kinders. Hy het ons net so lief.

verse.text: Kyk hoe lief het die Vader ons! Hy noem ons sy kinders.

lessons: God is een God: Vader, Seun en Heilige Gees.
God die Vader het Jesus lief, en Hy het jou ook lief.
Jesus het gekom om ons te wys hoe God is.
questions: Hoe voel dit as Mamma sê sy is trots op jou? God voel so oor sy kinders.
Hoe dink jy het die duif gelyk?
prayer: Liewe Vader in die hemel,
dankie dat U my liefhet.
Dankie vir Jesus, u Seun.
Ek wil u kind wees. Amen.

mission.text: Vra Mamma om jou te vertel van ’n doop wat sy onthou.

en.title: God Loves His Son
story: Jesus grew up to be a big man.
He went into the river, and John put Him under the water. Splash!
A white dove flew down from the sky. Flap, flap!
God said from heaven: ‘This is my Son. I love Him!’
God loves you too. You are His child!

verse.text: God calls us His children.

en.action: Flap your arms like a gentle dove flying down. Then give yourself a big hug: ‘God loves me!’
lessons: God is my Father, and He loves me.
questions: What colour was the dove?
prayer: Dear Father God,
thank you for loving me. Amen.

af.title: God Is Lief vir sy Seun
story: Jesus het grootgeword en ’n groot man geword.
Hy het in die rivier ingegaan, en Johannes het Hom onder die water gedoop. Plons!
’n Wit duif het uit die lug neergevlieg. Fladder, fladder!
God het uit die hemel gesê: ‘Dit is my Seun. Ek is lief vir Hom!’
God is ook lief vir jou. Jy is sy kind!

verse.text: God noem ons sy kinders.

af.action: Fladder met jou arms soos ’n sagte duif wat neervlieg. Druk jouself dan styf vas: ‘God is lief vir my!’
lessons: God is my Vader, en Hy is lief vir my.
questions: Watter kleur was die duif?
prayer: Liewe Vader God,
dankie dat U my liefhet. Amen.

en.title: This Is My Beloved Son
story: Jesus grew up in the small town of Nazareth, working as a carpenter. For about thirty years almost nobody knew who He really was. Then the time came for His public work to begin.

His cousin John was baptising people in the Jordan River. Crowds came to confess their sins and be dipped under the water as a sign that they wanted a clean, new start with God. Then Jesus came and asked John to baptise Him too.

John was shocked. ‘I need to be baptised by you, and do you come to me?’ John knew Jesus had no sin to confess. But Jesus said, ‘Let it be so now; it is proper for us to do this to fulfil all righteousness.’ Jesus was choosing to stand with sinners, the very people He had come to save.
As Jesus came up out of the water, heaven opened. The Spirit of God came down like a dove and rested on Him. And a voice from heaven said, ‘This is my Son, whom I love; with Him I am well pleased.’

Here, at the river, we see the Trinity at the same moment: the Father speaking from heaven, the Son standing in the water, and the Holy Spirit coming down like a dove. One God in three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, perfectly united in love.

Notice when the Father said He was pleased with Jesus: before Jesus had preached a sermon or performed a miracle. The Father’s love wasn’t a reward for Jesus’ work; it came first. And here is the good news: when we receive Jesus, we are born again into God’s family. The Bible says, ‘See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are!’ God speaks the same love over you.

verse.text: See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God! And that is what we are!

lessons: God is one God in three Persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
The Father loved Jesus before He did any work. His love is not a reward to be earned.
Everyone who receives Jesus becomes a child of God, loved by the Father.
questions: Why was John surprised that Jesus wanted to be baptised?
Where do you see the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit in this story?
How does it feel to know God loves you as His child, not because of what you do?
en.listen: Be still and imagine the Father speaking over you: ‘You are my child, whom I love.’ Ask Him: ‘Father, what else do you want to say to me?’ Listen and write it down.
prayer: Father, thank you that you love me as your child.
Thank you for Jesus, your beloved Son, and for your Holy Spirit.
Help me to live like your child, especially when…

mission.text: Learn 1 John 3:1 by heart. Every time you look in a mirror tomorrow, say: ‘I am a child of God.’

en.journal: Write ‘I am a child of God’ in the middle of a page. Around it, write what you think a loving Father would say to His child.

af.title: Dit Is My Geliefde Seun
story: Jesus het in die klein dorpie Nasaret grootgeword en as ’n timmerman gewerk. Omtrent dertig jaar lank het byna niemand geweet wie Hy regtig is nie. Toe het die tyd gekom vir sy openbare werk om te begin.

Sy neef Johannes het mense in die Jordaanrivier gedoop. Skares het gekom om hulle sondes te bely en onder die water gedompel te word as ’n teken dat hulle ’n skoon, nuwe begin met God wou maak. Toe kom Jesus en vra Johannes om Hom ook te doop.

Johannes was geskok. ‘Ek moet deur U gedoop word, en U kom na my toe?’ Johannes het geweet Jesus het geen sonde om te bely nie. Maar Jesus het gesê: ‘Laat dit nou so wees; dit is reg dat ons alles doen wat God wil hê.’ Jesus het gekies om saam met sondaars te staan, die einste mense wat Hy gekom het om te red.

Toe Jesus uit die water opkom, het die hemel oopgegaan. Die Gees van God het soos ’n duif neergedaal en op Hom kom rus. En ’n stem uit die hemel het gesê: ‘Dit is my Seun, vir wie Ek liefhet; in Hom het Ek ’n welbehae.’

Hier, by die rivier, sien ons die Drie-eenheid op dieselfde oomblik: die Vader wat uit die hemel praat, die Seun wat in die water staan, en die Heilige Gees wat soos ’n duif neerdaal. Een God in drie Persone, Vader, Seun en Heilige Gees, volkome een in liefde.

Let op wanneer die Vader gesê het Hy is bly oor Jesus: voordat Jesus een preek gepreek of een wonderwerk gedoen het. Die Vader se liefde was nie ’n beloning vir Jesus se werk nie; dit het eerste gekom. En hier is die goeie nuus: as ons Jesus aanneem, word ons weergebore in God se familie. Die Bybel sê: ‘Kyk hoe groot is die liefde wat die Vader aan ons gegee het, dat ons kinders van God genoem word! En dit is wat ons is!’ God spreek dieselfde liefde oor jou uit.

verse.text: Kyk hoe groot is die liefde wat die Vader aan ons gegee het, dat ons kinders van God genoem word! En dit is wat ons is!

lessons: God is een God in drie Persone: Vader, Seun en Heilige Gees.
Die Vader het Jesus liefgehad voordat Hy enige werk gedoen het. Sy liefde is nie ’n beloning wat verdien moet word nie.
Elkeen wat Jesus aanneem, word ’n kind van God, geliefd deur die Vader.
questions: Hoekom was Johannes verbaas dat Jesus gedoop wou word?
Waar sien jy die Vader, die Seun en die Heilige Gees in hierdie storie?
Hoe voel dit om te weet God het jou lief as sy kind, nie oor wat jy doen nie?
af.listen: Wees stil en stel jou voor die Vader sê oor jou: ‘Jy is my kind, vir wie Ek liefhet.’ Vra Hom: ‘Vader, wat wil U nog vir my sê?’ Luister en skryf dit neer.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U my as u kind liefhet.
Dankie vir Jesus, u geliefde Seun, en vir u Heilige Gees.
Help my om soos u kind te lewe, veral as…

mission.text: Leer 1 Johannes 3:1 uit jou kop. Sê môre elke keer as jy in ’n spieël kyk: ‘Ek is ’n kind van God.’

af.journal: Skryf ‘Ek is ’n kind van God’ in die middel van ’n bladsy. Skryf rondom dit wat jy dink ’n liefdevolle Vader vir sy kind sou sê.

trait.en: God is my loving Father
trait.af: God is my liefdevolle Vader

en.title: Come, Follow Me!
story: Peter and his brother Andrew were fishermen. One morning they were very tired and grumpy. They had fished ALL night and caught nothing. Not one tiny fish!

Jesus got into Peter’s boat and said, ‘Go out to deep water and let down your nets.’ Peter said, ‘Master, we worked all night and caught nothing… but because you say so, I will.’ Splash went the nets, and suddenly they were so full of wriggling, jumping fish that the nets began to tear! They needed another boat to help, and both boats nearly sank!

Peter fell on his knees, amazed. Jesus smiled and said, ‘Come, follow me. From now on you will fish for people!’ He meant they would help bring people to God. Peter, Andrew, James and John left their boats and followed Jesus.
Jesus is still inviting people today: ‘Come, follow me.’ And that includes you!

verse.text: ‘Come, follow me,’ Jesus said.

lessons: Jesus invites us to be his friends and followers.
Following Jesus means listening to him and doing what he says.
Jesus has a job for us: helping others know him.
questions: What does it mean to follow someone? Let’s play follow-the-leader for one minute!
What would you tell someone about Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you for inviting me to follow you.
I want to be on your team.
Show me how to follow you. Amen.

mission.text: Play follow-the-leader tomorrow and remember: Jesus leads, we follow.

af.title: Kom, Volg My!
story: Petrus en sy broer Andreas was vissermanne. Een oggend was hulle baie moeg en knorrig. Hulle het die HELE nag gevis en niks gevang nie. Nie een klein vissie nie!

Jesus het in Petrus se boot geklim en gesê: ‘Vaar na die diep water en gooi julle nette uit.’ Petrus sê: ‘Meester, ons het die hele nag gewerk en niks gevang nie… maar omdat U dit sê, sal ek.’ Plons het die nette gegaan, en skielik was hulle so vol wriemelende, springende visse dat die nette begin skeur het! Hulle het nog ’n boot nodig gehad om te help, en albei bote het amper gesink!

Petrus het verbaas op sy knieë geval. Jesus het geglimlag en gesê: ‘Kom, volg My! Van nou af sal jy mense vang!’ Hy het bedoel hulle sal help om mense na God te bring. Petrus, Andreas, Jakobus en Johannes het hulle bote gelos en Jesus gevolg.
Jesus nooi vandag nog mense: ‘Kom, volg My.’ En dit sluit jou in!

verse.text: ‘Kom, volg My,’ het Jesus gesê.

lessons: Jesus nooi ons om sy vriende en volgelinge te wees.
Om Jesus te volg beteken om na Hom te luister en te doen wat Hy sê.
Jesus het ’n werk vir ons: om ander te help om Hom te leer ken.
questions: Wat beteken dit om iemand te volg? Kom ons speel een minuut lank ‘volg die leier’!
Wat sou jy vir iemand oor Jesus vertel?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U my nooi om U te volg.
Ek wil in u span wees.
Wys my hoe om U te volg. Amen.

mission.text: Speel môre ‘volg die leier’ en onthou: Jesus lei, ons volg.

en.title: Come, Follow Me!
story: Peter was a fisherman. He fished all night, but caught no fish.
Jesus said, ‘Throw your net in the water again.’
Splash! The net was full of wiggly fish! So many!
Jesus smiled and said, ‘Come, follow me!’
Peter followed Jesus. We can follow Jesus too!

verse.text: Jesus said, ‘Come, follow me.’

en.action: Throw a pretend net into the water, then pull it in, heavy with wiggly fish! Then walk behind Mom, following her.
lessons: Jesus wants me to follow Him and be His friend.
questions: Can you wiggle like a fish?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
I want to follow you. Amen.

af.title: Kom, Volg My!
story: Petrus was ’n visserman. Hy het die hele nag gevis, maar geen vis gevang nie.
Jesus het gesê: ‘Gooi jou net weer in die water.’
Plons! Die net was vol wriemelende visse! So baie!
Jesus het geglimlag en gesê: ‘Kom, volg My!’
Petrus het Jesus gevolg. Ons kan Jesus ook volg!

verse.text: Jesus het gesê: ‘Kom, volg My.’

af.action: Gooi ’n kamma-net in die water, en trek dit dan in, swaar van wriemelende visse! Loop dan agter Mamma aan, en volg haar.
lessons: Jesus wil hê ek moet Hom volg en sy vriend wees.
questions: Kan jy wriemel soos ’n vis?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
ek wil U volg. Amen.

en.title: Leaving the Nets
story: One morning, crowds were pressing around Jesus by the Sea of Galilee to hear Him teach. Jesus saw two fishing boats at the water’s edge. The fishermen, Simon (later called Peter) and his partners, were washing their nets after a long, disappointing night. Jesus climbed into Simon’s boat and asked him to push out a little from shore, so He could teach the crowd from the water.

When He had finished speaking, Jesus said to Simon, ‘Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch.’ Simon was an expert fisherman, and this was the wrong time of day. ‘Master, we’ve worked hard all night and haven’t caught anything. But because you say so, I will let down the nets.’

‘Because you say so.’ That is faith: doing what Jesus says even when it doesn’t make sense to us. And when they let down the nets, they caught so many fish that the nets began to break! They signalled to their partners, James and John, and they filled both boats so full that they began to sink.

Simon fell at Jesus’ knees: ‘Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man!’ In that moment he realised that Jesus was far more than a teacher. He felt how unworthy he was. But Jesus didn’t go away. He said, ‘Don’t be afraid; from now on you will fish for people.’
Jesus didn’t ask Simon to clean himself up first. He invited him, just as he was, to follow. And ‘they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything and followed Him’.

Jesus still says, ‘Come, follow me.’ Following Jesus means being with Him, learning from Him, trusting what He says, and joining His mission of bringing people into God’s family. He invites you, just as you are.

verse.text: ‘Come, follow me,’ Jesus said, ‘and I will send you out to fish for people.’

lessons: Faith means doing what Jesus says, ‘because you say so’, even when it doesn’t make sense to us.
Jesus invites us to follow Him just as we are; we don’t have to be good enough first.
Following Jesus means being with Him and joining His mission to bring people to God.
questions: What did Simon say before he let down the nets? Why is that important?
Why did Simon say, ‘Go away from me, Lord’? How did Jesus answer?
What might Jesus be asking you to do ‘because He says so’?
en.listen: Be still and hear Jesus say to you: ‘Come, follow me.’ Ask Him: ‘What does following you look like for me this week?’ Listen and write down what you sense.
prayer: Jesus, I want to follow you.
Because you say so, I will…
Show me who you want me to tell about you.

mission.text: Tomorrow, do one thing Jesus says in the Bible that feels hard, simply ‘because He says so’.

en.journal: Draw a boat full of fish. On some of the fish, write names of people you would love to know Jesus. Pray for them.

af.title: Die Nette Agterlaat
story: Een oggend het skares by die See van Galilea om Jesus saamgedrom om na sy onderrig te luister. Jesus het twee vissersbote by die water se rand gesien. Die vissermanne, Simon (later Petrus genoem) en sy vennote, was besig om hulle nette te was ná ’n lang, teleurstellende nag. Jesus het in Simon se boot geklim en hom gevra om ’n entjie van die wal af weg te stoot, sodat Hy die skare van die water af kon leer.

Toe Hy klaar gepraat het, het Jesus vir Simon gesê: ‘Vaar uit na die diep water en gooi julle nette uit om vis te vang.’ Simon was ’n kenner visserman, en dit was die verkeerde tyd van die dag. ‘Meester, ons het die hele nag hard gewerk en niks gevang nie. Maar omdat U dit sê, sal ek die nette uitgooi.’

‘Omdat U dit sê.’ Dit is geloof: om te doen wat Jesus sê, selfs as dit vir ons nie sin maak nie. En toe hulle die nette uitgooi, het hulle soveel vis gevang dat die nette begin skeur het! Hulle het vir hulle vennote, Jakobus en Johannes, gewaai, en hulle het albei bote so vol gemaak dat hulle begin sink het.

Simon het by Jesus se knieë neergeval: ‘Gaan weg van my af, Here; ek is ’n sondige mens!’ Op daardie oomblik het hy besef Jesus is baie meer as ’n leermeester. Hy het gevoel hoe onwaardig hy is. Maar Jesus het nie weggegaan nie. Hy het gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie; van nou af sal jy mense vang.’
Jesus het nie vir Simon gevra om homself eers reg te kry nie. Hy het hom genooi, net soos hy was, om te volg. En ‘hulle het hulle bote op die wal getrek, alles agtergelaat en Hom gevolg’.

Jesus sê vandag nog: ‘Kom, volg My.’ Om Jesus te volg beteken om by Hom te wees, by Hom te leer, te vertrou wat Hy sê, en saam te werk aan sy opdrag om mense in God se familie in te bring. Hy nooi jou, net soos jy is.

verse.text: ‘Kom, volg My,’ het Jesus gesê, ‘en Ek sal julle stuur om mense te vang.’

lessons: Geloof beteken om te doen wat Jesus sê, ‘omdat U dit sê’, selfs as dit vir ons nie sin maak nie.
Jesus nooi ons om Hom te volg net soos ons is; ons hoef nie eers goed genoeg te wees nie.
Om Jesus te volg beteken om by Hom te wees en saam te werk aan sy opdrag om mense na God te bring.
questions: Wat het Simon gesê voordat hy die nette uitgegooi het? Hoekom is dit belangrik?
Hoekom het Simon gesê: ‘Gaan weg van my af, Here’? Hoe het Jesus geantwoord?
Wat vra Jesus jou dalk om te doen ‘omdat Hy dit sê’?
af.listen: Wees stil en hoor hoe Jesus vir jou sê: ‘Kom, volg My.’ Vra Hom: ‘Hoe lyk dit vir my om U hierdie week te volg?’ Luister en skryf neer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: Jesus, ek wil U volg.
Omdat U dit sê, sal ek…
Wys my vir wie U wil hê ek van U moet vertel.

mission.text: Doen môre een ding wat Jesus in die Bybel sê wat moeilik voel, net ‘omdat Hy dit sê’.

af.journal: Teken ’n boot vol visse. Skryf op ’n paar van die visse die name van mense wat jy graag wil hê Jesus moet ken. Bid vir hulle.

trait.en: Jesus invites me to follow him
trait.af: Jesus nooi my om Hom te volg

en.title: Quiet! Be Still!
story: One evening Jesus and his friends got into a boat to cross the lake. Jesus was so tired that he lay down at the back of the boat on a cushion and fell fast asleep.

Suddenly a huge storm came. The wind howled, WHOOO! Waves crashed over the sides, and the boat started filling with water. Even the fishermen were terrified! They woke Jesus up: ‘Teacher, don’t you care that we’re going to drown?’
Jesus stood up. He looked at the wind and the waves and said, ‘Quiet! Be still!’ And at once the wind stopped. The waves went flat. Everything was completely calm.
His friends whispered to each other, ‘Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!’ They were learning that Jesus is God. The One who made the sea is in charge of the sea.

verse.text: When I am afraid, I will trust in you.

lessons: Jesus is more powerful than any storm.
Jesus cares when we are scared.
We can call to Jesus when we are afraid, just like his friends did.
questions: What storms make you feel scared? (Thunder, the dark, bad dreams?)
What can you say to Jesus when you feel scared?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
you can calm any storm.
When I feel scared,
help me remember you are with me. Amen.

mission.text: Learn Psalm 56:3 by heart and say it if you feel scared at night.

af.title: Swyg! Bedaar!
story: Een aand het Jesus en sy vriende in ’n boot geklim om oor die meer te vaar. Jesus was so moeg dat Hy agter in die boot op ’n kussing gaan lê en vas aan die slaap geraak het.

Skielik kom daar ’n groot storm. Die wind het gehuil, WOEEE! Golwe het oor die kante gebreek, en die boot het vol water begin loop. Selfs die vissermanne was doodbang! Hulle het Jesus wakker gemaak: ‘Meester, gee U nie om dat ons gaan verdrink nie?’
Jesus het opgestaan. Hy het na die wind en die golwe gekyk en gesê: ‘Swyg! Bedaar!’ En dadelik het die wind gaan lê. Die golwe het plat geword. Alles was heeltemal stil.
Sy vriende het vir mekaar gefluister: ‘Wie is Hy? Selfs die wind en die golwe luister na Hom!’ Hulle het geleer dat Jesus God is. Die Een wat die see gemaak het, is in beheer van die see.

verse.text: Wanneer ek bang is, vertrou ek op U.

lessons: Jesus is magtiger as enige storm.
Jesus gee om as ons bang is.
Ons kan na Jesus roep as ons bang is, net soos sy vriende gedoen het.
questions: Watter storms maak jou bang? (Donderweer, die donker, nare drome?)
Wat kan jy vir Jesus sê as jy bang voel?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
U kan enige storm laat bedaar.
As ek bang voel,
help my om te onthou U is by my. Amen.

mission.text: Leer Psalm 56:4 uit jou kop en sê dit as jy snags bang voel.

en.title: Jesus Stops the Storm
story: Jesus and His friends were in a boat. Jesus fell asleep. Shh!
Then a big storm came. Whoosh went the wind! Splash went the waves!
His friends were scared. ‘Jesus, wake up! Help!’
Jesus stood up and said, ‘Quiet! Be still!’
And everything was calm. Jesus is stronger than any storm!

verse.text: When I am scared, I will trust in you.

en.action: Make storm noises and wave your arms wildly. Then put your finger on your lips and say: ‘Quiet! Be still!’ Freeze!
lessons: When I am scared, Jesus is with me.
questions: What can you say to Jesus when you feel scared?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
when I am scared, please help me. Amen.

af.title: Jesus Laat die Storm Bedaar
story: Jesus en sy vriende was in ’n boot. Jesus het aan die slaap geraak. Sjuut!
Toe kom ’n groot storm. Woesj het die wind gewaai! Plons het die golwe gegaan!
Sy vriende was bang. ‘Jesus, word wakker! Help!’
Jesus het opgestaan en gesê: ‘Swyg! Bedaar!’
En alles was stil. Jesus is sterker as enige storm!

verse.text: As ek bang is, sal ek op U vertrou.

af.action: Maak stormgeluide en swaai jou arms wild. Sit dan jou vinger op jou lippe en sê: ‘Swyg! Bedaar!’ Staan doodstil!
lessons: As ek bang is, is Jesus by my.
questions: Wat kan jy vir Jesus sê as jy bang voel?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
as ek bang is, help my asseblief. Amen.

en.title: Who Is This?
story: After a long day of teaching crowds, Jesus said to His disciples, ‘Let us go over to the other side.’ They set off across the Sea of Galilee in a fishing boat. Jesus was so tired that He fell asleep in the back of the boat with His head on a cushion.

Suddenly a furious storm blew up. The Sea of Galilee lies low between hills, and winds can rush down and whip up huge waves very quickly. Waves broke over the boat until it was nearly swamped. Several of the disciples were experienced fishermen, and even they were sure they were going to die.
They woke Jesus: ‘Teacher, don’t you care if we drown?’ Fear often makes us wonder whether God cares. But notice: Jesus was in the boat with them the whole time.

Jesus got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, ‘Quiet! Be still!’ Immediately the wind died down and it was completely calm. Not slowly calmer, like after a normal storm, but instantly still, like glass.

Then Jesus asked them, ‘Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?’ And the disciples were terrified in a new way, with a holy awe. They asked each other, ‘Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey Him!’

That is the most important question in the story. Only God commands the wind and the sea. The disciples were beginning to understand that the man sleeping in their boat was God in the flesh, the Creator of the very sea that was trying to drown them.

Storms still come: fears, hard news, worries at night. Jesus doesn’t always stop the storm straight away, but He is always in the boat with His children, and He is stronger than anything we face. We can call out to Him, and trust Him.

verse.text: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.

lessons: Jesus is God in the flesh: even the wind and the waves obey Him.
Jesus is with His children in every storm, even when He seems quiet.
When we are afraid, we can call out to Jesus and choose to trust Him.
questions: What did the disciples ask Jesus when they woke Him? Why do you think they felt that way?
Why was the question ‘Who is this?’ so important?
What ‘storms’ make you afraid? What can you do when they come?
en.listen: Bring Jesus your biggest worry. Then imagine Him standing up and saying to it, ‘Quiet! Be still!’ Be still yourself for one minute and ask: ‘Jesus, what do you want me to know about this?’
prayer: Jesus, you are stronger than any storm.
When I feel afraid of…, help me to trust you.
Thank you that you are always in the boat with me.

mission.text: Write Psalm 56:3 on a card and keep it next to your bed. Say it if you feel afraid at night.

en.journal: Draw a stormy sea on one half of a page and a calm sea on the other half. In the middle, write ‘Who is this? Jesus!’

af.title: Wie Is Hy Tog?
story: Ná ’n lang dag waarin Hy skares geleer het, het Jesus vir sy dissipels gesê: ‘Kom ons gaan oor na die ander kant.’ Hulle het in ’n vissersboot oor die See van Galilea vertrek. Jesus was so moeg dat Hy agter in die boot met sy kop op ’n kussing aan die slaap geraak het.

Skielik het ’n woeste storm opgekom. Die See van Galilea lê laag tussen heuwels, en winde kan baie vinnig afstorm en groot golwe opsweep. Golwe het oor die boot gebreek totdat dit amper vol water was. Party van die dissipels was ervare vissermanne, en selfs hulle was seker hulle gaan verdrink.
Hulle het Jesus wakker gemaak: ‘Meester, gee U nie om dat ons vergaan nie?’ Vrees laat ons dikwels wonder of God omgee. Maar let op: Jesus was die hele tyd saam met hulle in die boot.

Jesus het opgestaan, die wind bestraf en vir die golwe gesê: ‘Swyg! Bedaar!’ Dadelik het die wind gaan lê en dit was heeltemal stil. Nie stadig stiller, soos ná ’n gewone storm nie, maar onmiddellik stil, soos glas.

Toe vra Jesus vir hulle: ‘Hoekom is julle so bang? Het julle nog nie geloof nie?’ En die dissipels was op ’n nuwe manier bang, met ’n heilige ontsag. Hulle het vir mekaar gevra: ‘Wie is Hy tog? Selfs die wind en die see luister na Hom!’

Dit is die belangrikste vraag in die storie. Net God gee bevele aan die wind en die see. Die dissipels het begin verstaan dat die man wat in hulle boot geslaap het, God in die vlees is, die Skepper van die einste see wat hulle wou laat verdrink.

Storms kom steeds: vrese, slegte nuus, bekommernisse in die nag. Jesus laat nie altyd die storm dadelik ophou nie, maar Hy is altyd saam met sy kinders in die boot, en Hy is sterker as enigiets wat ons teëkom. Ons kan na Hom roep, en Hom vertrou.

verse.text: As ek bang is, vertrou ek op U.

lessons: Jesus is God in die vlees: selfs die wind en die see luister na Hom.
Jesus is by sy kinders in elke storm, selfs as Hy stil lyk.
As ons bang is, kan ons na Jesus roep en kies om Hom te vertrou.
questions: Wat het die dissipels vir Jesus gevra toe hulle Hom wakker gemaak het? Hoekom dink jy het hulle so gevoel?
Hoekom was die vraag ‘Wie is Hy tog?’ so belangrik?
Watter ‘storms’ maak jou bang? Wat kan jy doen as hulle kom?
af.listen: Bring vir Jesus jou grootste bekommernis. Stel jou dan voor hoe Hy opstaan en daarvoor sê: ‘Swyg! Bedaar!’ Wees self een minuut lank stil en vra: ‘Jesus, wat wil U hê moet ek hieroor weet?’
prayer: Jesus, U is sterker as enige storm.
As ek bang is vir…, help my om U te vertrou.
Dankie dat U altyd saam met my in die boot is.

mission.text: Skryf Psalm 56:4 op ’n kaartjie en hou dit langs jou bed. Sê dit as jy snags bang voel.

af.journal: Teken ’n stormsee op die een helfte van ’n bladsy en ’n kalm see op die ander helfte. Skryf in die middel: ‘Wie is Hy tog? Jesus!’

trait.en: Jesus is stronger than my fears
trait.af: Jesus is sterker as my vrese

en.title: One Boy's Lunch
story: A huge crowd followed Jesus up a hill to hear him teach: five thousand men, plus all the women and children! By evening everyone was very hungry. ‘Where can we buy food for all these people?’ Jesus asked his friend Philip. Philip said, ‘Even if we worked for months, we couldn’t buy enough!’
Then Andrew found a boy who had a little lunch: five small loaves of bread and two little fish. The boy gave it all to Jesus. ‘But what is that among so many?’ said Andrew.

Jesus took the bread, looked up to heaven and thanked God. Then he broke it and kept handing it out… and handing it out… and HANDING IT OUT! Everybody ate until they were full. There were even twelve baskets of leftovers!
It all started with one boy who was willing to share what he had.

verse.text: Here is a boy with five small loaves and two small fish.

lessons: Jesus cares about our everyday needs, even rumbling tummies!
Jesus can do something big with whatever we give him.
Sharing what we have makes Jesus happy.
questions: How do you think the boy felt watching his lunch feed everyone?
What could you give Jesus? (Your time, your toys, your kindness.)
prayer: Dear Jesus,
here is what I have:
my hands, my heart and my time.
Please use them for you. Amen.

mission.text: Share something of yours tomorrow, like a snack or a toy.

af.title: Een Seun se Kos
story: ’n Groot skare het Jesus teen ’n heuwel op gevolg om na sy onderrig te luister: vyfduisend mans, plus al die vroue en kinders! Teen die aand was almal baie honger. ‘Waar kan ons kos koop vir al hierdie mense?’ het Jesus sy vriend Filippus gevra. Filippus het gesê: ‘Al werk ons maande lank, sal ons nie genoeg kan koop nie!’
Toe kry Andreas ’n seun met ’n bietjie padkos: vyf klein broodjies en twee vissies. Die seun het alles vir Jesus gegee. ‘Maar wat is dit vir so baie mense?’ sê Andreas.

Jesus het die brood geneem, opgekyk na die hemel en God gedank. Toe breek Hy dit en hou aan uitdeel… en uitdeel… en UITDEEL! Almal het geëet totdat hulle versadig was. Daar was selfs twaalf mandjies oorskiet!
Dit het alles begin met een seun wat bereid was om te deel wat hy gehad het.

verse.text: Hier is ’n seun met vyf klein broodjies en twee vissies.

lessons: Jesus gee om oor ons alledaagse behoeftes, selfs grommende mae!
Jesus kan iets groots doen met wat ons ook al vir Hom gee.
Om te deel wat ons het, maak Jesus bly.
questions: Hoe dink jy het die seun gevoel toe hy sien hoe sy kos almal voed?
Wat kan jy vir Jesus gee? (Jou tyd, jou speelgoed, jou gaafheid.)
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
hier is wat ek het:
my hande, my hart en my tyd.
Gebruik dit asseblief vir U. Amen.

mission.text: Deel môre iets van jou, soos ’n peuselhappie of ’n speelding.

af.deeper: Die seun se kos het te min gelyk om saak te maak. Watter klein dingetjies kan jy vir Jesus gee?
af.journal: Teken vyf broodjies en twee vissies. Skryf op elkeen iets wat jy kan deel.

en.title: A Boy Shares His Lunch
story: Lots and lots of people came to see Jesus. They were hungry!
A little boy had five bread rolls and two fish.
He gave his lunch to Jesus.
Jesus said thank you to God, and shared it out… and out… and out!
Everybody ate until they were full. Yum! Jesus can do big things with little things.

verse.text: Here is a boy with five loaves and two fish.

en.action: Count five bread rolls on one hand and two fish on the other. Then pretend to share them with everyone in the room!
lessons: I can share with Jesus, and He does big things.
questions: What can you share with someone tomorrow?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
I want to share like the little boy. Amen.

af.title: ’n Seuntjie Deel sy Kos
story: Baie, baie mense het gekom om Jesus te sien. Hulle was honger!
’n Seuntjie het vyf broodjies en twee vissies gehad.
Hy het sy kos vir Jesus gegee.
Jesus het dankie gesê vir God, en dit uitgedeel… en uitgedeel… en uitgedeel!
Almal het geëet totdat hulle vol was. Lekker! Jesus kan groot dinge met klein dingetjies doen.

verse.text: Hier is ’n seuntjie met vyf broodjies en twee vissies.

af.action: Tel vyf broodjies op een hand en twee vissies op die ander hand. Maak dan of jy dit met almal in die kamer deel!
lessons: Ek kan met Jesus deel, en Hy doen groot dinge.
questions: Wat kan jy môre met iemand deel?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
ek wil deel soos die seuntjie. Amen.

en.title: Little Is Much in Jesus’ Hands
story: A huge crowd followed Jesus to a hillside near the Sea of Galilee, because they had seen Him heal the sick. The Bible says there were about five thousand men, plus women and children, so maybe more than ten thousand people.

Jesus looked at the crowd and asked Philip, ‘Where shall we buy bread for these people to eat?’ John tells us Jesus asked this ‘only to test him, for He already had in mind what He was going to do’. Philip did the maths: ‘It would take more than half a year’s wages to buy enough bread for each one to have a bite!’

Andrew had found something, though it hardly seemed worth mentioning: ‘Here is a boy with five small barley loaves and two small fish, but how far will they go among so many?’ Barley loaves were the cheap bread of poor families. It was a child’s lunch.

Jesus told everyone to sit down on the grass. He took the loaves, gave thanks to His Father, and handed them out, and the same with the fish, ‘as much as they wanted’. Everyone ate until they were full. Then Jesus said, ‘Gather the pieces that are left over. Let nothing be wasted.’ They filled twelve baskets with leftovers!
Think about the boy. He could have kept his lunch. It was all he had, and it looked far too small to matter. But he gave it to Jesus, and Jesus multiplied it to feed thousands.

The next day Jesus explained what the miracle meant: ‘I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry.’ Jesus doesn’t just provide food; He is what our hearts are hungry for. And whatever small things we give Him, our time, our talents, our kindness, He can multiply in ways we would never imagine.

verse.text: Here is a boy with five small barley loaves and two small fish, but how far will they go among so many?

lessons: Jesus cares about people’s everyday needs, even hungry tummies.
Whatever we give to Jesus, however small, He can multiply.
Jesus is the bread of life: He satisfies the deepest hunger of our hearts.
questions: What did Philip and Andrew think about the problem? How was Jesus thinking differently?
Why do you think the boy gave his lunch away?
What is something small you could give to Jesus this week?
en.listen: Hold out your hands as if you are holding a little lunch. Ask Jesus: ‘What do I have that I can give to you?’ Listen. Maybe He will remind you of a talent, some time, or something you own.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you are the bread of life.
Here is what I have: … Please use it.
Help me to share generously, like the boy did.

mission.text: Share something tomorrow: a snack, a toy, your time, or a kind word. Give it as if you were giving it to Jesus.

en.journal: Draw five loaves and two fish. On each one, write something small you can give to Jesus (for example ‘my singing’ or ‘helping at home’).

af.title: Min Is Baie in Jesus se Hande
story: ’n Groot skare het Jesus na ’n heuwel naby die See van Galilea gevolg, omdat hulle gesien het hoe Hy siekes gesond maak. Die Bybel sê daar was omtrent vyfduisend mans, plus vroue en kinders, so dalk meer as tienduisend mense.

Jesus het na die skare gekyk en vir Filippus gevra: ‘Waar sal ons brood koop dat hierdie mense kan eet?’ Johannes vertel ons Jesus het dit gevra ‘net om hom te toets, want Hy het reeds geweet wat Hy gaan doen’. Filippus het gesomme gemaak: ‘Meer as ’n half jaar se loon sal nie genoeg brood koop dat elkeen ’n happie kry nie!’

Andreas het iets gekry, al het dit skaars die moeite werd gelyk om te noem: ‘Hier is ’n seuntjie met vyf klein garsbrode en twee vissies, maar wat is dit vir so baie mense?’ Garsbrode was die goedkoop brood van arm families. Dit was ’n kind se kos.

Jesus het vir almal gesê om op die gras te gaan sit. Hy het die brode geneem, sy Vader gedank, en dit uitgedeel, en net so met die visse, ‘soveel as wat hulle wou hê’. Almal het geëet totdat hulle versadig was. Toe sê Jesus: ‘Maak die stukke bymekaar wat oorbly. Laat niks verlore gaan nie.’ Hulle het twaalf mandjies met oorskiet volgemaak!

Dink aan die seuntjie. Hy kon sy kos gehou het. Dit was al wat hy gehad het, en dit het heeltemal te klein gelyk om saak te maak. Maar hy het dit vir Jesus gegee, en Jesus het dit vermeerder om duisende te voed.

Die volgende dag het Jesus verduidelik wat die wonderwerk beteken: ‘Ek is die brood van die lewe. Wie na My toe kom, sal nooit honger kry nie.’ Jesus gee nie net kos nie; Hy is waarna ons harte honger is. En watter klein dingetjies ons ook al vir Hom gee, ons tyd, ons talente, ons goedheid, kan Hy vermeerder op maniere wat ons ons nooit sou kon indink nie.

verse.text: Hier is ’n seuntjie met vyf klein garsbrode en twee vissies, maar wat is dit vir so baie mense?

lessons: Jesus gee om oor mense se alledaagse behoeftes, selfs honger magies.
Wat ons ook al vir Jesus gee, hoe klein ook al, kan Hy vermeerder.
Jesus is die brood van die lewe: Hy stil die diepste honger van ons harte.
questions: Wat het Filippus en Andreas oor die probleem gedink? Hoe het Jesus anders gedink?
Hoekom dink jy het die seuntjie sy kos weggegee?
Wat is iets kleins wat jy hierdie week vir Jesus kan gee?
af.listen: Hou jou hande uit asof jy ’n klein kossakkie vashou. Vra Jesus: ‘Wat het ek wat ek vir U kan gee?’ Luister. Dalk herinner Hy jou aan ’n talent, ’n bietjie tyd, of iets wat jy besit.
prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U die brood van die lewe is.
Hier is wat ek het: … Gebruik dit asseblief.
Help my om vrygewig te deel, soos die seuntjie.

mission.text: Deel môre iets: ’n peuselhappie, ’n speelding, jou tyd, of ’n gawe woord. Gee dit asof jy dit vir Jesus gee.

af.journal: Teken vyf brode en twee vissies. Skryf op elkeen iets kleins wat jy vir Jesus kan gee (byvoorbeeld ‘my sing’ of ‘help by die huis’).

trait.en: Jesus does big things with small gifts
trait.af: Jesus doen groot dinge met klein gawes

en.title: Let the Children Come
story: Parents loved Jesus, so they brought their children to him so he could bless them. But Jesus’ disciples said, ‘Shoo! Go away! Jesus is far too busy and important for kids!’
When Jesus saw this, he wasn’t happy with his disciples at all. ‘Let the little children come to me!’ he said. ‘Don’t stop them! God’s kingdom belongs to people like these.’
Then Jesus took the children in his arms. He put his hands on their heads and blessed them. Maybe he laughed with them, listened to their stories and gave them big hugs.
Jesus is never too busy for you. You don’t have to be grown-up, clever or good enough first. You can come to him anytime, just as you are.

verse.text: Let the little children come to me.

lessons: Jesus loves children and is never too busy for them.
You can talk to Jesus anytime, anywhere.
Grown-ups can learn from the way children trust Jesus.
questions: If you could sit on Jesus’ lap, what would you tell him?
Let’s tell him that right now!
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you that you are never too busy for me.
I’m coming to you just as I am.
I love you. Amen.

mission.text: Tell Jesus about your day tomorrow, like you would tell a friend.

af.title: Laat die Kinders Kom
story: Ouers was lief vir Jesus, en hulle het hulle kinders na Hom gebring sodat Hy hulle kon seën. Maar Jesus se dissipels het gesê: ‘Sjuut! Gaan weg! Jesus is te besig en te belangrik vir kinders!’
Toe Jesus dit sien, was Hy glad nie bly met sy dissipels nie. ‘Laat die kindertjies na My toe kom!’ het Hy gesê. ‘Moenie hulle keer nie! God se koninkryk behoort aan mense soos hulle.’
Toe het Jesus die kinders in sy arms geneem. Hy het sy hande op hulle koppe gesit en hulle geseën. Dalk het Hy saam met hulle gelag, na hulle stories geluister en hulle styf vasgedruk.
Jesus is nooit te besig vir jou nie. Jy hoef nie eers groot, slim of goed genoeg te wees nie. Jy kan enige tyd na Hom toe kom, net soos jy is.

verse.text: Laat die kindertjies na My toe kom.

lessons: Jesus het kinders lief en is nooit te besig vir hulle nie.
Jy kan enige tyd en enige plek met Jesus praat.
Grootmense kan leer uit hoe kinders Jesus vertrou.
questions: As jy op Jesus se skoot kon sit, wat sou jy vir Hom vertel?
Kom ons vertel Hom dit nou!
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U nooit te besig is vir my nie.
Ek kom na U toe net soos ek is.
Ek is lief vir U. Amen.

mission.text: Vertel môre vir Jesus van jou dag, soos jy vir ’n vriend sou vertel.

af.fact: In Jesus se tyd is kinders nie as baie belangrik gesien nie. Jesus het almal verras deur hulle te verwelkom.
af.deeper: Jesus het gesê ons moet God se koninkryk aanneem soos ’n kind. Wat dink jy het Hy bedoel?
af.journal: Skryf ’n brief aan Jesus, asof jy reg langs Hom sit.

en.title: Jesus Loves Children
story: Mommies and daddies brought their children to see Jesus.
Jesus’ friends said, ‘Go away! Jesus is too busy!’
But Jesus said, ‘No! Let the children come to me!’
Jesus picked them up and gave them big hugs.
Jesus loves children. Jesus loves YOU!

verse.text: Let the little children come to me.

en.action: Run to Mom with your arms open wide, and give her the biggest hug, like Jesus hugged the children.
lessons: Jesus loves me and always has time for me.
questions: What would you like to tell Jesus?
prayer: Dear Jesus,
thank you for loving me. Amen.

af.title: Jesus Is Lief vir Kinders
story: Mammas en pappas het hulle kinders na Jesus gebring.
Jesus se vriende het gesê: ‘Gaan weg! Jesus is te besig!’
Maar Jesus het gesê: ‘Nee! Laat die kinders na My toe kom!’
Jesus het hulle opgetel en styf vasgedruk.
Jesus is lief vir kinders. Jesus is lief vir JOU!

verse.text: Laat die kindertjies na My toe kom.

af.action: Hardloop na Mamma met jou arms wyd oop, en gee haar die grootste drukkie, soos Jesus die kinders vasgedruk het.
lessons: Jesus is lief vir my en het altyd tyd vir my.
questions: Wat sou jy graag vir Jesus wou vertel?
prayer: Liewe Jesus,
dankie dat U my liefhet. Amen.

en.title: Never Too Busy for You
story: Jesus was surrounded by important people and serious questions. Religious teachers came to test Him with difficult debates. Crowds followed Him everywhere, wanting healing. His schedule was full.

Then some parents started bringing their little children to Jesus, hoping He would place His hands on them and bless them. The disciples were annoyed. In their culture, children weren’t thought of as very important. They probably thought, ‘Jesus has far more important work to do!’ So they rebuked the parents and sent them away.

When Jesus saw this, Mark says, ‘He was indignant.’ That means He was properly upset. It is one of the very few times the Bible tells us Jesus was angry, and it was because someone was keeping children away from Him!

‘Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them,’ He said, ‘for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these. Truly I tell you, anyone who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.’
Then Jesus did something beautiful. ‘He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them and blessed them.’ He didn’t just pat them on the head and move on. He held them close.

What does it mean to receive God’s kingdom ‘like a child’? Children don’t earn a place in their family; they simply receive it. They trust, they ask, and they come close without worrying whether they are good enough. That is exactly how Jesus wants all of us to come to Him: not with a list of achievements, but with open, trusting hearts.
Jesus has never been too busy for children, and He isn’t too busy for you tonight.

verse.text: Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

lessons: Jesus loves children and is never too busy for them.
We receive God’s kingdom like children: by trusting, not by earning.
Jesus wants to bless you and hold you close.
questions: Why do you think the disciples sent the children away?
Why did this make Jesus so upset?
What does it mean to come to Jesus ‘like a child’?
en.listen: Imagine yourself as one of the children Jesus is holding. Be still. Ask Jesus: ‘What blessing do you want to speak over me?’ Listen and write it down.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you are never too busy for me.
I come to you just as I am, and I want to tell you about…
Thank you for blessing me.

mission.text: Find five minutes alone with Jesus tomorrow, just to talk to Him like a friend about your day.

en.journal: Write a letter to Jesus as if you were sitting on His lap. Tell Him what is on your heart.

af.title: Nooit Te Besig vir Jou Nie
story: Jesus was omring deur belangrike mense en ernstige vrae. Godsdienstige leermeesters het gekom om Hom met moeilike argumente te toets. Skares het Hom oral gevolg, op soek na genesing. Sy dag was vol.

Toe begin party ouers hulle klein kindertjies na Jesus bring, in die hoop dat Hy sy hande op hulle sou lê en hulle seën. Die dissipels was geïrriteerd. In hulle kultuur is kinders nie as baie belangrik gesien nie. Hulle het seker gedink: ‘Jesus het baie belangriker werk om te doen!’ Toe raas hulle met die ouers en stuur hulle weg.

Toe Jesus dit sien, sê Markus, ‘was Hy verontwaardig’. Dit beteken Hy was regtig ontsteld. Dit is een van die baie min kere wat die Bybel vertel dat Jesus kwaad was, en dit was omdat iemand kinders van Hom af weggehou het!

‘Laat die kindertjies na My toe kom, en moet hulle nie keer nie,’ het Hy gesê, ‘want die koninkryk van God behoort aan mense soos hulle. Dit verseker Ek julle: Wie die koninkryk van God nie soos ’n kindjie ontvang nie, sal nooit daar ingaan nie.’
Toe het Jesus iets pragtigs gedoen. ‘Hy het die kinders in sy arms geneem, sy hande op hulle gelê en hulle geseën.’ Hy het hulle nie net op die kop geklop en aanbeweeg nie. Hy het hulle naby gehou.

Wat beteken dit om God se koninkryk ‘soos ’n kind’ te ontvang? Kinders verdien nie hulle plek in hulle familie nie; hulle ontvang dit net. Hulle vertrou, hulle vra, en hulle kom naby sonder om bekommerd te wees of hulle goed genoeg is. Dit is presies hoe Jesus wil hê ons almal na Hom toe moet kom: nie met ’n lys van prestasies nie, maar met oop, vertrouende harte.
Jesus was nog nooit te besig vir kinders nie, en Hy is vanaand nie te besig vir jou nie.

verse.text: Laat die kindertjies na My toe kom, en moet hulle nie keer nie, want die koninkryk van God behoort aan mense soos hulle.

lessons: Jesus is lief vir kinders en is nooit te besig vir hulle nie.
Ons ontvang God se koninkryk soos kinders: deur te vertrou, nie deur te verdien nie.
Jesus wil jou seën en naby hou.

Hoekom het dit Jesus so ontstel?
Wat beteken dit om ‘soos ’n kind’ na Jesus toe te kom?

prayer: Jesus, dankie dat U nooit te besig vir my is nie.
Ek kom na U toe net soos ek is, en ek wil U vertel van…
